## Product Memory

Product documentation for **Agentic CRR** — the **Regulatory Filing Operator**, a governed, conversational, action-capable surface that carries the regulatory filing lifecycle so people can govern it rather than execute every step. This set mirrors the structure of the base [CRR Product Memory](../CRR%20Product%20Memory/INDEX.md) and is optimized for AI agents (YAML frontmatter, consistent headings, cross-links) and product managers (plain-language prose with model/governance detail confined to dedicated sections).

> **Status note.** Agentic CRR is a **proposed north-star**, not shipped behavior. This memory is synthesized from the *Agentic CRR Product Brief (v3, In Review)* and the *Agentic CRR JTBD Map*. Where the base product exists in code, that behavior lives in the base [CRR Product Memory](../CRR%20Product%20Memory/INDEX.md); Agentic CRR can only automate what Base CRR can represent.

## What it is

Agentic CRR is the **Regulatory Filing Operator** — a single conversational, action-capable surface that coordinates the regulatory filing lifecycle through governed rules, deterministic evaluators, evidence, permissions, and human approval gates. It sits on top of Base CRR and turns regulatory filing from a manual coordination process into a **governed operating system for filing readiness**.

The shift for the customer is **from doing the work to governing it**. Today a person runs a filing by hand — pulling figures, mapping accounts, applying ownership math and exemption thresholds, reconciling line items, chasing owners, and assembling a package — and a controller signs on faith. With the Operator, one action-capable surface carries that work and surfaces only the exceptions that need judgment.

## Value proposition

What the customer buys:

- **Fewer manual coordination cycles** and faster filing readiness
- **Fewer missed inputs**, with chasing handled for them
- **A clearer audit trail** and more confident sign-off
- **An easier path to expand** into new filings

## The three-layer model

Three distinct layers, each with a non-overlapping role:

| Layer | Verb | What it does |
|-------|------|--------------|
| **Base CRR** | Governs | System of record: reports/workspaces, form classes, entities & ownership, source data & mappings, data collection, tasks, evidence, validation, review, package readiness, audit trail. Must keep getting more deterministic and workflow-complete. |
| **Ask AI** | Explains | Read-only intelligence in its own right. Explains fields, forms, entities, periods, and blockers; shows where values came from. **Never** creates, changes, approves, submits, or publishes. Shares the same governed context the Operator's *Read* level uses. |
| **Agentic CRR** | Acts | Moves customers from *"What do we need to file?"* to *"What's ready, what's missing, who needs to act, and can we trust the output?"* Acts through the Operator under a bounded, four-level action model. |

Ask AI is **not** a bridge to Agentic CRR — it is a valuable read-only step in its own right, and the near-term deliverable in Base CRR.

## The core guardrail

> Agentic CRR can only automate what Base CRR can represent.

The Operator is not magic on top of an incomplete system. It depends on continued investment in the Base CRR data model, workflow state, tasking, evidence, permissions, and package readiness. See [governed-substrate.md](../06-features/governed-substrate.md).

## Primary user types (seats)

Two seats **govern** the filing; two more **supply** what it runs on. See [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md).

- [Preparer](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer) — directs the Operator and resolves exceptions
- [Reviewer-approver (Controller / Responsible Officer)](../03-personas/personas.md#reviewer-approver-controller--responsible-officer) — confirms scope and gives final approval
- [SDC / SME](../03-personas/personas.md#sdc--sme) — authors and publishes the governed substrate
- [Data / Source Owner (Contributor)](../03-personas/personas.md#data--source-owner-contributor) — supplies the source truth behind figures

## Capability map

The lifecycle decomposes into capabilities the customer experiences as one coordinated workflow. See [06 — Capabilities & Governance](../06-features/README.md).

- [Obligation Scout](../06-features/obligation-scout.md) — surfaces what's required, including *not-yet-decidable* *(wedge 1)*
- [Scope & Entity](../06-features/scope-and-entity.md) — reasons over ownership & thresholds to decide who files what
- [Source Discovery & Ingestion](../06-features/source-discovery-and-ingestion.md) — finds sources, schemas, periods; pulls in-scope figures
- [Mapping & Resolve](../06-features/mapping-and-resolve.md) — maps data to requirements; flags low-confidence mappings
- [Data Collection & Chase](../06-features/data-collection-and-chase.md) — creates, routes, chases, escalates & tracks every gap *(wedge 2)*
- [Filing Preparation](../06-features/filing-preparation.md) — populates values from accepted facts
- [Validation & Readiness](../06-features/validation-and-readiness.md) — runs checks, interprets results, judges readiness
- [Review & Approval](../06-features/review-and-approval.md) — routes reviews, builds the judgment ledger, manages gates
- [Package & Filing](../06-features/package-and-filing.md) — composes the package & evidence bundle, orchestrates the run

Foundational:

- [Governed substrate](../06-features/governed-substrate.md) — the six governed elements authored by SDCs/SMEs
- [Governance & action model](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md) — the four action levels, signature commits, and the contract

## Two wedges, two entry points

- **Obligation Scout** — the *on-ramp into CRR*. Reads signals Workiva already holds (e.g. a 10-K's subsidiary disclosures) and nudges toward a likely obligation. Recommends, never asserts. See [obligation-scout.md](../06-features/obligation-scout.md).
- **Data Collection & Chase** — the *wedge into the full Operator*. The most visible pain in any filing, and where "agentic" gets concrete. A customer can adopt it alone and grow into the full Operator. See [data-collection-and-chase.md](../06-features/data-collection-and-chase.md).

**Commercial path:** Base CRR → Ask AI → high-value agent → full Operator.

## Tech surface (brief)

Hosted on Workiva's **Agent Factory** — capabilities and human-confirmed actions are configured and versioned. Governed autonomy is enforced *below the UI*: every load-bearing figure comes from a **deterministic tool**, and scope and final approval are backed by an **independent verification** the Operator cannot bypass. **Evaluation is a product capability** — a permanent harness and shadow mode gate anything before it becomes customer-facing. Filing data is confidential and the UI must respect that. See [operator-surface-and-navigation.md](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md).

## Out of scope

This product memory does **not** cover:

- Base CRR shipped behavior — see the base [CRR Product Memory](../../CRR%20Product%20Memory/INDEX.md)
- Agency portal upload / e-file — the Operator *stages* the package for the customer's approved submission process; submission happens outside CRR
- Detailed Agent Factory platform internals
- Commercial pricing detail beyond the Pack model ([report-patterns/](../05-operator-flows/report-patterns/README.md))

## How to read this

Each gap: **what's missing**, **why it matters**, **evidence** (what the brief does/doesn't say), and a **proposed solution**. Severity is a judgment. Gaps are grouped loosely by theme but numbered by priority.

---

## G1 · No correction, amendment, or restatement lifecycle

**Severity: Critical · Theme: Trust & correctness**

**What's missing.** The entire model is designed forward (obligation → close). There is no story for what happens *after* a wrong value, mapping, or scope decision is discovered — mid-filing, post-approval, or post-submission. Restatements and amendments are a fact of regulatory life.

**Why it matters.** The brief's core promise is a *penalty-bearing* filing carried under a "never-invent, fully-audited contract." A filing product that can't cleanly correct itself is not trustworthy for exactly the high-stakes cases it targets. An accepted email response *will* sometimes be wrong; a controller *will* sometimes approve and then need to reopen.

**Evidence.** The lifecycle ([lifecycle-and-action-model.md](../04-information-architecture/lifecycle-and-action-model.md)) has reopen paths *within* a cycle (E→B, G→F) but nothing after H·Close. The contract says "no silent state changes" but doesn't define the *corrective* change. The North Star ends at "package complete."

**Proposed solution.**
- Add a **post-close amendment lifecycle**: a locked package can be *reopened as an amendment* (new version), carrying forward the prior package as the baseline and producing a **change delta** for re-approval — the same signature-commit machinery, applied to corrections.
- Treat every governed fact as **revisable with lineage**: superseding a fact records the old value, new value, reason, and re-propagates to any dependent calculation (with a recompute + re-validation pass).
- Define a **"trust event"**: when an accepted fact is later contradicted (e.g. a corrected source), the Operator flags every filing that consumed it (ties to [I1](./product-improvements.md#i1--compounding-facts-across-the-portfolio)).
- Add an amendment state to the object model ([object-model.md](../04-information-architecture/object-model.md)): `filing run → amendment run`.

---

## G2 · Confidentiality & LLM data-handling under-specified

**Severity: Critical · Theme: Foundation & security**

**What's missing.** The appendix says "filing data is confidential and the UI must respect that" — one sentence. There is no treatment of: what confidential data (financials, PII, ownership structures) is exposed to the LLM vs kept in deterministic tools; data residency; per-seat visibility; redaction; retention; or how email/Teams ingestion (which crosses trust boundaries) is secured.

**Why it matters.** The target buyers are controllers and responsible officers filing penalty-bearing regulatory returns. Security review will gate every deal. "Confidential" is not a design principle until it's an architecture. This is also the most likely reason a security-conscious enterprise says no.

**Evidence.** Appendix, "Platform constraints." No security/privacy section anywhere in the brief; the memory inherits the same one-line treatment ([operator-surface-and-navigation.md](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#access-permissions--confidentiality)).

**Proposed solution.**
- Define a **data-exposure boundary**: which classes of data may enter a model prompt vs must stay inside deterministic evaluators. Default load-bearing figures to deterministic tools (already implied by "no invented figures") and keep raw confidential values out of free-form generation where possible.
- Specify **per-seat, per-entity visibility** enforced below the UI (the base `authorizationService` is a stub today — see [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md) gaps).
- Add a **confidentiality classification** to blueprint fields and treat PII/MNPI explicitly (redaction in prompts, restricted display, retention rules).
- Harden **inbound channel ingestion** (email/Teams): sender verification, tenancy binding, and a quarantine step before a reply becomes a governed fact (ties to [G8](#g8--chase-ingestion-trust--security)).
- Produce a **data-flow + trust-boundary diagram** as a first-class artifact for the security narrative.

---

## G3 · SDC/SME authoring throughput is the real scaling constraint

**Severity: Critical · Theme: Foundation & scale**

**What's missing.** "One pattern, many reports" is the commercial thesis, but every net-new filing requires SDCs/SMEs to author a blueprint + rule set + knowledge base + skills + test cases, then shepherd it through shadow mode. The brief asserts the supply model ("agents draft, SDC/SME review and publish") but never quantifies or de-risks **throughput and cost per filing** — which is the actual bottleneck on "many reports."

**Why it matters.** The portfolio promise (Packs spanning many forms) and the Obligation Scout on-ramp both assume a deep, growing catalog of governed bundles. If each bundle takes a scarce SME weeks, the catalog grows slowly and the TAM story stalls. This is the silent constraint behind everything else.

**Evidence.** §6–7 describe the substrate and the governed bundle but give no authoring effort, cadence, or scaling model. §8 asks leadership to "stand up the governed substrate and the supply + evaluation model" — i.e. it's explicitly unresolved.

**Proposed solution.**
- Treat **authoring velocity as a headline product metric** (bundles/quarter, SME-hours/bundle) and design toward it.
- Invest early in **assisted authoring** (agent-drafted blueprints/rules/test-cases from the knowledge base, SME reviews) — see [I8](./product-improvements.md#i8--assisted-self-service-substrate-authoring).
- Build a **bundle template & inheritance system**: report categories ([report-patterns/](../05-operator-flows/report-patterns/README.md)) share scaffolding so a new BEA survey inherits from the statistical/corporate template.
- Auto-generate **test cases** from the rule set and from prior filings to make shadow-mode gating cheaper.
- Sequence the catalog by **signal density** (which filings the Obligation Scout can detect for the most customers — ties to the §8 sizing question).

---

## G4 · No defined confidence model

**Severity: High · Theme: Trust & correctness**

**What's missing.** "Confidence: high" and "low-confidence mappings" appear throughout, but there is no definition of *what confidence means*, how it's computed, what thresholds route an item to human review vs auto-accept, or how it's calibrated.

**Why it matters.** Confidence is the dial that governs [P7 surface-ambiguity](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine) and the whole "hide routine, surface exceptions" promise. If it's vibes, the Operator either over-surfaces (no time saved) or under-surfaces (unsafe). It's also the input to [earned autonomy](./product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy).

**Evidence.** North Star §4–5; [mapping-and-resolve.md](../06-features/mapping-and-resolve.md) references confidence without a model.

**Proposed solution.**
- Define confidence as a **typed, per-decision score** with named sources (source-match strength, rule determinism, historical accuracy for this field/customer).
- Set **explicit, per-report routing thresholds** (auto-accept / needs-review / must-collect), authored in the rule set so they're governed and versioned.
- Separate **deterministic certainty** (a value from a deterministic evaluator = certain) from **inferential confidence** (a mapping guess) — never blend them into one number.
- Make confidence **calibrated and auditable** (track predicted vs actual over time; expose in the [trust dashboard](./product-improvements.md#i9--operator-trust-dashboard)).

---

## G5 · Evaluation / shadow mode asserted, not designed

**Severity: High · Theme: Trust & correctness**

**What's missing.** "Evaluation is a product capability" with "a permanent harness and shadow mode" is stated as a pillar, but there's no design for it: what "correct" means for a filing, what ground truth is measured against, who adjudicates shadow results, and the pass/fail bar for going customer-facing.

**Why it matters.** Shadow mode is the safety gate the whole risk posture leans on ("prove BE-11 end-to-end in shadow before anything is customer-facing"). An undefined gate is not a gate.

**Evidence.** §3 appendix + §8 ("stand up … the evaluation model … shadow-mode gating"). Named as a to-do, not designed.

**Proposed solution.**
- Define **ground truth**: real prior filings (recompute and compare), SME-adjudicated golden sets, and deterministic-evaluator agreement as the reference.
- Define **eval dimensions**: scope correctness, mapping accuracy, no-invented-figures compliance, chase closure, readiness accuracy, and reviewer-acceptance rate.
- Set a **release bar per report type** (e.g. N shadow filings at ≥X accuracy, zero invented-figure violations) authored alongside the bundle.
- Make eval **continuous, not one-time**: every live filing is a shadow comparison against deterministic checks; regressions re-gate. Ties to [I2](./product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy) and [I9](./product-improvements.md#i9--operator-trust-dashboard).

---

## G6 · The "not-yet-decidable" loop has no trigger

**Severity: High · Theme: Continuity**

**What's missing.** The front door honestly surfaces "not decidable yet — until current-year financials are available," which is excellent. But nothing defines *how the deferred decision gets picked back up* when the dependency arrives. The Operator identifies the blocker but doesn't own resolving it.

**Why it matters.** An honest "not yet" that no one watches becomes a silent miss — the exact failure the product is meant to prevent. The elegance of the front door is undercut without a resolution mechanism.

**Evidence.** North Star §1 (5 affiliates not-yet-decidable); §3 (2 require current-year financials). No follow-up trigger anywhere; the base JTBD map had an "always-on Lifecycle Agent" for this that the brief dropped (see [G7](#g7--loss-of-the-always-on-monitoring-dimension)).

**Proposed solution.**
- Make each *not-yet-decidable* item a **watched dependency** with a condition (e.g. "FY25 financials loaded for entity X") and an owner.
- When the condition is met (source freshness, a collected fact, a date), the Operator **re-evaluates and re-surfaces** the item as a next-best-step ("Brazil's FY25 financials arrived — ready to decide scope for this affiliate").
- Show a persistent **"deferred decisions" tray** in the portfolio workspace so nothing sits invisibly.

---

## G7 · Loss of the always-on monitoring dimension

**Severity: High · Theme: Continuity**

**What's missing.** The JTBD map had a **Lifecycle Agent** — always-on, spanning all stages, monitoring status, deadlines, source freshness, and regulatory changes. The brief consolidated everything into "one Operator" but in doing so narrowed the *continuous, between-cycles* dimension down to Obligation Scout (front door) + the next-year monitoring plan (close). The steady-state "watch everything for me" capability is thin.

**Why it matters.** Much of a compliance team's real anxiety is *between* filings: is a deadline creeping up, did source data change, did a rule change, is a filing slipping. A product that's only "on" during an active filing run misses the always-on value that Obligation Scout hints at but doesn't deliver alone.

**Evidence.** The base JTBD map's "Lifecycle Agent — always on" (source synthesis doc, external to this repo); the brief has no standing monitor between front door and close.

**Proposed solution.**
- Define a **standing monitoring layer** in the portfolio workspace: deadlines, source freshness, deferred decisions ([G6](#g6--the-not-yet-decidable-loop-has-no-trigger)), regulatory changes ([G11](#g11--regulatory-change-management-mid-cycle)), and in-flight filing health — surfaced as proactive next-best-steps.
- Position it as the **portfolio front door's steady state**, not a separate agent, preserving the "one Operator" framing.
- This is the natural home for [I6 regulatory-change radar](./product-improvements.md#i6--regulatory-change-radar) and [I10 benchmarking](./product-improvements.md#i10--anonymized-peer-benchmarking).

---

## G8 · Chase ingestion trust & security

**Severity: High · Theme: Trust & correctness**

**What's missing.** The chase captures replies "by email" and maps them to fields as governed facts. But there's no treatment of: verifying the reply is genuinely from the right owner; handling partial/ambiguous replies, attachments, or free-text; preventing spoofing; or what happens when the reply contradicts a system source.

**Why it matters.** This is the wedge capability (wedge 2) *and* the point where untrusted, unstructured input becomes a load-bearing governed fact. It's the most attackable and most error-prone seam in the product.

**Evidence.** North Star §5 ("Response received from Maria Keller … Confidence: high"); [collect-and-chase.md](../06-features/data-collection-and-chase.md). Verification/robustness unaddressed.

**Proposed solution.**
- **Sender verification & tenancy binding** on every inbound reply before it can become a fact (ties to [G2](#g2--confidentiality--llm-data-handling-under-specified)).
- A **quarantine + human-accept step** (already implied by the *Commit* accept) but with the parsed interpretation shown side-by-side with the raw reply for the preparer to confirm.
- **Reply intelligence** to handle attachments, partial answers, and clarifying follow-ups — see [I7](./product-improvements.md#i7--data-owner-reply-intelligence).
- **Conflict rule**: a collected value that contradicts a system source is flagged, never silently preferred.

---

## G9 · Ask AI is a named layer with no spec

**Severity: High · Theme: Experience**

**What's missing.** Ask AI is the **near-term deliverable** and step 2 of the commercial path, but it's defined only by negation (read-only; "not a bridge"). There's no spec for what it does, its surface, or how it seeds the move to the Operator without contradicting "not a bridge."

**Why it matters.** It's the thing shipping first. Under-specifying the near-term product to focus on the north star risks shipping a vague "chat with your filing" that neither delivers standalone value nor sets up the Operator.

**Evidence.** §2 ("Ask AI explains … read-only intelligence in its own right"), §8 ("Deliver Ask AI in Base CRR as the near-term, read-only step"). No feature detail. Memory reflects the same ([overview.md](../01-product-overview/overview.md)).

**Proposed solution.**
- Write an **Ask AI capability spec**: compliance Q&A grounded in the knowledge base (with citations — honoring "no uncited regulatory answers"), field/period/entity explanations, provenance lookups, and blocker explanations.
- Define its **standalone value metric** (questions answered without opening a ticket / SME) so it earns its keep independently.
- Design it to **share the Operator's Read context and provenance UI** so users who later adopt the Operator find it familiar — continuity without positioning it as a mere on-ramp.

---

## G10 · No collaboration / concurrency model

**Severity: Medium · Theme: Experience**

**What's missing.** The four seats are defined as roles, but real filings involve multiple preparers, delegation, out-of-office handoffs, and concurrent work across many entities. There's no model for who can act when, delegation, locking, or notifications between humans (as opposed to between human and Operator).

**Why it matters.** Enterprise filings are team sports. A single-preparer mental model breaks for large multi-entity filings (BE-11 with 42 affiliates already implies parallel work).

**Evidence.** [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md) defines seats, not collaboration; no concurrency treatment in flows.

**Proposed solution.**
- Support **multiple preparers with scoped assignment** (by entity/section) and explicit **delegation** with audit.
- Define **concurrency semantics** for the shared filing run (who can commit what; optimistic locking on scope/package).
- Add **human-to-human notifications/handoffs** distinct from Operator prompts (e.g. "reassign these 10 affiliates to a colleague").

**Now designed →** [F6 Collaboration & presence](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md) implements this: presence, role tiers (viewer/commenter/actor), per-actor attribution (human + agent), concurrency with locking on signature commits, and delegation/handoff.

---

## G11 · Regulatory-change management mid-cycle

**Severity: Medium · Theme: Continuity**

**What's missing.** Rule packs are versioned, but there's no story for a rule/regulation change *landing while filings are in flight* or affecting future obligations — how customers are notified, how in-progress runs are re-checked, and how the SDC/SME publishing loop is triggered by an external change.

**Why it matters.** Regulations change; agencies revise forms and thresholds. If the substrate only updates when an SME happens to notice, the "governed" promise has a blind spot.

**Evidence.** §6 (rule sets "versioned"); no change-propagation mechanism. Blueprint has "effective dates" but propagation is unaddressed.

**Proposed solution.**
- Define **rule-pack version propagation**: when a new version publishes, the Operator identifies affected in-flight runs and future obligations and surfaces a re-check / delta.
- Respect **effective dates** so a mid-cycle change applies correctly (not retroactively unless required).
- Feed the **regulatory-change radar** ([I6](./product-improvements.md#i6--regulatory-change-radar)) into the SDC authoring queue automatically.

---

## G12 · No success metrics / measurement framework

**Severity: Medium · Theme: Commercial**

**What's missing.** The value story ("fewer coordination cycles, faster readiness, more confident sign-off") is entirely qualitative. There are no defined KPIs, baselines, or instrumentation to prove ROI — for the customer or for Workiva.

**Why it matters.** Leadership will ask "how will we know it's working?" and customers will ask "what's the ROI?" The before/after story needs numbers. Metrics also feed adaptive autonomy and the trust dashboard.

**Evidence.** §8 asks for a *sizing* number but no *product* metrics. Before/after in [customer-journey-map.md](../08-customer-journey/customer-journey-map.md#before--after) is qualitative.

**Proposed solution.**
- Define **outcome KPIs**: time-to-readiness, coordination cycles saved, chase closure rate & time, reviewer sign-off time, exception rate, override rate, on-time filing rate.
- Capture a **baseline** (the operating history already saved at close — [package-and-close.md](../05-operator-flows/package-and-close.md) — is the perfect substrate for this) and show trend across cycles.
- Surface a **customer-facing ROI view** and an internal product-health dashboard.

---

## G13 · Pricing / packaging of the Operator undefined

**Severity: Medium · Theme: Commercial**

**What's missing.** The commercial path (Base CRR → Ask AI → high-value agent → full Operator) and the Pack SKU model are described, but *how the Operator itself is priced* — per Pack, per filing, per seat, or consumption (agent actions) — is absent.

**Why it matters.** The action model has real per-action cost (agent runs, deterministic checks, chase orchestration). Pricing must align value capture with that cost and with the wedge strategy (Data Collection & Chase adoptable alone implies a component price).

**Evidence.** §5 (Packs set "pricing and packaging"); §7 (wedges adoptable alone). No Operator pricing model.

**Proposed solution.**
- Decide the **pricing axis**: recommend Pack-based platform pricing (predictable for the buyer) with the wedge capabilities as **entry SKUs** (Obligation Scout, Data Collection & Chase) that credit toward the full Operator.
- Model **cost-to-serve** per filing (agent + eval + deterministic compute) to protect margin as autonomy rises.
- Align pricing with the **earned-autonomy** ladder ([I2](./product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy)) — value grows as trust grows.

---

## G14 · The submission last mile is a broken audit loop

**Severity: Medium · Theme: Commercial**

**What's missing.** Submission is deliberately "outside CRR" — the Operator *stages* the package. But the audit trail therefore ends *before the actual filing*, and the proof-of-filing (agency receipt) isn't captured back. The story that closes with "prove what we filed" has a hole at the last step.

**Why it matters.** The whole value is a defensible, complete audit trail. Ending it one step short of the actual submission weakens the strongest claim. Base CRR already has a "submission receipt" concept to build on.

**Evidence.** [package-and-close.md](../05-operator-flows/package-and-close.md) ("agency upload happens outside CRR"); base CRR [submission receipts](../../CRR%20Product%20Memory/02-glossary/glossary.md).

**Proposed solution.**
- **Capture the receipt back**: prompt the preparer to upload/record the agency confirmation into the audit trail, closing the loop (lightweight, no e-file build).
- Where agency APIs exist, offer **optional direct submission** as a later capability (a *Commit*-level action with the heaviest gate).
- Reconcile **filed vs approved**: the Operator confirms what was submitted matches the approved package.

---

## G15 · Change management for the human roles

**Severity: Medium · Theme: Adoption**

**What's missing.** The product asks controllers to shift from "sign on faith" to "sign on a ledger produced by an agent," and preparers from operators to governors. That's a significant behavior and trust change with no onboarding, trust-building, or objection-handling story.

**Why it matters.** The best-designed Operator fails if a controller doesn't trust it enough to sign, or a preparer keeps re-doing the work manually "to be safe." Adoption risk is a product risk, not just a GTM one.

**Evidence.** §4 ("confidence, not faith") describes the destination, not the transition. No onboarding/trust-ramp in the memory.

**Proposed solution.**
- Ship a **trust ramp**: shadow/advisory mode for a customer's first cycles (Operator recommends, human still does), then graduate to acting — mirrors [earned autonomy](./product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy) at the org level.
- Provide the **[trust dashboard](./product-improvements.md#i9--operator-trust-dashboard)** as an onboarding artifact ("here's the Operator's track record on your filings").
- Design the **first-approval experience** specifically for a skeptical controller (make the cross-check and provenance impossible to miss).

---

## Theme summary

| Theme | Gaps | Net message |
|-------|------|-------------|
| Trust & correctness | G1, G4, G5, G8 | Design for being *wrong*, not just right — correction, confidence, eval, ingestion trust |
| Foundation & security | G2, G3 | The substrate's *security* and *authoring throughput* are the real constraints |
| Continuity | G6, G7, G11 | The always-on / between-cycles dimension is under-built |
| Experience | G9, G10 | Ship-first (Ask AI) and team reality (collaboration) need specs |
| Commercial & adoption | G12, G13, G14, G15 | Prove it, price it, close the loop, and land the behavior change |

## How to read this

These are **additive** ideas that would make Agentic CRR better — not holes to fill (those are in [gaps-and-solutions.md](./gaps-and-solutions.md)), but opportunities to strengthen the product's moat, value, and demo. Each has an **impact × effort** call, the **idea**, **why it wins**, and **how to build it**. Some amplify a gap-solution; those links are noted.

---

## I1 · Compounding facts across the portfolio

**Impact: High · Effort: Med**

**Idea.** Make an accepted [governed fact](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-fact) reusable across *every* filing that needs it, not just year-over-year within one report. If FY25 net income for Germany Manufacturing GmbH is accepted for BE-11, it should pre-populate BE-577, BE-125, and any other Pack filing that requires the same figure — with shared provenance.

**Why it wins.** The brief's own problem statement is *"knowledge never compounds."* The current solution compounds *within* a report over time (next-year baseline) but not *across* the portfolio in a period. Cross-filing reuse is the deepest expression of the thesis and a hard-to-copy moat — it's only possible because Workiva holds the governed substrate and the data. It also multiplies the value of every chase (collect once, use everywhere).

**How to build it.** A **period fact store** keyed by (entity, field concept, period) that any filing run can draw from, with confidence and provenance carried across. Conflicts and supersessions propagate (ties to [G1](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g1--no-correction-amendment-or-restatement-lifecycle)). Requires a shared field ontology across blueprints (the master-field/knowledge-base layer already points here).

---

## I2 · Earned, adaptive autonomy

**Impact: High · Effort: Med**

**Idea.** Make the action model's default confirmation levels **adaptive per report type and customer**, tightening or loosening based on measured track record. Where the Operator has proven (low override rate, high deterministic agreement) it can default certain *Prepare* steps to auto — always within the customer's configured ceiling.

**Why it wins.** The brief says autonomy "rises as trust accrues" but the mechanism is static. Making it *measured and earned* turns trust into a product feature, directly reduces approval fatigue over time, and gives customers a controllable dial. It's the natural payoff of a real [confidence model (G4)](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g4--no-defined-confidence-model) and [eval (G5)](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g5--evaluation--shadow-mode-asserted-not-designed).

**How to build it.** Track predicted-vs-actual accuracy per capability/report/customer; expose a customer-set **autonomy ceiling**; never let earned autonomy cross a signature commit or a regulatory gate. Surface the current level in the [trust dashboard (I9)](#i9--operator-trust-dashboard).

---

## I3 · Regulator-ready explainability artifact

**Impact: High · Effort: Low**

**Idea.** Turn the [judgment ledger](../02-glossary/glossary.md#judgment-ledger) + audit trail into an **exportable, regulator-/auditor-facing narrative** of exactly how the filing was produced: every decision, source, threshold, override, and verification, in a clean document.

**Why it wins.** The audit trail is the product's strongest claim; today it lives inside the app. Making it a *deliverable* creates a tangible artifact auditors and regulators love, differentiates hard from spreadsheet-based filing, and turns "defensible" from a promise into a document. Low effort because the data already exists at close.

**How to build it.** A templated export from the ledger + package metadata (blueprint/rule-pack versions, approvals, provenance). Reuse Workiva's document/branding tooling. Offer as part of the evidence bundle in [package-and-close.md](../05-operator-flows/package-and-close.md).

---

## I4 · Diff-first reviewer experience

**Impact: High · Effort: Low**

**Idea.** Make **"what changed"** the primary lens for the reviewer everywhere, not just at scope. At final approval, lead with the delta vs last approved version / last year, so review collapses to adjudicating changes rather than re-reading the whole filing.

**Why it wins.** The brief already does this for scope ("what changed from last year"); extending it to review is the single highest-leverage way to hit the "sign in minutes" goal and design against approval fatigue. Very low effort — it's a presentation of data already in the ledger.

**How to build it.** A diff view over prior approved state; group unchanged items collapsed by default ([P7](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine)); highlight new/changed/removed outcomes and values with their reasons.

---

## I5 · What-if simulation before commit

**Impact: Med · Effort: Med**

**Idea.** Let preparers run **non-committal simulations** against the deterministic evaluators — "if Brazil's FY25 revenue comes in at X, which affiliates change treatment?" — to see downstream scope/readiness impact before data is final.

**Why it wins.** Turns the deterministic substrate into a planning tool, not just a checker. Helps teams anticipate the threshold flips the Operator would otherwise catch late (North Star §6), and makes the "not-yet-decidable" wait productive.

**How to build it.** Run the rule set/evaluators on hypothetical inputs in a sandboxed *Read/Recommend* mode; never writes state. Surface as an option on scope items and deferred decisions.

---

## I6 · Regulatory-change radar

**Impact: High · Effort: High**

**Idea.** Proactively monitor for agency rule/form/threshold changes and alert affected customers, in-flight runs, and future obligations — auto-opening a rule-pack delta for SDC/SME review.

**Why it wins.** Extends the "front door" from *do I have an obligation* to *did my obligations change* — the always-on compliance value that [G7](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g7--loss-of-the-always-on-monitoring-dimension) and [G11](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g11--regulatory-change-management-mid-cycle) call for. It's a strong retention and expansion hook and reinforces "governed."

**How to build it.** Feed agency-source monitoring into the knowledge base; diff against current rule packs; route deltas to the SDC authoring queue ([I8](#i8--assisted-self-service-substrate-authoring)) and surface customer alerts via the standing monitoring layer. High effort due to the breadth of agency sources.

---

## I7 · Data-owner reply intelligence

**Impact: Med · Effort: Med**

**Idea.** Make the chase robust to how people actually reply: parse attachments (spreadsheets, PDFs), extract values from free-text, handle partial answers, and auto-send clarifying follow-ups — before the preparer accepts.

**Why it wins.** The chase is wedge 2 and the most concrete "agentic" moment; its real-world robustness determines whether it delights or frustrates. Directly strengthens [G8](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g8--chase-ingestion-trust--security).

**How to build it.** Attachment extraction + value mapping with confidence; a clarification loop when a reply is partial/ambiguous; show parsed interpretation beside the raw reply for human accept. Bind to sender verification (G8/G2).

---

## I8 · Assisted self-service substrate authoring

**Impact: High · Effort: High**

**Idea.** Tooling that lets SDCs/SMEs (and eventually advanced customers) author and extend governed bundles far faster — agent-drafted blueprints, rules, and test cases from the knowledge base, with SME review and auto-generated shadow tests.

**Why it wins.** This is the lever on the single biggest scaling constraint ([G3](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g3--sdcsme-authoring-throughput-is-the-real-scaling-constraint)). Faster authoring = a bigger catalog = more Obligation Scout on-ramps = more of the "many reports" promise realized. It compounds every other capability.

**How to build it.** An authoring studio in the config builder: knowledge-base → drafted blueprint/rule set, test-case generation from prior filings, diff/version review, shadow-mode wiring. Governed: agents draft, humans publish (the brief's stated model, made real and fast).

---

## I9 · Operator trust dashboard

**Impact: Med · Effort: Low**

**Idea.** A view of the Operator's **track record**: recommendations accepted vs overridden, agreement with deterministic checks, exceptions caught, chase closure, accuracy trends — per report type and customer.

**Why it wins.** Trust is the adoption bottleneck ([G15](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g15--change-management-for-the-human-roles)). Making the Operator's reliability *visible* builds institutional confidence, supports [earned autonomy (I2)](#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy), and gives champions an internal selling tool. Low effort if [metrics (G12)](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g12--no-success-metrics--measurement-framework) exist.

**How to build it.** Aggregate the metrics from G12/G4/G5 into a per-customer view; pair with the ROI/outcome KPIs.

---

## I10 · Anonymized peer benchmarking

**Impact: Med · Effort: Med**

**Idea.** Use Workiva's multi-tenant position to offer anonymized benchmarks: "filings like yours take N days; your chase volume is 20% above peers; teams like you start BE-11 six weeks earlier."

**Why it wins.** A moat only Workiva's install base enables. Turns the saved operating history into cross-customer insight, strengthens the monitoring plan, and adds standalone value to the portfolio workspace.

**How to build it.** Aggregate operating-history metrics across tenants with strict anonymization/privacy controls (ties to [G2](./gaps-and-solutions.md#g2--confidentiality--llm-data-handling-under-specified)); surface as optional benchmarks in monitoring and close.

---

## I11 · Graceful degradation to manual

**Impact: Med · Effort: Low**

**Idea.** When the Operator can't safely proceed (no source, novel case, confidence below floor, capability not configured), hand off cleanly to fully-manual Base CRR **without losing state** — and let the preparer resume Operator assistance later.

**Why it wins.** Removes the "what if it gets stuck?" objection, reinforces "the human is a governor," and makes the Operator safe to adopt even where the substrate is incomplete (respecting the "can only automate what Base CRR can represent" guardrail). Low effort because Base CRR already does the manual path.

**How to build it.** A defined fallback state per phase that preserves the filing run and provenance; an explicit "take it from here" / "hand back to Operator" toggle.

---

## I12 · Unstructured / human-only source capture

**Impact: Med · Effort: Med**

**Idea.** Handle data that lives in documents or people's heads, not source systems — extract from uploaded PDFs/spreadsheets and structure ad-hoc human knowledge into governed facts with provenance.

**Why it wins.** The model assumes source systems + mappings, but real filings depend on unstructured and human-only inputs. Broadens coverage of the "84% of values found" gap toward the harder remaining fraction, and reduces the chase burden.

**How to build it.** Document extraction into candidate facts (with confidence + provenance to the source doc); route low-confidence extractions to review; reuse the chase-ingestion trust controls (G8).

**Now designed →** the first slice ships as **manual upload on request**: when a required figure has no connected source, the Operator asks the preparer to upload a file, accepts it as a governed fact with the file as evidence, and registers it on the **Source data** surface. See [source-discovery-and-ingestion.md](../06-features/source-discovery-and-ingestion.md#manual-upload--when-no-source-exists).

---

## Sequencing recommendation

| Horizon | Ship | Rationale |
|---------|------|-----------|
| **Now (fold into prototype)** | I3, I4, I11 | Low effort, high demo/adoption impact; make the two signature moments and the "safe to adopt" story land |
| **Foundational (build alongside substrate)** | I8, I2 (needs G4/G5) | Attack the scaling constraint and turn trust into a feature |
| **Differentiators (portfolio value)** | I1, I6, I10 | The compounding-knowledge moat that only Workiva can build |
| **Robustness (make the wedge delightful)** | I7, I12, I5, I9 | Harden the chase and the planning experience |

A critical read of the current Agentic CRR thinking, as captured in the [product brief](../INDEX.md) and this product memory. The goal is to strengthen the concept **before** the North Star prototype is locked — surfacing what the brief assumes, skips, or under-specifies, and where the product could be materially better.

> **Method.** This is an internal product-strategy analysis grounded in the *Agentic CRR Product Brief (v3)*, the *JTBD Map*, and the memory in sections 01–09. It is opinionated by design. Severity/priority calls are judgments to debate, not verdicts. Where a gap or idea connects to an existing memory doc, it's linked.

> **Update (2026-07-01).** Several items here now have proposed feature designs in [section 11 — Agent Operations & Workspace](../11-agent-operations/README.md): scheduled agents address **G6, G7, G11** and deliver **I6**; the registry delivers **I2** and supports **I8**; the Artifact Library delivers **I3** and supports **G1**; context management supports **I1, G4, G15**; and **collaboration & presence (F6) resolves G10**. The brief nails the **operating model** (govern, not operate) and the **governance spine** (action model + contract + substrate). The biggest *upside* left on the table is **compounding knowledge across the portfolio**, not just year-over-year within one report — which is the brief's own stated problem ("knowledge never compounds").

## Summary

The Operator **reconciles and re-tests on real numbers**. Now that accepted facts exist, it re-runs the checks — and if a figure flips a threshold status, it does **not** quietly continue with a stale scope decision. It surfaces the change and prepares an approval delta.

## Actor(s)

- [Preparer](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer)
- [Reviewer-approver](../03-personas/personas.md#reviewer-approver-controller--responsible-officer) — confirms any scope delta
- Operator (Validation & Readiness capability)

## Steps

1. Operator reconciles accepted facts and re-tests thresholds/rules on the real numbers.
2. Detects a **scope change** where a figure now crosses a threshold (e.g. *"Brazil Services Ltd. now appears to exceed the BE-11B threshold based on accepted FY25 revenue"*).
3. Next best step: *"Want me to reopen scope for this affiliate and prepare the approval delta?"*
4. Preparer clicks **Prepare scope update**; the reviewer reviews the **delta** and confirms the change (loops back to [Scope](./scope-and-confirmation.md) for that item only).
5. When reconciliation is clean, the run advances to [Prepare & assemble](./prepare-and-assemble.md).

## Flow diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Facts[Accepted governed facts] --> Reconcile[Reconcile + re-test on real numbers]
  Reconcile --> Flip{Figure flips threshold status?}
  Flip -->|yes| Delta[Prepare approval delta]
  Delta --> ReviewerDelta[Reviewer confirms scope delta]
  ReviewerDelta --> Clean[Reconciliation clean]
  Flip -->|no| Clean
  Clean --> Next[Advance to Prepare & assemble]
```

## Human checkpoint

Preparer adjudicates flagged anomalies; the reviewer confirms any scope delta. This is *Recommend · Prepare* — with a *Commit* only when a scope delta is confirmed.

## Action level & state signal

- **Action level:** Recommend · Prepare (Commit on confirmed scope delta)
- **State signal:** Facts reconciled; scope reopened only where a figure changed treatment.

## Contract guardrail

**No silent state changes.** A threshold flip reopens scope with an explicit, approvable delta — never a quiet edit to a confirmed decision.

## Outcomes

- **Success:** Numbers reconciled; any treatment change is caught and re-approved.
- **Loop:** Confirmed deltas re-enter scope for the affected item only, not the whole plan.

## Related

- Prev: [Collect & chase](./collect-and-chase.md) · Next: [Prepare & assemble](./prepare-and-assemble.md)
- Reopen path: [Scope & confirmation](./scope-and-confirmation.md)

## Summary

After approval, the Operator **stages the filing package** for the customer's approved submission process and **closes the cycle so next year starts ahead** — saving both the filing record and the operating history behind it.

## Actor(s)

- [Preparer](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer)
- Operator (Package & Filing capability)

## Steps

1. Operator stages the package (*"BE-11 package is complete · Evidence bundle created · Next-year baseline saved"*).
2. The package includes: final forms, evidence, source provenance, approval record, comments, exceptions, overrides, audit trail, blueprint version, and rule-pack version.
3. Operator also saves the **operating history**: confirmed scope, mappings, source locations, routed owners, response times, late inputs, rework, scope changes, evidence gaps, and resolved exceptions.
4. Next best step: *"Want me to create next year's monitoring plan?"* Preparer clicks **Create monitoring plan**.
5. Operator recommends when next year's filing should start — based on how long this one took, which entities caused delays, where manual collection was needed, and which inputs created rework.

## Flow diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Approved[Package approved & locked] --> Stage[Stage package for approved submission process]
  Stage --> Bundle[Assemble evidence bundle + provenance + audit]
  Bundle --> Baseline[Save next-year baseline]
  Baseline --> History[Save operating history of the cycle]
  History --> Monitor[Create next-year monitoring plan]
```

## Human checkpoint

Preparer authorizes staging and creation of the monitoring plan. Agency upload happens **outside CRR** via the customer's approved submission process.

## Action level & state signal

- **Action level:** Commit (stage/close) · Read (monitoring recommendation)
- **State signal:** Filing complete; baseline + operating history saved; next cycle seeded.

## Boundary

The Operator **stages** the package; it does not e-file to the agency. Submission is the customer's approved process, outside CRR.

## Outcomes

- **Success:** Complete package staged; next year starts pre-scoped, not from a blank page.
- **Loop to front door:** The monitoring plan feeds next period's [Front door / Obligation Scout](./front-door-obligation.md).

## Summary

**This is where the Operator becomes visibly agentic** — the system acts. The preparer stops chasing people across email threads and spreadsheets. Each missing fact becomes a targeted request tied to a specific filing field, affiliate, owner, due date, and evidence requirement. The Operator sends, chases, escalates, and captures replies — turning each response into a [governed fact](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-fact) once accepted.

> This is **wedge 2** — the entry point into the full Operator. A customer can adopt Data Collection & Chase alone, feel the value, and grow into the rest.

## Actor(s)

- [Preparer](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer) — approves who's asked and deadlines, accepts returned values
- [Data / Source Owner](../03-personas/personas.md#data--source-owner-contributor) — answers targeted requests in place
- Operator (Data Collection & Chase capability)

## Steps

1. Operator turns each gap into managed work (e.g. *"12 missing inputs · 8 requests ready to send · 2 need owner confirmation · 2 overdue from prior cycle"*).
2. Previews a task: *"For the FY25 BE-11 filing, please provide year-end employee count and net income after foreign income tax for Germany Manufacturing GmbH. These values will be used for BE-11B readiness."*
3. Next best step: *"Send this request by email and track the response here?"* Preparer reviews and clicks **Send** (*Commit*).
4. Owner replies on their existing channel — **no new workflow to learn**.
5. Operator captures the reply and maps values to fields (*"Employee count → BE-11B Item 10 · Net income → BE-11B Item 7 · Confidence: high · Evidence attached"*).
6. Next best step: *"Accept these values as governed facts?"* Preparer clicks **Accept** (*Commit*). Worklist updates (*8 received · 2 pending · 2 overdue*).
7. For overdue items: *"Send a Teams reminder and escalate if no response by Friday?"* → escalation.

## Flow diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Gaps[Missing facts] --> Requests[Draft field-level requests]
  Requests --> Preview[Preview request to owner]
  Preview --> Send[Preparer: Send - Commit]
  Send --> Wait[Track: requested]
  Wait --> Reply[Owner replies on their channel]
  Reply --> Capture[Capture & map to fields]
  Capture --> Accept{Accept as governed fact?}
  Accept -->|yes Commit| Fact[Governed fact + evidence]
  Wait -->|overdue| Escalate[Reminder / escalate]
  Escalate --> Reply
```

## Request state machine

`requested → submitted → accepted / rejected` (with escalation on overdue) — full provenance and audit. See [lifecycle-and-action-model.md](../04-information-architecture/lifecycle-and-action-model.md#request-lifecycle-within-phase-d).

## Human checkpoints

- **Preparer** approves who is asked and the deadlines; accepts each returned value (Commit).
- **Data owners** enter/confirm their own values — the data stays theirs.

## Action level & state signal

- **Action level:** Prepare (drafts) · Commit (sends, accepts)
- **State signal:** Gaps move requested → submitted → accepted; accepted replies become governed facts.

## Contract guardrails

Acts only through bounded tools — *Prepare* drafts, *Commit* sends with permission and audit, accepted replies become governed facts. **No silent state changes.**

## Outcomes

- **Success:** Missing data closed to governed facts without manual chasing.
- **Escalation:** Overdue items get reminders/escalation on the right channel.

## Related

- Capability: [Data Collection & Chase](../06-features/data-collection-and-chase.md)

## Summary

The Operator **starts ahead**. Before the preparer touches anything, it has read the prior filing, current entity data, available source context, the filing blueprint, and the current rule pack — and organizes what is *known*, what is *likely*, and what still needs *confirmation*. It does not declare a legal conclusion.

## Actor(s)

- [Preparer](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer)
- Operator (Obligation Scout capability)

## Entry points & preconditions

- **Entry:** Preparer opens Agentic CRR and sees a readiness briefing already prepared; or Obligation Scout nudges from a signal Workiva already holds (e.g. 10-K subsidiary disclosures).
- **Preconditions:** A published [governed bundle](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-bundle) for the filing (blueprint + rule set + skills); prior-year filing and entity data available in Base CRR.

## What the Operator does

1. Reads rules, facts, and prior filings.
2. Returns each obligation as **required**, **confirm**, or **not-yet-decidable** — the honest state when a dependency (e.g. current-year financials) doesn't exist yet.
3. Presents a **readiness briefing** (e.g. *"Prior-year filing found. 42 foreign affiliates detected. 31 unchanged. 6 need ownership confirmation. 5 not yet decidable until current-year financials."*).
4. Offers the **next best step**: *"Want me to prepare a scope plan for review?"*

## Human checkpoint

Preparer reviews the briefing and clicks **Prepare scope plan**. Nothing official has changed — this phase is *Read · Recommend*.

## Flow diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Open[Preparer opens Operator] --> Scan[Scan rules / facts / prior filings]
  Signal[Obligation signal e.g. 10-K Exhibit 21] --> Scan
  Scan --> Briefing[Readiness briefing]
  Briefing --> Classify{Per obligation}
  Classify --> Req[Required]
  Classify --> Conf[Needs confirmation]
  Classify --> NYD[Not yet decidable]
  Briefing --> NBS[Next best step: prepare scope plan?]
  NBS --> Prepare[Preparer clicks Prepare scope plan]
```

## Multi-obligation intake

The front door is **not limited to one form.** A user can start from data — *"Here's our group data, figure out what we need to file"* — and the Operator detects the **full [obligation set](../02-glossary/glossary.md#obligation-set)**, spinning up a coordinated filing per obligation.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Data[User: here's our data, what do we file?] --> Detect[Scan data vs all governed rule sets]
  Detect --> Set{Obligation set}
  Set --> O1[BE-11 - required]
  Set --> O2[Country-by-Country - required]
  Set --> O3[Another - not yet decidable]
  O1 --> Confirm[Human confirms which to pursue]
  O2 --> Confirm
  Confirm --> Runs[One filing run per confirmed obligation]
  Runs --> Reuse[Shared facts reused across runs]
  Runs --> Home[Coordinated on Home / Dashboard]
```

- Each obligation is **recommended, never asserted** — cited evidence + threshold; the human picks which to run.
- Each confirmed obligation then runs the normal lifecycle ([Scope → Close]), while shared facts flow between them.
- See [Obligation Scout](../06-features/obligation-scout.md#multi-obligation-intake-here-is-my-data-what-do-i-file) and the [Country-by-Country example](./report-patterns/country-by-country.md).

## Action level & state signal

- **Action level:** Read · Recommend (runs freely; cites evidence)
- **State signal:** No filing run yet; readiness briefing (or obligation set) produced. Transitioning to Phase B on Prepare — **per obligation**.

## Outcomes

- **Success:** A prepared briefing and a clear next best step — no blank page.
- **Honest gap:** *Not-yet-decidable* items are named, not guessed.
- **On-ramp variant:** For a non-CRR customer, Obligation Scout is the way in; the upgrade lands **pre-scoped** (affiliate list, prior context, blueprint, required facts already prepared).

## Summary

The reviewer **signs from a judgment ledger**, not a stack of forms. This is the second [signature commit](../02-glossary/glossary.md#signature-commits) and the moment the whole design is built around: the reviewer signs in minutes because the ledger is complete — or refuses with the exact divergence named.

## Actor(s)

- [Reviewer-approver](../03-personas/personas.md#reviewer-approver-controller--responsible-officer) — final approval
- Operator (Review & Approval capability + final verification)

## Steps

1. Operator presents the **judgment ledger**: final scope, changes from last year, every affiliate & filing outcome, every threshold decision, every value with source, every warning & resolution, every override, and the final verification result.
2. Operator summarizes (*"Final verification passed · No blocking issues · 3 warnings resolved · 1 accepted value came from an email response rather than a direct system source — evidence attached"*).
3. Operator asks for the decision: *"Approve final package, or send back with comments?"*
4. Reviewer clicks **Approve final package** → package is **locked**, approval recorded. (Or sends back → returns to [Prepare & assemble](./prepare-and-assemble.md).)

## Flow diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Ready[Package ready for review] --> Ledger[Judgment ledger]
  Ledger --> Verify[Final verification]
  Verify --> Decision{Approve or send back?}
  Decision -->|Approve - Commit| Lock[Package locked + approval recorded]
  Decision -->|Send back with comments| Back[Return to Prepare & assemble]
```

## Human checkpoint

The reviewer makes the **signature commit** — *Approve final package*. Recorded with user, timestamp, versions, and the ledger state.

## Action level & state signal

- **Action level:** **Commit** (signature commit #2)
- **State signal:** Package locked; approval recorded; run advances to close.

## Design weight & governance

The second of the two design-weight moments: the ledger must make the reviewer's judgment **legible** so approval is confidence, not faith. Final certification is typically **regulatory** governance (legally binding); internal reviewer count is **corporate** governance (configurable). See [governance-and-action-model.md](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md).

## Contract guardrails

**No package release without final approval.** **Every override recorded** — the ledger names any override rather than hiding it.

## Outcomes

- **Success:** Locked, approved package with a complete decision record.
- **Refusal:** Reviewer sends back with the exact divergence named; the run returns to Prepare.

## Related

- Prev: [Prepare & assemble](./prepare-and-assemble.md) · Next: [Package & close](./package-and-close.md)
- Capability: [Review & Approval](../06-features/review-and-approval.md)

## Summary

Scope becomes a **decision**, not a rebuild. The Operator builds the ownership graph, groups affiliates/claims by recommended outcome with evidence and the rule behind each, self-cross-checks with a deterministic evaluator, and routes the few flagged items — then the reviewer **confirms scope** (the first [signature commit](../02-glossary/glossary.md#signature-commits)).

## Actor(s)

- [Preparer](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer) — reviews and resolves flags, sends for approval
- [Reviewer-approver](../03-personas/personas.md#reviewer-approver-controller--responsible-officer) — confirms scope
- Operator (Scope & Entity capability + deterministic cross-check)

## Steps

1. Operator opens a **Scope Plan**: affiliates grouped by outcome (e.g. *BE-11B*, *BE-11D*, *BE-11A rollup*, *Claim for Not Filing*, *Needs confirmation*, *Not decidable yet*).
2. Each item shows evidence + rule (e.g. *"Germany Manufacturing GmbH — BE-11B recommended · majority-owned · current-year sales above threshold · Evidence: FY25 ERP revenue table · Rule: BE-11 affiliate size test"*).
3. A few rows are flagged for review (*"3 scope items need review before approval"*).
4. Next best step: *"Route these scope questions to the right owners before sending for approval?"* Preparer resolves some, routes others.
5. Operator re-runs the **independent cross-check** (*"no blocking issues"*) and marks the plan **ready for reviewer confirmation**.
6. Preparer clicks **Send for scope approval**.
7. Reviewer opens scope review — sees proposed scope, what changed from last year, exceptions resolved, and the cross-check — and clicks **Confirm scope** (or sends back with comments).

## Flow diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Prepare[Prepare scope plan] --> Graph[Build ownership graph]
  Graph --> Group[Group by recommended outcome]
  Group --> Flag{Flagged items?}
  Flag -->|yes| Route[Route questions to owners / resolve]
  Route --> Xcheck[Deterministic cross-check]
  Flag -->|no| Xcheck
  Xcheck --> Ready[Ready for reviewer confirmation]
  Ready --> Send[Preparer: Send for scope approval]
  Send --> Review[Reviewer: what changed + exceptions + cross-check]
  Review -->|Confirm scope| Locked[Scope confirmed - recorded]
  Review -->|Send back| Route
```

## Human checkpoints

- **Preparer** approves who is asked and resolves flags (Recommend → Prepare).
- **Reviewer-approver** makes the **signature commit** — *Confirm scope* — recorded with user, timestamp, scope version, evidence, and rule-pack version.

## Action level & state signal

- **Action level:** Recommend → **Commit** (signature commit #1)
- **State signal:** Scope confirmed; filing run scoped. Ownership graph decides *who files*.

## Design weight

This is the first of the two moments that carry the most design weight: **present the plan beside its deterministic cross-check** — the most expensive mistakes are cheapest to catch here. See [design-patterns.md](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md).

## Outcomes

- **Success:** Confirmed scope on a legible plan; reviewer commits on evidence, not faith.
- **Reopen:** Scope can be reopened later if a figure flips status in [Validate](./validate.md); the Operator prepares an **approval delta** rather than continuing silently.

## Summary

With scope confirmed, the Operator **finds the data**. It matches required fields to source systems and prior mappings, pulls in-scope figures, and is honest about what it doesn't have — surfacing low-confidence mappings and missing facts rather than pretending everything is done.

## Actor(s)

- [Preparer](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer)
- Operator (Source Discovery & Ingestion + Mapping & Resolve capabilities)

## Steps

1. Operator reports coverage (e.g. *"I found likely sources for 84% of required BE-11 values"*).
2. Matches required fields to source systems and prior mappings — assets, sales/operating revenue, net income, employee count, industry classification, intercompany balances.
3. Produces an honest breakdown, e.g.:
   - 18 fields mapped with **high confidence**
   - 7 fields **need review**
   - 12 required facts **missing**
   - 4 source periods **need confirmation**
4. Offers the next best step: *"Want me to prepare the missing-data requests?"*
5. Preparer clicks **Prepare requests** → hands off to [Collect & chase](./collect-and-chase.md).

## Flow diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Confirmed[Scope confirmed] --> Discover[Discover sources / schemas / periods]
  Discover --> Map[Map fields to requirements]
  Map --> Pull[Pull in-scope figures]
  Pull --> Assess{Confidence per field}
  Assess --> High[High-confidence mapped]
  Assess --> Review[Needs review]
  Assess --> Missing[Missing facts]
  Assess --> Periods[Periods to confirm]
  Missing --> NBS[Next best step: prepare requests?]
```

## Human checkpoint

Preparer confirms source-file selection and reviews low-confidence mappings. This phase is *Recommend · Prepare* — figures are pulled but nothing is committed as a governed fact until accepted.

## Action level & state signal

- **Action level:** Recommend · Prepare
- **State signal:** Sources matched; required-fact gaps enumerated. Source & org intelligence identifies *where data lives* and *who to ask*.

## Contract guardrail

**No invented figures.** Every load-bearing number traces to a deterministic tool or an accepted source value; low-confidence mappings are flagged, not silently trusted.

## Outcomes

- **Success:** Most required values mapped from source; a precise list of what's still missing.
- **Handoff:** Missing facts become tracked requests in Phase D.

## Related

- Prev: [Scope & confirmation](./scope-and-confirmation.md) · Next: [Collect & chase](./collect-and-chase.md)
- Capabilities: [Source Discovery & Ingestion](../06-features/source-discovery-and-ingestion.md), [Mapping & Resolve](../06-features/mapping-and-resolve.md)

| **Agency** | IRS (Form 8975 / Schedule A) in the US; OECD BEPS Action 13 framework globally |
| **Category** | Multi-jurisdiction · multi-entity |
| **Files on** | Revenues, profit, tax paid/accrued, capital, earnings, employees, tangible assets — per tax jurisdiction |

## Why CbCR is here

CbCR is the memory's second concrete report (alongside the [BE-11 proof point](./be-11.md)) and the canonical example of **multi-obligation intake**: the *same* subsidiary and financial data that triggers BE-11 also triggers CbCR for large multinational groups. It proves the point that the product **does not work one form at a time** — see [obligation-scout.md](../../06-features/obligation-scout.md#multi-obligation-intake-here-is-my-data-what-do-i-file) and [front-door-obligation.md](../front-door-obligation.md#multi-obligation-intake).

## The multi-obligation moment

> Preparer: *"Here's our group data — figure out what we need to file."*
>
> Operator: *"From your subsidiary and financial data I see two likely obligations: **BE-11** (BEA direct-investment survey) and **Country-by-Country (Form 8975)** — your group appears above the €750M consolidated-revenue threshold. 1 more is not-yet-decidable pending final consolidation. Want me to prepare scope plans for both?"*

The Operator detects the **[obligation set](../../02-glossary/glossary.md#obligation-set)** from one data intake, recommends (never asserts) each, and — on confirmation — spins up **one coordinated filing run per obligation**, reusing shared facts across them ([I1 compounding facts](../../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i1--compounding-facts-across-the-portfolio)).

## What it shares with BE-11 (and what differs)

| Shared (same shape / substrate) | Differs (report-specific content) |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Front-door → close lifecycle; Read-to-Commit action model | Aggregation is by **tax jurisdiction**, not by affiliate |
| Ownership graph & entity data (who's in scope) | €750M consolidated-revenue filing threshold |
| Source & org intelligence (who to ask) | OECD/IRS taxonomy & Form 8975 layout; XML schema |
| Evidence, audit, judgment ledger, signature commits | Constituent-entity jurisdiction assignment rules |
| Many shared source facts (revenue, profit, tax, headcount) | Public/CbC exchange & confidentiality nuances |

**Fact reuse in action:** revenue, profit-before-tax, income-tax-paid, and employee counts accepted once as [governed facts](../../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-fact) feed *both* the BE-11 and CbCR runs — with shared provenance. Collect once, use across the obligation set.

## Coordination across the two filings

- Both runs appear on **[Home (Dashboard)](../../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout)** with their own readiness.
- Recommended to work in **separate sessions** (one per filing) for [context hygiene](../../11-agent-operations/context-and-communication.md), while shared facts flow between them via the fact store.
- Each keeps its own scope confirmation and final approval (signature commits are per filing).

## Report summary

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Report** | BE-11 — Annual Survey of U.S. Direct Investment Abroad |
| **Agency** | Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) |
| **Category** | Statistical / corporate · multi-entity |
| **Form types** | BE-11A (reporter), BE-11B (majority-owned), BE-11C (minority-owned), BE-11D (estimated) |
| **Pack** | Corporate Controllership (with BE-577, BE-125, BE-185, Census forms) |

## Why BE-11 is the first proof point

BE-11 is a strong proving ground because it combines, in one report, everything the Operator must do well:

- **Statistical filing** — survey items with agency-specific rules and exemptions
- **Multi-entity scoping** — many foreign affiliates, each with an outcome
- **Ownership logic** — majority/minority ownership drives form type (A/B/C/D)
- **Source mapping** — assets, revenue, net income, employee count, industry classification, intercompany balances
- **Validation & readiness** — threshold tests that can flip on real numbers
- **Package readiness** — multi-schedule package + evidence bundle

The same Operator, the same Read-to-Commit model, and the same governed substrate carry every other report — only the content changes.

## How the lifecycle instantiates for BE-11

| Phase | BE-11 specifics |
|-------|-----------------|
| **A · Front door** | Prior-year filing + affiliate list read; affiliates classified unchanged / needs confirmation / not-yet-decidable (pending current-year financials) |
| **B · Scope** | Affiliates grouped by outcome: BE-11B / BE-11D / BE-11A rollup / Claim for Not Filing / Needs confirmation / Not decidable. Ownership graph + affiliate size test; reviewer confirms scope |
| **C · Map & ingest** | Match required BE-11 values to ERP / consolidation sources & prior mappings; flag low-confidence mappings and periods to confirm |
| **D · Collect & chase** | Field-level requests to affiliate controllers (e.g. employee count → BE-11B Item 10, net income → Item 7) |
| **E · Validate** | Re-test size thresholds on accepted figures; reopen scope if an affiliate crosses (e.g. Brazil Services Ltd. now exceeds BE-11B threshold) |
| **F · Prepare & assemble** | Populate BE-11A + affiliate forms from accepted facts; readiness view (% ready, blockers, warnings, evidence) |
| **G · Review** | Judgment ledger: final scope, changes from last year, every outcome/threshold/value/override + final verification |
| **H · Close** | Stage package + evidence bundle; save next-year baseline & operating history; create monitoring plan |

## How this differs from base CRR's BE-11 flow

Base CRR ships BE-11 as a workbench the report owner operates step by step (scoping UI, one-click population, per-schedule editing, submission CSVs/bundle) — see the base [BE-11 form-class flow](../../../CRR%20Product%20Memory/05-user-flows/form-classes/be-11.md). Agentic CRR keeps the same underlying blueprint and exports but **inverts the operating model**:

| Base CRR (operate) | Agentic CRR (govern) |
|--------------------|----------------------|
| Owner scopes each entity × form by hand; AI scoping assists BE-11 only | Operator recommends per-affiliate outcomes with evidence + rule; reviewer confirms scope |
| One-click population is shallow; owner chases data by email | Operator maps from source, then chases every gap as tracked requests |
| Owner remembers what's left across forms | Readiness is visible (% ready, blockers, warnings) |
| No shipped formal review | Reviewer signs from a judgment ledger |
| Owner-gated exports; upload outside CRR | Operator stages the package + evidence bundle; upload still outside CRR |

## Related

- Full narrative: [North Star BE-11 story](../../08-customer-journey/north-star-be-11.md)
- Flows: [Front door](../front-door-obligation.md) → [Package & close](../package-and-close.md)

# Report Patterns

One pattern, many reports. The Operator is **report-agnostic in shape and report-specific in content** — the same Read-to-Commit action model and the same governed substrate carry every report; only the content changes. A preparer who has filed BE-11 should recognize the tax or grant flow instantly, because it is the same flow.

These docs are the Agentic CRR analog of base CRR's [form-class flows](../../../CRR%20Product%20Memory/05-user-flows/form-classes/README.md).

## Concrete reports

| Report | Why it's here | Doc |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| **BE-11** | The proof point — combines statistical filing, multi-entity scoping, ownership logic, source mapping, validation, and package readiness | [be-11.md](./be-11.md) |
| **Country-by-Country (CbCR)** | The multi-obligation example — arises from the *same* data as BE-11, proving the product doesn't work one form at a time | [country-by-country.md](./country-by-country.md) |

> **One data intake, many filings.** The Operator is not limited to one form at a time. From a single data intake it detects the whole **obligation set** (e.g. BE-11 *and* CbCR) and spins up a coordinated filing per obligation, reusing shared facts across them. See [Obligation Scout — multi-obligation intake](../../06-features/obligation-scout.md#multi-obligation-intake-here-is-my-data-what-do-i-file).

## Report categories

The same operating model spans the CRR portfolio. Each category doc describes **what varies** vs **what stays consistent**.

| Category | What varies | What stays consistent | Doc |
|----------|-------------|-----------------------|-----|
| Statistical / corporate | Agency rules, survey items, exemptions | Operator flow, Read-to-Commit, evidence, audit | [statistical-corporate.md](./statistical-corporate.md) |
| Multi-jurisdiction | Country rules, thresholds, agency formats | Same operating model, report-specific content | [multi-jurisdiction.md](./multi-jurisdiction.md) |
| Multi-entity | Ownership, intercompany, consolidation | Same scoping and exception model | [multi-entity.md](./multi-entity.md) |
| Financial | Taxonomies, standards, disclosures | Same provenance, validation, review model | [financial.md](./financial.md) |
| Sector-specific (FS, Public Sector) | Regulator layouts, sector rules, entity tiering | Same governed substrate and approval model | [sector-specific.md](./sector-specific.md) |

## How this maps to Packs

Commercially, filings are sold as **Packs** — SKU bundles of related forms. A Pack is a bundle of reports; each report is delivered by one [governed bundle](../../06-features/governed-substrate.md) (blueprint + rule set + skills). Example: the **Corporate Controllership** pack bundles BEA statistical surveys (BE-11, BE-577, BE-125, BE-185) with Census forms (ABS-1, AIES, QFR 200/201/300). The Pack is what the customer buys; the blueprint and rule set are how the Operator runs each form inside it.
