## Glossary

Alphabetical product-language definitions. Base CRR terms (Report, Entity, Form class, Source data mapping, etc.) are defined in the base [CRR Glossary](../../CRR%20Product%20Memory/02-glossary/glossary.md); only Agentic-specific language appears here.

**Action model** — The four-level bound on what the Operator may do, with confirmation graded to consequence: [Read](#read-action-level), [Recommend](#recommend-action-level), [Prepare](#prepare-action-level), [Commit](#commit-action-level). See [governance-and-action-model.md](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md).

**Activity view (Work view)** — The drill-down surface that makes multi-agent orchestration legible: the orchestrator → specialist-agent → task tree with live status, provenance, and pending approvals. Default is a summarized work rollup; the activity view is "one step away." See [multi-agent-orchestration.md](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md).

**Agent Factory** — Workiva's platform hosting the Operator's capabilities and human-confirmed actions, versioned and configured. Governed autonomy is enforced below the UI.

**Agent task** — A unit of work the Operator dispatches to a specialist agent (e.g. "chase the German affiliate's employee count"). Has its own state (`queued → running → done`, with waiting/blocked/failed). See [multi-agent-orchestration.md](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md#task-state-machine).

**Agents & Skills registry (Capability Registry)** — The surface listing every agent and skill, with its role, action-level ceiling, applicable reports, version/governance status, and on/off state. Users **configure** (enable/disable, tune within bounds); **authoring** logic routes to SDC/SME + shadow mode. See [agent-and-skill-registry.md](../11-agent-operations/agent-and-skill-registry.md).

**App shell** — The desktop application frame: a persistent, **collapsible left sidebar** (New session, Home, Agents & Skills, Artifacts, session search/pinned/all, Settings) plus a **main content area** that renders the active session or a selected global view. Modeled on the Hermes agent desktop app. See [operator-surface-and-navigation.md](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout).

**Artifact** — Any output an agent produces (readiness briefing, scope plan, mapping table, draft package, judgment ledger, evidence bundle, run report, CSV/XML/PDF). Versioned, provenance-linked, permissioned. Distinct from [evidence](#evidence-audit--permissions) (source proof). Surfaced in the **Artifacts** sidebar destination, grouped by Reports / Packages / Audits. See [artifact-library.md](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md).

**Artifact Library** — The central, searchable store of all artifacts (per-filing and portfolio-wide) — the user's quick-access surface and the Operator's externalized durable memory.

**Attribution** — The record, on every action, of *who* did it (which person or which agent), when, what changed, and why (for overrides). Shown inline and in the audit trail; the basis of the collaboration model. See [collaboration-and-presence.md](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md).

**Autonomy ceiling** — The configurable cap on how far an agent may act unattended (up to Prepare) before a human must confirm. Can be *earned* upward via track record but can never authorize a [signature commit](#signature-commits) or bypass a regulatory gate. Set in the [registry](#agents--skills-registry-capability-registry).

**Ask AI** — Read-only intelligence layer. Explains fields, forms, entities, periods, and blockers, and shows provenance. Shares the Operator's *Read*-level governed context; never creates, changes, approves, submits, or publishes.

**Change log (activity feed)** — The durable, attributed record of every material action on a filing — human and agent — chronological, each linked to its artifact/decision. The *durable* companion to the live [Activity view](#activity-view-work-view). See [collaboration-and-presence.md](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md).

**Commit (action level)** — Create a filing run, accept data, confirm a fact, mark ready, route/approve, or lock the package. Requires **permission + confirmation + audit trail**. The heaviest tier of action.

**Context budget** — The bounded working context an agent holds for a task. The product keeps it small by externalizing memory (governed facts + [artifacts](#artifact)), running math in deterministic tools, and scoping worker tasks — because an overloaded context window degrades accuracy. See [context-and-communication.md](../11-agent-operations/context-and-communication.md).

**Contributor** — See [Data / Source Owner](#data--source-owner-contributor).

**Corporate governance** — The customer's own policy gates: number of reviewers, segregation of duties, internal sign-off order. Configured in Base CRR; varies by company; **adjustable**. Contrast [Regulatory governance](#regulatory-governance).

**Data / Source Owner (Contributor)** — The seat that owns the source truth behind figures. Receives targeted, contextual requests and resolves them in place — no new workflow to learn. See [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md#data--source-owner-contributor).

**Data source** — A connected source system (ERP, consolidation, HRIS, email/Teams) or a manually-uploaded file the Operator draws on. Managed on the **Source data** surface; each is linked to the filings it feeds. See [source-discovery-and-ingestion.md](../06-features/source-discovery-and-ingestion.md).

**Deterministic evaluator** — The authority for repeatable logic (scope, ownership, reconciliation, packaging math). The independent cross-check behind scope and final approval is a deterministic evaluator the Operator **cannot lower or bypass**.

**Digest** — A periodic rollup (daily/weekly) of non-urgent findings from [scheduled agents](#scheduled-agent-standing-agent), so steady-state monitoring informs without noise. Principle: *digest, not deluge.*

**Evidence, audit & permissions** — First-class substrate elements: provenance, approval history, version history, and a complete audit trail attached to every load-bearing value and official action.

**Filing blueprint** — Defines *what the filing is*: forms, sections, fields, instructions, conditional logic, package and evidence requirements, effective dates, version, approval status. Authored by SDCs/SMEs. See [governed-substrate.md](../06-features/governed-substrate.md).

**Filing run** — An in-progress instance of the Operator carrying one report through the lifecycle. Created at *Commit* level.

**Form** — A single agency document within a [report](#report). A report bundles many forms: for BEA's BE-11 survey there is a **BE-11A** for the U.S. Reporter's consolidated domestic business plus **one form per foreign affiliate in scope** — a **BE-11B** for each majority-owned affiliate and a **BE-11C** for each minority-owned affiliate above the size test (a BE-577 report produces a form per affiliate with reportable transactions), while Country-by-Country produces a schedule per tax jurisdiction and SF-425 a form per federal award. Forms are generated once scope is confirmed; **each form has its own page** — the agency form laid out section by section (identification, ownership, employment, income, balance sheet) with values populated from accepted, sourced facts or shown as awaiting data. The report's readiness rolls up from the state of its forms. The set of forms and their fields is defined in the [filing blueprint](#filing-blueprint). See base [CRR Glossary](../../CRR%20Product%20Memory/02-glossary/glossary.md) (*Form class*).

**Governed bundle** — How a net-new filing deploys: three things shipped together — [blueprint](#filing-blueprint), [rule set](#rule-set-rule-pack), and [skills & tools](#skills--tools). Not a toggle. Only what's relevant to the customer turns on.

**Governed fact** — An accepted value with provenance, mapped to a specific filing field. Produced only at *Commit* level (e.g. accepting a returned data response). Load-bearing figures are governed facts, never invented numbers.

**Governed prompt library** — The curated set of next-best-step prompts through which the Operator proposes work; keeps the surface a control surface, not a free-form chatbot.

**Home (Dashboard)** — The sidebar's landing view: an overview of everything you, the agents, and other people are doing — active filings & readiness, agent activity, people activity, deadlines, and pending approvals. The portfolio workspace lives here. See [operator-surface-and-navigation.md](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout).

**Judgment ledger** — The reviewer's view at final approval: final scope, changes from last year, every affiliate/outcome, every threshold decision, every value with source, every warning & resolution, every override, and the final verification result. Lets the reviewer sign in minutes on evidence, not faith.

**Knowledge base** — The regulatory reference for a filing: agency instructions, definitions, guidance, filing guides, citations. What SDCs/SMEs draw on to author the blueprint and rule set, and what powers Ask AI's compliance Q&A. Distinct from [source & org intelligence](#source--org-intelligence) (customer data).

**New session** — The sidebar CTA that starts a fresh, context-bounded [session](#session-working-thread) — the clean-context entry point that protects accuracy.

**Manual upload** — The path the Operator offers when a required figure has **no connected source**: the preparer uploads a file, which the Operator maps to the field and accepts as a [governed fact](#governed-fact) with the file attached as evidence — never invented, never silently skipped. See [source-discovery-and-ingestion.md](../06-features/source-discovery-and-ingestion.md).

**Next best step** — The Operator's signature interaction: after each phase it proposes the single most useful next action (e.g. *"Want me to prepare a scope plan for review?"*), which the human accepts, edits, or declines.

**Not-yet-decidable** — An honest obligation/scope state: the Operator cannot conclude until a dependency (e.g. current-year financials) exists. Surfaced explicitly rather than guessed.

**Obligation Scout** — The net-new capability and *on-ramp into CRR*: scans rules, facts & prior filings to surface what's required, including *not-yet-decidable*. Recommends, never asserts a legal obligation. *(Wedge 1.)* See [obligation-scout.md](../06-features/obligation-scout.md).

**Obligation set** — The full set of filings the Operator detects from a single data intake (e.g. BE-11 *and* Country-by-Country), rather than one form at a time. Each obligation is recommended (not asserted) and, on confirmation, becomes its own coordinated [filing run](#filing-run) with shared facts reused across the set. See [obligation-scout.md](../06-features/obligation-scout.md#multi-obligation-intake-here-is-my-data-what-do-i-file).

**Operator (Regulatory Filing Operator)** — The Agentic CRR experience: one conversational, action-capable control surface that carries the filing lifecycle. Hides the machinery (which capability is running) but never hides the reasoning (provenance and cross-check are one step away).

**Orchestrator** — The Operator in its role of decomposing a phase into [agent tasks](#agent-task) and dispatching [specialist agents](#specialist-agent-worker-agent) (often many in parallel), then reconciling their results. The user supervises the orchestrator; it hides the machinery but never the reasoning. See [multi-agent-orchestration.md](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md).

**Override-with-record** — The rule that every override is recorded, never silent.

**Ownership graph** — The equity-ownership structure used to decide *who files* (scope). Distinct from the org operating model in [source & org intelligence](#source--org-intelligence), which decides *who to ask*.

**Pack** — The commercial unit: a SKU bundle of related forms that sets pricing and packaging (e.g. the *Corporate Controllership* pack bundling BE-11, BE-577, BE-125, BE-185 with Census forms ABS-1, AIES, QFR 200/201/300). A Pack is a bundle of reports; each report is delivered by one [governed bundle](#governed-bundle). See [report-patterns/](../05-operator-flows/report-patterns/README.md).

**Pinned session** — A [session](#session-working-thread) pinned in the sidebar for quick access — typically an active or important report.

**Prepare (action level)** — Draft a task set, mapping, filing-run setup, or review package. **Staged** — user review before any official change. No official state changes yet.

**Preparer** — The seat that owns getting the filing right and on time. Directs the Operator and resolves routed exceptions instead of executing every step. See [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer).

**Presence** — The live indication of who else is in a filing/session and what they're viewing. Viewing is passive; acting requires the right role. Part of the collaboration model. See [collaboration-and-presence.md](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md).

**Read (action level)** — Inspect state, explain a field/rule, compare periods, show provenance. **Runs freely** — no confirmation. Same governed context Ask AI uses.

**Readiness** — The visible state of how complete and trustworthy a package is (e.g. *"92% ready, 0 blocking errors, 3 warnings, 2 pending evidence items"*). Replaces "remembering whether it's done."

**Recommend (action level)** — Propose a filing, scope, mapping, routing, or next step. **Cites evidence and confidence.** No change made.

**Regulatory governance** — Gates intrinsic to the filing that the agency requires (e.g. a statutory officer certification or e-signature). Defined in the blueprint/rule set; **non-negotiable**; the Operator cannot relax or bypass. Contrast [corporate governance](#corporate-governance).

**Report** — One regulatory obligation for a period (e.g. *BE-11 · FY25*), and the top-level object a user works in **My Reports**. A report is not a single document — it **bundles the [forms](#form)** the obligation requires (for BEA, one per entity in scope). A [Pack](#pack) bundles reports; each report is delivered by one [governed bundle](#governed-bundle) and carried through the lifecycle by a [filing run](#filing-run). Users can create one from **My Reports → New report** (type, period, lead preparer, optional deadline), though most are surfaced proactively by [Obligation Scout](../06-features/obligation-scout.md). See base [CRR Glossary](../../CRR%20Product%20Memory/02-glossary/glossary.md) (*Report*).

**Report dashboard** — A read-first, per-report page (reached from **My Reports**) showing agents used & their outputs, the **forms in the report** and their status, the current phase, people involved, what's pending human confirmation, and needs-attention/blockers. A *view* over the [filing run](#filing-run), linked to but distinct from its Operator [session](#session-working-thread). See [operator-surfaces.md](../07-pages/operator-surfaces.md#the-report-dashboard).

**Reviewer-approver** — The seat holding legal sign-off (controller / responsible officer). Confirms scope and final approval on a legible ledger and clean cross-check. See [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md#reviewer-approver-controller--responsible-officer).

**Rule set (rule pack)** — The executable encoding of a filing's rules: applicability, scoping, thresholds, exemptions, routing, required & derived facts, validation, review gates, citations, test cases. Governed, versioned, testable, auditable. Each rule **cites** the knowledge-base passage it encodes. Agents never invent rules.

**Scheduled agent (standing agent)** — An agent set to run on a cadence or event trigger (deadline watch, source-freshness monitor, deferred-decision re-check, regulatory-change radar, readiness sweep). Bounded to Read/Recommend/Prepare — it queues Commit-level findings for a human and never files unsupervised. The operational form of the always-on monitoring layer. See [scheduled-agents.md](../11-agent-operations/scheduled-agents.md).

**SDC / SME** — Solution Delivery Consultant / Subject-Matter Expert. Authors, reviews, and publishes the governed substrate in the config builder. See [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md#sdc--sme).

**Session (working thread)** — The bounded working context for a stretch of related work (typically per filing) — the [app shell](#app-shell)'s core object, started via [New session](#new-session) and listed in the sidebar (searchable, [pinnable](#pinned-session), full history). Distinct from a [filing run](#filing-run) (the durable governed work object): one run may be worked across sessions. Keeping sessions scoped prevents context bleed and keeps results accurate. See [context-and-communication.md](../11-agent-operations/context-and-communication.md).

**Shadow mode** — The evaluation gate: the Operator runs an end-to-end filing without being customer-facing, so behavior is proven before release. Part of the permanent evaluation harness.

**Signature commits** — The two heaviest *Commit* actions that carry the most legal weight: **confirming scope** and **final approval**. Protected against approval fatigue by design.

**Skills & tools** — What the Operator *can do* for a given filing: discovery, mapping, collection, validation, packaging, routing. Shipped as part of the [governed bundle](#governed-bundle); SDC-configurable per report.

**Source & org intelligence** — Understanding of source systems, schemas, periods, prior filings, and entity data (what data likely exists, where it lives, what's missing), plus the org operating model (who owns/provides which data, review & reporting lines). Decides *who to ask*. Distinct from the [ownership graph](#ownership-graph).

**Specialist agent (worker agent)** — A capability instantiated as an agent the Operator dispatches to do one kind of job (scope, mapping, collection, validation, etc.). Runs at Read/Recommend/Prepare within its [autonomy ceiling](#autonomy-ceiling); every Commit escalates to a human. Many can run in parallel. See [multi-agent-orchestration.md](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md).

**The contract** — The six invariants the product runs under: no invented figures; no silent state changes; no unapproved rules; no uncited regulatory answers; no package release without final approval; every override recorded. See [governance-and-action-model.md](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md#the-contract).

title: The Governed Substrate
type: foundation
status: derived-from-brief
last_generated: 2026-07-01
source_refs:
  - Agentic CRR Product Brief - v3.docx (§6, §7 governed bundle)
related:

## Purpose

Everything the Operator does runs on a **governed substrate** — authored and managed by [SDCs/SMEs](../03-personas/personas.md#sdc--sme) in the config builder. It is the heart of why Workiva can do this credibly. The elements are defined by **role, not topic**: where two seem to touch, the relationship is a **link (citation), not a duplicate**.

## The six governed elements

### 1. Filing blueprints — *what the filing is*

Forms, sections, fields, instructions, conditional logic, package and evidence requirements, effective dates, version, approval status.

### 2. Knowledge base — *the regulatory reference*

Agency instructions, definitions, guidance, filing guides, and citations. It's what SDCs/SMEs draw on to author the blueprint and rule set, and what powers Ask AI's compliance Q&A. **Distinct from source & org intelligence** (which is about the customer's own data).

### 3. Rule sets — *how it reasons (executable)*

Applicability, scoping, thresholds, exemptions, routing, required and derived facts, validation, review gates, citations, test cases. Governed, versioned, testable, auditable. **Each rule cites the knowledge-base passage it encodes** — so where scope logic appears in both, it's source (knowledge base) and encoding (rule set) linked by citation, not duplicated. **Agents never invent rules.**

### 4. Source & org intelligence — *not just "master fields"*

An understanding of source systems, schemas, periods, prior filings, and entity data — so the product knows what data likely exists, where it lives, and what's missing. It also captures the org's operating model — who owns or provides which data per entity, plus review and reporting lines — which is what lets the Operator route reviews to the right people and chase the right owner. **Distinct from the equity-ownership graph used for scope:** one decides *who files*, the other decides *who to ask*.

### 5. Deterministic evaluators — *the authority for repeatable logic*

The independent cross-check behind scope and final approval is one the Operator **cannot lower or bypass**. Every load-bearing figure comes from a deterministic tool.

### 6. Evidence, audit & permissions — *first-class*

Provenance, approval history, version history, and a complete audit trail.

## Element roles at a glance

| Element | Defines | Linked to |
|---------|---------|-----------|
| Filing blueprint | What the filing is | Authored from knowledge base |
| Knowledge base | Regulatory reference | Cited by rule set; powers Ask AI |
| Rule set | How it reasons (executable) | Cites knowledge base |
| Source & org intelligence | Customer data + operating model (*who to ask*) | Feeds discovery, mapping, routing |
| Ownership graph | Equity structure (*who files*) | Feeds scope |
| Deterministic evaluators | Repeatable logic + cross-check | Underwrites signature commits |
| Evidence / audit / permissions | Provenance & accountability | Attached to every value & action |

## New filings deploy as a governed bundle

Each net-new obligation ships **three things together** — not a toggle:

1. **Blueprint** — the filing's structure.
2. **Rule set** — how it reasons (applicability, thresholds, exemptions, routing, required facts, validations, citations, test cases).
3. **Skills & tools** — what the Operator can do: discovery, mapping, collection, validation, packaging, routing.

Only what's relevant to that customer turns on — focused, lower-risk, explainable. This is how **one Pack spans many forms on a single experience**.

## Supply & evaluation model

- **Agents draft, SDC/SME review and publish.** Only published, governed artifacts run.
- **Shadow mode gating** — behavior is proven end-to-end before it becomes customer-facing.
- **Evaluation is a permanent capability**, not a one-time test.

## The guardrail this enforces

> Agentic CRR can only automate what Base CRR can represent.

The Operator depends on continued investment in the Base CRR data model, workflow state, tasking, evidence, permissions, and package readiness.

## Related

- Governance & action model: [governance-and-action-model.md](./governance-and-action-model.md)
- Object model: [object-model.md](../04-information-architecture/object-model.md)
- Authoring seat: [SDC / SME](../03-personas/personas.md#sdc--sme)

## Purpose

Find the right sources, schemas, and periods, and pull in-scope figures — so preparation starts from real data, not a blank form.

## Base vs Agentic

| 🟢 Base foundation | 🚀 Agentic upgrade |
|--------------------|--------------------|
| Data store & connectors | Finds the right sources, schemas & periods; pulls in-scope figures |

## Capabilities

- Identify likely source systems (ERP, consolidation tools) and prior mappings.
- Confirm source **periods** relevant to the filing (e.g. FY25).
- Pull in-scope figures for scoped entities/fields.
- Report coverage honestly (e.g. *"likely sources for 84% of required values"*).
- **Request a manual upload** when a required figure has *no* connected source — rather than silently guessing or omitting it.

## Source data management (the Source data surface)

Connected sources and manually-uploaded files are managed in one place — the **Source data** destination in the [app shell](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md). It lists each source's type, freshness, and which filings it feeds. This is also where the agent's **upload requests** land.

## Manual upload — when no source exists

Some figures genuinely have no system of record — a one-off classification, a subsidiary's local schedule, a value that lives only in a spreadsheet or a person's head. When the Operator hits such a gap it does not invent or quietly skip it; in the [Map & ingest](../05-operator-flows/map-and-ingest.md) phase it explicitly says *"this figure has no connected source"* and offers two governed paths:

1. **Upload it yourself** — the preparer drops the file; the Operator maps it to the field, **accepts it as a [governed fact](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-fact) with the file attached as evidence**, and registers it under Source data.
2. **Request it from an owner** — hand off to [Data Collection & Chase](./data-collection-and-chase.md) as a tracked request.

Either way the value ends up sourced and auditable — never invented. This is the design realization of [I12 — unstructured / human-only source capture](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i12--unstructured--human-only-source-capture).

## Behaviors & rules

- Uses **source & org intelligence** to know what data likely exists and where it lives.
- **No invented figures** — pulled values trace to a source; gaps become an upload or a request.
- A **manually uploaded** value is a governed fact like any other: it carries provenance (the file), a confidence, and an audit entry, and is subject to the same validation.
- Flags source periods that need confirmation rather than assuming.

## Action level

- Recommend · Prepare

## Dependencies

- [Governed substrate](./governed-substrate.md) — source & org intelligence
- [Mapping & Resolve](./mapping-and-resolve.md) — maps pulled figures to requirements

## Related

- Flow: [Map & ingest](../05-operator-flows/map-and-ingest.md)

## Purpose

The governance spine and risk posture: **four action levels graded to consequence**, **two signature commits**, a clear split between **regulatory** and **corporate** governance, and the **contract** the whole product runs under.

## The four-level action model

The Operator is bounded by a four-level action model, with confirmation graded to consequence — so the heaviest moments are a *tier of action*, not the only checkpoints.

| Level | What it covers | Confirmation |
|-------|----------------|--------------|
| **Read** | Inspect state, explain a field/rule, compare periods, show provenance | None — runs freely |
| **Recommend** | Propose a filing, scope, mapping, routing, or next step | Cites evidence and confidence |
| **Prepare** | Draft a task set, mapping, filing-run setup, or review package | Staged — user review before any official change |
| **Commit** | Create a filing run, accept data, confirm a fact, mark ready, route/approve, lock the package | Permission + confirmation + audit trail |

## The two signature commits

**Confirming scope** and **giving final approval** carry the most legal weight, but live inside the same model as every other commit.

- **Confirm scope** — the most expensive mistakes are cheapest to catch here; present the plan beside its deterministic cross-check.
- **Final approval** — usually a regulatory, legally binding certification; the reviewer signs from a complete judgment ledger.

**Designing against approval fatigue is a first-class goal.** The Operator confirms only where judgment, accountability, or official state matters. See [design-patterns.md](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md).

## Two kinds of governance, kept separate

Not every gate is the same kind of requirement. The Operator **tags each gate by type**:

| Type | What it is | Set where | Negotiable? |
|------|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| **Regulatory governance** | Intrinsic to the filing — e.g. a statutory officer certification or e-signature the agency requires | Defined in the blueprint & rule set | **No** — the Operator cannot relax or bypass |
| **Corporate governance** | The customer's own policy — number of reviewers, segregation of duties, internal sign-off order | Configured in Base CRR | **Yes** — varies by company |

This sharpens the two signature commits: **final certification is usually regulatory** (legally binding), while the **number of internal reviewers is corporate** (configurable). Tagging each gate by type determines what's mandatory vs adjustable, and how the audit trail weights it.

## The contract

The invariants the product runs under:

1. **No invented figures** — every load-bearing number comes from a deterministic tool.
2. **No silent state changes** — official changes are permissioned and audited.
3. **No unapproved rules** — only published, governed rule packs run.
4. **No uncited regulatory answers.**
5. **No package release without final approval.**
6. **Every override is recorded** — never silent.

## The action model applies to every agent, not just the Operator

When the Operator [spins off specialist agents](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md) or runs [scheduled agents](../11-agent-operations/scheduled-agents.md), each one inherits this model — and the constraint is *strongest* for parallel and unattended work, where silent consequential action is most tempting.

- **Every agent has an [autonomy ceiling](../02-glossary/glossary.md#autonomy-ceiling)** (set in the [registry](../11-agent-operations/agent-and-skill-registry.md)) capping how far it acts unattended — at most *Prepare*.
- **Every Commit escalates to a human.** No sub-agent or scheduled agent commits, sends, accepts, or locks on its own.
- **No agent can cross a signature commit** (confirm scope, final approval) or a **regulatory gate** — those are structural, not configurable, and cannot be reached by any ceiling.
- **Ceilings can be earned upward** by track record ([earned autonomy](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy)) but never past the two limits above, and never past the customer's configured maximum.
- **Enabling/disabling an agent is a governed act** — permissioned and audited (see [P18](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p18--configuration-vs-authoring)) — because it changes what the system will do to a penalty-bearing filing.
- **Every unattended run is audited** and writes a run-report [artifact](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md), even when nothing was surfaced.

This is how "the Operator never files unsupervised" holds even when dozens of agents run in parallel or overnight. See [P17](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p17--sub-agents--scheduled-agents-inherit-the-action-model).

**Multi-user, too.** When several people share a filing, *Commit* is permissioned **per human role** as well: viewing never implies acting, the two signature commits are reserved to the Reviewer-approver, and **every action — human or agent — is attributed** in the audit trail. See [collaboration-and-presence.md](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md).

## Enforcement below the UI

Governed autonomy is enforced *below the UI*: every load-bearing figure comes from a deterministic tool, and scope and final approval are backed by an independent verification the Operator cannot bypass. **Evaluation is a product capability** — a permanent harness and [shadow mode](../02-glossary/glossary.md#shadow-mode) gate anything before it becomes customer-facing.

## Related

- Lifecycle × action levels: [lifecycle-and-action-model.md](../04-information-architecture/lifecycle-and-action-model.md)
- Substrate: [governed-substrate.md](./governed-substrate.md)
- Agents bounded by this model: [Agent operations & workspace](../11-agent-operations/README.md)
- Design patterns: [design-patterns.md](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md)

## Purpose

Proactively surface **what's required** — including the honest *not-yet-decidable* — by scanning rules, facts, and prior filings. Obligation Scout is a **net-new capability** and the **on-ramp into CRR** (wedge 1).

## Base vs Agentic

| 🟢 Base foundation | 🚀 Agentic upgrade |
|--------------------|--------------------|
| — not in Base CRR (roadmap candidate) | Scans rules, facts & prior filings to surface what's required, including *not yet decidable* |

## Capabilities

- Read signals Workiva already holds — e.g. a 10-K's subsidiary disclosures point to foreign affiliates and a possible BE-11.
- Nudge toward a likely obligation with cited evidence: *"Based on your subsidiary disclosures, you may have a BE-11 requirement — we can help assess and manage it."*
- Land the upgrade **pre-scoped** — affiliate list, prior context, blueprint, and required facts already prepared. No blank page.
- For CRR customers, act as the **portfolio front door**: what might we owe, what's due, what's missing, what to act on.

## Multi-obligation intake: here is my data, what do I file?

**The product does not work one form at a time.** A user can start from data, not from a form: *"Here's our group data — figure out what we need to file."* The Operator reasons over that data and surfaces the **full [obligation set](../02-glossary/glossary.md#obligation-set)** — every applicable filing — rather than assuming a single form.

**Worked example.** The same subsidiary + financial data can surface **more than one** obligation at once:

> *"From your subsidiary and financial data I see two likely obligations: **BE-11** (BEA direct-investment survey) and **Country-by-Country (Form 8975)** — your group appears above the €750M consolidated-revenue threshold. 1 more is not-yet-decidable pending final consolidation. Want me to prepare scope plans for both?"*

How it works:

1. **Detect the set** — scan the data against every governed [rule set](../02-glossary/glossary.md#rule-set-rule-pack) the customer has, not just one; classify each obligation as required / confirm / not-yet-decidable.
2. **Recommend, never assert** — each detected obligation cites its evidence and threshold; the human confirms which to pursue.
3. **Spin up coordinated filings** — on confirmation, the Operator creates **one [filing run](../02-glossary/glossary.md#filing-run) per obligation** and coordinates them in one place ([Home](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout)).
4. **Reuse facts across the set** — a value accepted once (revenue, headcount, tax paid) becomes a [governed fact](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-fact) that feeds *every* filing needing it, with shared provenance — **collect once, use across the obligation set** ([I1](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i1--compounding-facts-across-the-portfolio)).

This is the natural extension of "one pattern, many reports": the *shape* is reusable, and the *intake* now discovers the whole set. See [Country-by-Country report pattern](../05-operator-flows/report-patterns/country-by-country.md) and [P20](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p20--start-from-the-data-not-the-form).

## Behaviors & rules (two boundaries)

- **Recommends, never asserts** a legal obligation — cites the evidence, names what's uncertain, routes into a governed workflow.
- **Honest about uncertainty** — surfaces *not-yet-decidable* rather than guessing.

## Action level

- Read · Recommend — runs freely and cites evidence; never commits.

## Two audiences

- **Non-CRR customers** — the way in.
- **CRR customers** — the portfolio front door across all filings.

## Open question (sizing)

How many of Workiva's ~7,000 customers carry obligation signals in data they already hold (e.g. foreign subsidiaries in a 10-K's Exhibit 21)? That is the addressable base for the on-ramp. *[sizing TBD]*

## Related

- Flow: [Front door (Obligation)](../05-operator-flows/front-door-obligation.md)
- Governance: [Governance & action model](./governance-and-action-model.md)

---
title: Agentic CRR Personas
type: personas
status: synthesized-from-brief
last_generated: 2026-07-01
source_refs:
  - Agentic CRR Product Brief - v3.docx (§4)
  - solution_enablement/documentation/agentic-crr-jtbd-map.md (persona legend)
related:
  - ../01-product-overview/overview.md
  - ../08-customer-journey/customer-journey-map.md
  - ../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md
---

## Personas

The people in the flow split into two groups: **two seats govern the filing itself**, and **two more supply what it runs on**. The Operator carries the lifecycle between them. Under Agentic CRR the defining change for every seat is the same — *the human becomes a governor, not an operator-of-steps.*

> These four seats are the canonical **filing** personas — the people in a filing. They consolidate and rename the base CRR / JTBD personas (Workspace Admin, Report Owner, Assignee, Reviewer). A fifth, **operational** seat — [Workspace Admin (Agentic)](#workspace-admin-agentic--capability-owner) — is added by the [agent-operations layer](../11-agent-operations/README.md) to configure and monitor the agent workforce; it sits outside the filing flow. Mapping is given per persona and summarized at the end.

---

### Preparer

- **Group** — Governs the filing.
- **Owns** — Getting the filing right and on time.
- **What changes** — Directs the Operator and resolves the exceptions it routes, instead of executing every step.
- **Jobs to be done**
  - When a period opens, I want to know what we must file and start from a prepared plan, so that I never face a blank page.
  - When data is missing, I want the Operator to chase it for me, so that I stop coordinating people by hand.
  - When something changes mid-filing, I want to be told and offered the delta to approve, so that scope never goes stale silently.
- **Primary action levels** — Directs across [Read → Prepare](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md); confirms at *Commit* for filing-run creation and sending requests.
- **Base/JTBD mapping** — Report Owner (base CRR) · Compliance Manager (planning alias).
- **Serves them** — [Front door](../05-operator-flows/front-door-obligation.md), [Scope & confirmation](../05-operator-flows/scope-and-confirmation.md), [Map & ingest](../05-operator-flows/map-and-ingest.md), [Collect & chase](../05-operator-flows/collect-and-chase.md), [Validate](../05-operator-flows/validate.md), [Prepare & assemble](../05-operator-flows/prepare-and-assemble.md)

---

### Reviewer-approver (Controller / Responsible Officer)

- **Group** — Governs the filing.
- **Owns** — The legal sign-off.
- **What changes** — Confirms scope and final approval on a **legible ledger and a clean cross-check** — confidence, not faith. Enters only where accountability actually changes.
- **Jobs to be done**
  - When scope is proposed, I want to see what changed, the exceptions resolved, and an independent cross-check, so that I can confirm scope in minutes.
  - When the filing is ready, I want a judgment ledger — every decision, value, source, warning, and override — so that I approve on evidence or refuse with the exact divergence named.
- **Primary action levels** — The two [signature commits](../02-glossary/glossary.md#signature-commits): confirm scope and final approval (both *Commit*).
- **Governance note** — Final certification is usually **regulatory** governance (legally binding); the number of internal reviewers is **corporate** governance (configurable). See [governance-and-action-model.md](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md).
- **Base/JTBD mapping** — Reviewer (base CRR, emerging — `pending_review` only, no shipped UI). Agentic CRR makes this seat first-class.
- **Serves them** — [Scope & confirmation](../05-operator-flows/scope-and-confirmation.md), [Review & approval](../05-operator-flows/review-and-approval.md)

---

### SDC / SME

- **Group** — Supplies what the Operator runs on (build-time).
- **Owns** — Domain expertise for customer implementation patterns and configured artifacts.
- **What changes** — Configures, reviews, and publishes the governed substrate; additional regulatory/legal review applies where interpretation risk warrants.
- **Jobs to be done**
  - When a new filing is needed, I want to author its blueprint, rule set, and skills as a governed bundle, so that the Operator can run it without inventing rules.
  - When rules change, I want to version and test the rule pack in shadow mode, so that only published, governed rules ever run.
- **Primary action levels** — Authoring happens in the config builder, *outside* the Operator's runtime action model; the Operator only ever executes **published** artifacts.
- **Base/JTBD mapping** — Adjacent to Workspace Admin (base CRR) but distinct: the SDC/SME authors the *governed substrate*, not just workspace settings. See [governed-substrate.md](../06-features/governed-substrate.md).
- **Serves them** — [Governed substrate](../06-features/governed-substrate.md), [report patterns](../05-operator-flows/report-patterns/README.md)

---

### Data / Source Owner (Contributor)

- **Group** — Supplies what the Operator runs on (run-time).
- **Owns** — The source truth behind the figures.
- **What changes** — **Stops being chased by email.** Receives targeted, contextual requests tied to a specific field/affiliate/due date and resolves them in place — often just by replying on their existing channel.
- **Jobs to be done**
  - When the Operator needs a value only I hold, I want a specific request with context, so that I can answer without learning a new workflow.
  - When I answer, I want my value used as-is with evidence attached, so that the data stays mine and traceable.
- **Primary action levels** — Interacts with *Prepare*/*Commit* outputs (a request the Operator drafted and the Preparer sent); their reply becomes a [governed fact](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-fact) only when accepted.
- **Base/JTBD mapping** — Data Provider / Assignee (base CRR).
- **Serves them** — [Collect & chase](../05-operator-flows/collect-and-chase.md), [Data Collection & Chase capability](../06-features/data-collection-and-chase.md)

---

### Workspace Admin (Agentic — capability owner)

- **Group** — Supplies what the Operator runs on (configures the runtime environment). Often the same person as a senior Preparer in smaller orgs.
- **Owns** — Which governed capabilities are turned on, how far they may act, and what runs on a schedule — the [Agents & Skills registry](../11-agent-operations/agent-and-skill-registry.md) and workspace-wide [schedules](../11-agent-operations/scheduled-agents.md).
- **What changes** — Moves from managing workspace settings to **governing an agent workforce**: enabling/disabling agents, setting [autonomy ceilings](../02-glossary/glossary.md#autonomy-ceiling), tuning thresholds within governed bounds, and configuring how scheduled agents report back.
- **Jobs to be done**
  - When we adopt a new report, I want to turn on only the relevant agents and skills, so that the surface stays focused and lower-risk.
  - As trust builds, I want to raise an agent's autonomy ceiling within a safe maximum, so that routine work needs fewer confirmations without risking a signature commit.
  - When I want proactive monitoring, I want to schedule agents and set their reporting cadence, so that the team is informed without noise.
- **Boundary vs SDC/SME** — The admin **configures** (enable/disable, ceilings, thresholds — audited); the [SDC/SME](#sdc--sme) **authors** the logic (rule sets, blueprints, skills — governed + shadow-gated). Editing logic routes from the registry into the authoring flow. See [P18](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p18--configuration-vs-authoring).
- **Primary action levels** — Configuration changes are governed, permissioned, audited acts — not runtime *Commits* on a filing.
- **Base/JTBD mapping** — Workspace Administrator (base CRR), extended with agent-workforce management.
- **Serves them** — [Agents & Skills registry](../11-agent-operations/agent-and-skill-registry.md), [Scheduled agents](../11-agent-operations/scheduled-agents.md), [Artifact Library](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md)

---

## Persona × mapping summary

| Agentic CRR seat | Group | Base CRR / JTBD persona | Signature moment |
|------------------|-------|-------------------------|------------------|
| **Preparer** | Governs | Report Owner / Compliance Manager | Directs the Operator; commits filing-run & sends |
| **Reviewer-approver** | Governs | Reviewer (emerging) | Confirm scope · final approval |
| **SDC / SME** | Supplies (build) | Workspace Admin (adjacent) | Publishes governed bundle |
| **Workspace Admin (Agentic)** | Supplies (configure) | Workspace Administrator | Enables/tunes agents & schedules |
| **Data / Source Owner** | Supplies (run) | Data Provider / Assignee | Answers targeted requests |

## Collaboration & visibility

Filings are **multi-user** — several of these seats (and many agents) work one filing at once. Two clarifications the seats don't capture on their own:

- **Viewing vs acting.** Beyond the seats, access has a **role tier**: *Viewer* (read only), *Commenter* (read + comment), and the acting seats above. Presence shows who's viewing; only the right role can change state, and the two signature commits stay with the Reviewer-approver.
- **Everyone sees the same live progress, within permissions.** Data owners see their scope; the whole team sees agent activity on Home; every change is attributed to a person or an agent.

Full model: [collaboration-and-presence.md](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md). This resolves [G10](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g10--no-collaboration--concurrency-model).

## The Operator as an actor

Though not a persona, the **Operator** is the fifth actor in every diagram — it carries the work between the seats. Its authority is bounded by the [action model](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md) and it never files unsupervised. Where the base JTBD map assigned one agent per lifecycle stage (Config, Scoping, Population, Collection, Validation, Submission, Lifecycle), Agentic CRR unifies them into a single Operator experience with those capabilities beneath it — the Operator acts as an **orchestrator**, spinning off [specialist agents](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md) (often many in parallel), each bounded by its autonomy ceiling. The user supervises the orchestrator, not the individual agents.

## Confidence & gaps

- **High confidence (from brief):** Preparer, Reviewer-approver, Data/Source Owner, SDC/SME as the four seats.
- **Validate with PMs:** Exact naming and whether Preparer vs Reviewer-approver can be the same person in small orgs.
- **Corporate vs regulatory governance** determines how many reviewer seats exist per filing — configurable per customer.
- **Gap:** RBAC for these seats is not yet built in Base CRR (`authorizationService` returns view for all today).

title: F4 — Scheduled Agents
type: feature

## Purpose

Let the user **set agents to run on a cadence (or on an event)** — the operational form of the "always-on" monitoring the base JTBD map called the *Lifecycle Agent* — and define **how they report back** without creating noise. This directly resolves the [always-on monitoring gap (G7)](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g7--loss-of-the-always-on-monitoring-dimension), the [deferred-decision trigger (G6)](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g6--the-not-yet-decidable-loop-has-no-trigger), and [regulatory-change management (G11)](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g11--regulatory-change-management-mid-cycle).

## What you can schedule

Scheduled agents are the steady-state, between-cycles half of the Operator:

| Scheduled agent | Cadence | What it does |
|-----------------|---------|--------------|
| **Deadline watch** | Daily/weekly | Track filing deadlines across the portfolio; escalate as they approach |
| **Source-freshness monitor** | On event / daily | Detect new or stale source data; flag filings needing a refresh |
| **Deferred-decision re-check** | On event / daily | Watch each *not-yet-decidable* item's dependency; re-surface when resolvable ([G6](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g6--the-not-yet-decidable-loop-has-no-trigger)) |
| **Obligation Scout re-scan** | Weekly/monthly | Re-scan signals for new/changed obligations across the portfolio |
| **Regulatory-change radar** | Daily/weekly | Watch for agency rule/form/threshold changes; open a rule-pack delta for SDC review ([I6](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i6--regulatory-change-radar)) |
| **Readiness sweep** | Daily | Re-check active filings' readiness; flag new blockers/warnings |
| **Chase follow-up** | Per-request schedule | Reminders/escalations on outstanding requests |

## Setting one up

| Setting | Options |
|---------|---------|
| **Agent** | Any enabled agent from the [registry](./agent-and-skill-registry.md) that supports scheduling |
| **Trigger** | Time-based (cron-like: daily, weekly, monthly, custom) **and/or** event-based (new source data, dependency resolved, deadline within N days) |
| **Scope** | Which filings / reports / entities / period |
| **Action ceiling** | Capped at **Read / Recommend / Prepare** — see governance below |
| **Reporting** | Channel(s), digest vs immediate, severity threshold, recipients |
| **Quiet hours / limits** | Suppress non-urgent notifications; rate-limit to prevent noise |

Event-based triggers matter as much as time-based ones — "when Brazil's FY25 financials load" is more useful than "every Monday."

## The governance rule that makes this safe

**A scheduled agent may observe, recommend, and prepare — it may never Commit unsupervised, and never crosses a signature commit.** The Operator never files unsupervised; that principle is *strongest* for unattended, scheduled work.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Cron[Schedule / event fires] --> Run[Scheduled agent runs]
  Run --> Findings{Findings?}
  Findings -->|nothing material| Quiet[Log run quietly - artifact only]
  Findings -->|needs attention| Report[Report back to user]
  Report --> NBS[Surface as next-best-step]
  NBS --> Human[Human decides / Commits]
  Run -.every run.-> Audit[Audited + artifact in library]
```

- Anything requiring a *Commit* is **queued as a pending approval / next-best-step** for a human — never auto-executed.
- Every scheduled run is **audited** and writes a **run report artifact** to the [Artifact Library](./artifact-library.md).
- Ceilings and enablement come from the [registry](./agent-and-skill-registry.md); workspace-wide schedules are a Workspace Admin function.

## How they report back

Reporting is designed **against noise** ([P7](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine), [P16](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p16--progress-transparency)):

| Channel | Use |
|---------|-----|
| **Portfolio inbox / findings tray** | The default: findings land as prioritized next-best-steps in the portfolio workspace |
| **Digest** | Daily/weekly rollup of non-urgent findings ("here's what changed since Monday") — *digest, not deluge* |
| **Immediate notification** | Push (in-app / email / Teams) only for material or time-critical findings above the user's threshold |
| **Escalation** | Deadline-critical or overdue items escalate to the owner (and optionally their manager) |
| **Run report artifact** | Every run's full detail is retrievable in the Artifact Library, even when nothing was surfaced |
| **Quiet log** | A run that finds nothing logs quietly — visible if you look, silent if you don't |

**Principle: quiet by default, loud when it matters.** A scheduled agent that pings daily with "nothing to report" trains users to ignore it. It should surface only what needs a human, roll the rest into a digest, and always leave a retrievable trail.

## Managing schedules — the Schedules (Monitoring) sidebar destination

Scheduled agents get a **top-level home in the left sidebar: "⏱ Schedules"** ([app shell](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout)) — reflecting that proactive monitoring is a first-class activity, not a buried setting. This surface is the **monitoring hub**:

- Lists all scheduled/standing agents: what, cadence/trigger, scope, last run, next run, last findings, on/off.
- Shows the **findings history and digests** they produce.
- Users can create, pause, edit, or delete schedules; every change is **audited**.
- Schedules respect the same **confidentiality and permissions** as everything else.

Autonomy ceilings and enablement still come from the [registry](./agent-and-skill-registry.md); Schedules is where they're put on a cadence and monitored.

## Related

## Purpose

Give the user **one place to see every available agent and skill**, understand what each does, and **turn them on/off, configure them, and route deeper edits to governance** — without letting configuration become a backdoor around the contract ("no unapproved rules").

> **Where it lives.** The registry is reached from **Settings → Agents & Skills** ([app shell](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout)) — grouped with the workspace's other configuration and administration surfaces, since enabling/tuning the agent workforce is a governed configuration act.

## The core distinction: Configure vs Author

This is the pivotal governance decision for this feature.

| | **Configure** | **Author / edit logic** |
|---|---------------|-------------------------|
| **What** | Enable/disable, set autonomy ceiling, adjust thresholds *within governed bounds*, scope to reports/entities | Change the actual rule set, blueprint, skill definition, or prompts |
| **Who** | Workspace Admin / permitted Preparer | [SDC / SME](../03-personas/personas.md#sdc--sme) |
| **Where** | In the registry, directly | Routed from the registry into the **governed authoring flow** (config builder) |
| **Governance** | An **audited configuration change** | Versioned + **shadow-mode gated** + published; agents draft, humans publish |

So "edit" in the registry means: *safe, bounded configuration inline* — and *"propose/author a logic change"* which hands off to the governed pipeline. **Nothing unpublished ever runs.** This keeps the registry powerful without violating [the contract](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md#the-contract).

## What the registry shows

### Agents

Each specialist agent (and the Operator itself) as a catalog entry:

| Field | Example |
|-------|---------|
| **Name & role** | Collection & Chase agent — turns gaps into tracked, chased requests |
| **Capability** | Maps to a [capability doc](../06-features/README.md) |
| **Action-level ceiling** | e.g. *Prepare* (drafts & sends on approval; never Commits unsupervised) |
| **Applies to** | Which reports/Packs/entities it's enabled for |
| **Version + governance status** | `v4 · published` / `v5 · in shadow` |
| **Enabled state** | On / off (per workspace or per report) |
| **Configuration** | Autonomy ceiling, thresholds, channels, deadlines |
| **Track record** | Accepted vs overridden, accuracy — links to the [trust dashboard](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i9--operator-trust-dashboard) |
| **Skills/tools used** | The tools this agent can call |

### Skills & tools

Each skill/tool an agent can use:

| Field | Example |
|-------|---------|
| **Name & function** | "Send tracked request via email/Teams" |
| **Used by** | Which agents |
| **Inputs / outputs** | Field, owner, deadline → tracked request |
| **Permissions / scopes required** | e.g. `connected-process`, outbound email |
| **Governance status + version** | published / shadow |
| **Enabled state** | On / off |

## What the user can do

- **Browse & search** all agents and skills; see what's on, off, or in shadow.
- **View detail** — role, ceiling, applicable reports, version history, track record.
- **Toggle on/off** — per workspace or per report. Disabling an agent removes that capability from the Operator's repertoire (respecting "only automate what Base CRR can represent"). Every toggle is **audited**.
- **Configure within bounds** — set the **autonomy ceiling** (how far it may act before confirming), thresholds (confidence routing — [G4](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g4--no-defined-confidence-model)), channels, and deadlines.
- **Propose / author a logic change** — routes to SDC/SME + shadow mode; the user can track its status (`in shadow`, `published`).
- **See track record** — decide whether to raise or lower an agent's autonomy ([I2](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy)).

## Autonomy ceiling (the key control)

Per agent, the ceiling caps how far it may go unattended:

```text
Read ──▶ Recommend ──▶ Prepare ──▶ [Commit escalates to human, always]
                    ▲
              autonomy ceiling (configurable, earnable)
```

- Default ceilings are conservative; they can be **earned upward** as track record proves out ([I2](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy)) — always within a customer-set maximum.
- **No ceiling can authorize a signature commit** or override a regulatory gate — those are structural, not configurable ([governance](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md#two-kinds-of-governance-kept-separate)).

## Why "on/off" is a governed act, not a preference

Turning a governed capability on or off changes what the system will do to a penalty-bearing filing. So toggles are:

- **Permissioned** (Workspace Admin / permitted seat),
- **Audited** (who, when, why),
- **Scoped** (workspace vs report),
- and **reversible with record**.

## Relationship to the governed bundle

The registry is the **runtime, customer-facing view** of the [governed substrate](../06-features/governed-substrate.md): a published [governed bundle](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-bundle) (blueprint + rule set + skills) is what *populates* the registry for a given report. The registry lets customers **turn on and tune** what SDCs/SMEs have authored — "only what's relevant to that customer turns on."

## Related

- What the agents do: [capability model](../06-features/README.md)
- Where edits go: [governed substrate](../06-features/governed-substrate.md), [SDC/SME](../03-personas/personas.md#sdc--sme)
- Scheduling enabled agents: [Scheduled agents](./scheduled-agents.md)
- Patterns: [P18 Configuration vs authoring](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p18--configuration-vs-authoring)
- Realizes: [I2 earned autonomy](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy), supports [I8 authoring](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i8--assisted-self-service-substrate-authoring)

## Purpose

Define how the Operator **spins off specialist agents** to do different jobs in parallel, and how the user **observes, steers, and approves** that work — without being turned into an air-traffic controller.

## The model: one Operator, many specialists

The **Operator is the orchestrator** (the conductor). Beneath it, each capability in the [capability model](../06-features/README.md) can run as a **specialist agent** (a "worker"): Obligation Scout, Scope & Entity, Source Discovery, Mapping & Resolve, Collection & Chase, Filing Preparation, Validation & Readiness, Review routing, Packaging. The Operator decomposes a phase into **agent tasks** and dispatches workers — sometimes one, often many in parallel.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  User[User] <--> Operator[Operator - orchestrator]
  Operator --> W1[Scope agent]
  Operator --> W2[Collection agent]
  Operator --> W3[Mapping agent]
  W2 --> T1[Task: chase Germany affiliate]
  W2 --> T2[Task: chase Brazil affiliate]
  W2 --> T3[Task: chase 6 more owners]
  W1 --> T4[Task: evaluate 42 affiliates]
  subgraph escalate [Escalations to human]
    G1[Commit: send requests?]
    G2[Confirm scope?]
  end
  W1 -.escalates.-> G2
  W2 -.escalates.-> G1
  G1 --> User
  G2 --> User
```

**Fan-out is the norm, not the exception.** A BE-11 with 42 affiliates means the scope agent evaluates 42 in parallel and the collection agent may chase a dozen owners at once. Fan-out is how the product delivers speed; legibility is how it stays trustworthy.

## Design tension resolved: "hide the machinery, never the reasoning"

The brief says the Operator *hides which capability is running*. Multi-agent orchestration must not break that. Resolution:

- **Default view is summarized** — *"Chasing 12 inputs across 8 owners · 3 need your input."* The user does not have to know it is "the Collection agent running 12 tasks."
- **The reasoning is always one step away** — an **Activity view** lets the user expand the summary into the live work tree, drill into any agent/task, and see its provenance and cross-check.
- The user chooses their altitude: **glance** (summary) or **inspect** (activity view). Neither requires manual orchestration.

See [P13 Legible orchestration](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p13--legible-orchestration).

## The Activity view (a.k.a. Work view)

The surface where orchestration becomes legible and interruptible. It is *not* the primary surface — it's the "one step away" drill-down.

| Element | What it shows |
|---------|---------------|
| **Work summary** | Plain-language rollup of what's happening now and what needs the user (the default the user sees) |
| **Agent/task tree** | Orchestrator → specialist agents → tasks, each with status |
| **Per-task status** | `queued`, `running`, `waiting on human`, `waiting on owner`, `blocked`, `done`, `failed` |
| **Per-task detail** | What the agent is doing, inputs it used (provenance), confidence, the artifact it will/did produce |
| **Pending approvals** | Commit-level actions the workers have escalated, grouped for batch handling |
| **Timeline / log** | An auditable record of dispatches, escalations, and completions |

### Task state machine

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> queued
  queued --> running: dispatched
  running --> waiting_human: needs Commit / decision
  running --> waiting_owner: sent a request
  running --> blocked: missing dependency
  waiting_human --> running: user responds
  waiting_owner --> running: reply received
  blocked --> running: dependency resolved
  running --> done
  running --> failed: error
  failed --> queued: retry
  done --> [*]
```

## How the user interacts

Five verbs — all supervision, never operation ([P11](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p11--governor-not-operator)):

1. **Observe** — glance at the summary; expand into the activity view when curious or concerned.
2. **Steer** — redirect a worker mid-flight: narrow/broaden scope ("skip these 5 affiliates"), reprioritize, or change a deadline. Steering a *Prepare*-level worker is itself a *Prepare* action (no official change).
3. **Answer** — a worker that hits a decision (ambiguous mapping, missing owner) escalates a question; the user answers inline and the worker resumes.
4. **Approve** — Commit-level actions surface here as pending approvals, **grouped to fight approval fatigue** (see below).
5. **Pause / stop** — pause the whole run or cancel a single worker; state is preserved (ties to [graceful degradation](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i11--graceful-degradation-to-manual)).

### Batch approvals (approval-fatigue design)

Fan-out creates many small Commit moments. Instead of 12 separate confirmations, the Operator groups them:

> **8 requests ready to send** to 8 owners · [Review all] [Send all] [Review each]
> 2 need owner confirmation first · 2 are overdue → [Send reminders]

This honors [P3 graded confirmation](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p3--graded-confirmation): routine, homogeneous commits get a single grouped confirmation; a signature commit never gets batched away.

## Governance & guardrails

Every specialist agent inherits the [action model](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md):

- Workers run freely at **Read/Recommend/Prepare**; every **Commit escalates** to a human.
- No worker can cross a **signature commit** (confirm scope, final approval) — those always go to the Reviewer-approver.
- **No invented figures / no silent state changes** apply per worker; each task's output carries provenance and (where relevant) a deterministic cross-check.
- A worker's **autonomy ceiling** is set in the [registry](./agent-and-skill-registry.md) (and can be earned upward — [I2](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy)).

## Concurrency & conflict handling

- Workers operate on **scoped slices** (per entity/section/field) so parallel work doesn't collide.
- The orchestrator **reconciles** results (e.g. a mapping agent and a validation agent touching the same field) and surfaces genuine conflicts rather than silently picking one ([P5](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p5--reasoning-one-step-away)).
- Bounded scope per worker is also what keeps each agent's **context small and accurate** — see [context-and-communication.md](./context-and-communication.md).

## Failure handling

- A failed task is visible (`failed`), retryable, and never silently dropped.
- If a worker can't proceed safely (no source, confidence below floor), it **hands the slice back to the human** rather than guessing — clean degradation, state preserved.

## Artifacts produced

Every meaningful worker output is written to the [Artifact Library](./artifact-library.md) (scope plan, mapping table, drafted requests, validation report, etc.), so orchestration leaves a durable, retrievable trail rather than living only in the conversation.

## Related

- Where outputs land: [Artifact Library](./artifact-library.md)
- Turning agents on/off & setting ceilings: [Agents & Skills registry](./agent-and-skill-registry.md)
- Keeping it legible & accurate: [Context & communication](./context-and-communication.md)
- Patterns: [P13](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p13--legible-orchestration), [P16](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p16--progress-transparency), [P17](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p17--sub-agents--scheduled-agents-inherit-the-action-model)

## What this section is

The **operating environment around the Operator** — the surfaces and mechanics that let a single Operator experience run many agents safely, keep their outputs at your fingertips, let you manage and schedule them, and stay legible and accurate as the work scales.

> **Provenance note.** These features **extend** the product brief, which is silent on them. They are designed to be faithful to the brief's governance spine — the [contract](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md#the-contract), the [four action levels](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md), "hide the machinery but never the reasoning," and *design against approval fatigue* — and to the **Agent Factory** platform the brief names (versioned capabilities, human-confirmed actions, deterministic evaluators, shadow-mode evaluation). Status: `proposed-extension`.

## The five features

| # | Feature | Doc | One-liner |
|---|---------|-----|-----------|
| F1 | Multi-agent orchestration | [multi-agent-orchestration.md](./multi-agent-orchestration.md) | How the Operator spins off specialist agents and how you observe/steer them |
| F2 | Artifact Library | [artifact-library.md](./artifact-library.md) | One place for everything the agents produce |
| F3 | Agents & Skills registry | [agent-and-skill-registry.md](./agent-and-skill-registry.md) | See every agent & skill; configure, toggle, and route edits to governance |
| F4 | Scheduled agents | [scheduled-agents.md](./scheduled-agents.md) | Run agents on a cadence and control how they report back |
| F5 | Context & communication | [context-and-communication.md](./context-and-communication.md) | Keep the user informed and keep agent context bounded for accurate results |
| F6 | Collaboration & presence | [collaboration-and-presence.md](./collaboration-and-presence.md) | Multiple people + agents on one filing — who's viewing, who's acting, what changed |

## How they fit together

The five are one loop, not five products:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Operator[Operator - orchestrator] -->|spins off| Workers[Specialist agents - F1]
  Workers -->|produce| Artifacts[Artifact Library - F2]
  Registry[Agents & Skills registry - F3] -->|enable / configure / govern| Workers
  Registry -->|enable / configure| Schedules[Scheduled agents - F4]
  Schedules -->|dispatch on cadence| Workers
  Workers -->|report via| Comms[Context & communication - F5]
  Artifacts -->|externalized memory| Comms
  Comms -->|legible, bounded, accurate| Operator
  People[People - many, F6] -->|view / act / approve| Operator
  People -->|presence + attribution| Comms
```

**F6 (collaboration)** wraps the whole loop: many people share the workspace, see the same live progress, and act within their roles — every action attributed to a person or an agent.

- The **Operator orchestrates** specialist agents (F1) —
- whose outputs are stored as **artifacts** (F2) —
- managed and toggled through the **registry** (F3) —
- some of them running on **schedules** (F4) —
- all kept **legible and context-bounded** by the communication + memory layer (F5).

## In the app shell

Three of these features are **top-level destinations in the left sidebar** of the [app shell](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout); the other two are cross-cutting:

| Sidebar destination | Feature |
|---------------------|---------|
| **⌂ Home (Dashboard)** | Surfaces F1 orchestration activity + F4 scheduled findings + people activity |
| **⚙ Settings → Agents & Skills** | F3 registry (a configuration surface, grouped under Settings) |
| **▣ Artifacts** | F2 library (grouped by Reports / Packages / Audits) |
| **⏱ Schedules (Monitoring)** | F4 scheduled/standing agents + findings & digests |
| **Sessions (search / pinned / all)** | F5 sessions — the context-bounding unit of work |
| *(cross-cutting, one step away)* | F1 activity view, F5 findings tray & session indicator, F6 presence & change log |

## One principle governs all five

Everything here obeys the brief's spine: **the Operator is the experience, not a fleet of chatbots the user has to babysit.** Multiple agents, artifacts, registries, and schedules exist to make the work *carriable and legible* — never to push orchestration burden onto the user, and never to file unsupervised. Sub-agents and scheduled agents inherit the [action model](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md): they may Read, Recommend, and Prepare autonomously, but **Commit always escalates to a human**, and neither can cross a [signature commit](../02-glossary/glossary.md#signature-commits).

## Purpose

Two intertwined jobs:

1. **Keep the user informed** — the Operator is never a silent black box; the user always knows what it's doing, what it read, what it's about to do, and what it needs.
2. **Keep agent context bounded for accurate results** — the product actively manages how much an agent holds in its working context, and **guides the user** to keep requests well-scoped, because an overloaded context window produces inaccurate results.

The second is the substantive ask: **how the product prevents context-window overflow and helps the user avoid it.**

---

## Part A — Keeping the user informed

### Progress transparency (no silent black box)

At every altitude the user can see, in plain language:

- **Now:** what the Operator/agents are doing (*"Mapping 25 fields · chasing 8 owners"*).
- **Read:** what sources/artifacts it used (provenance one step away — [P5](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p5--reasoning-one-step-away)).
- **Next:** the proposed next-best-step ([P2](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p2--next-best-step)).
- **Needs you:** pending approvals, blocking questions, exceptions.

Long-running work streams progress rather than freezing; the [Activity view](./multi-agent-orchestration.md#the-activity-view-aka-work-view) is the drill-down. See [P16 Progress transparency](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p16--progress-transparency).

### Status & communication surfaces

| Surface | Role |
|---------|------|
| **Work summary** | Always-visible rollup of current activity + what needs the user |
| **Activity view** | Drill-down into agents/tasks/provenance ([F1](./multi-agent-orchestration.md)) |
| **Findings tray / inbox** | Where [scheduled agents](./scheduled-agents.md) and workers surface items needing attention |
| **Notifications** | Push for material/time-critical items, threshold-gated |
| **Session context indicator** | A subtle signal of how "loaded" the current working session is (see Part B) |

### Right-sized communication (against fatigue & noise)

- **Quiet by default, loud when it matters** — routine progress is glanceable; only exceptions and decisions interrupt ([P7](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine)).
- **Digest, not deluge** — non-urgent findings roll into digests.
- **One clear ask at a time** — decisions are framed as a single next-best-step, not a wall of options.

---

## Part B — Keeping context bounded for accuracy

### Why this matters

Agents produce accurate, reproducible results only when their working context holds the *right, relevant* information — not everything. An overloaded context window degrades accuracy, buries load-bearing facts, and undermines the "no invented figures" contract. For a penalty-bearing filing, **bounded context is a correctness requirement, not an optimization.**

### The core mechanism: externalize memory, don't accumulate it

The product's answer is architectural, not just advisory — **memory lives in the substrate and the [Artifact Library](./artifact-library.md), not in a growing conversation.**

| Mechanism | How it bounds context |
|-----------|-----------------------|
| **Governed facts + fact store** | Accepted values live in the substrate; agents load the specific facts a task needs, not the whole history ([I1](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i1--compounding-facts-across-the-portfolio)) |
| **Artifacts as durable memory** | Agents reference prior outputs by artifact + lineage instead of re-deriving or re-pasting them ([P14](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p14--artifacts-as-durable-memory)) |
| **Deterministic tools do the math** | Load-bearing computation runs in deterministic evaluators, *not* in the model's context — keeping the model's job small |
| **Provenance by pointer** | Sources are referenced and retrieved on demand (retrieval), not dumped wholesale into context |
| **Scoped worker tasks** | Fan-out ([F1](./multi-agent-orchestration.md)) gives each specialist agent only the slice it needs (one entity/section/field) — small, focused context per worker |
| **Phase handoff summaries** | Moving between lifecycle phases hands off a compact state, not the full transcript |

Net effect: no single agent ever needs to "hold the whole filing" in context. It holds *its slice*, backed by durable memory it can query.

### Guiding the user to keep context healthy

The product doesn't rely on users understanding token limits — it **steers them**:

- **The governed prompt library steers scope.** Because work is proposed as well-scoped next-best-steps ([P2](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p2--next-best-step)), users are naturally guided away from open-ended mega-requests.
- **Decompose big asks automatically.** If a user asks for something too broad (*"do all 200 filings now"*), the Operator proposes breaking it into batches/slices, explains *why* (accuracy and safety), and runs it as orchestrated workers ([F1](./multi-agent-orchestration.md)) rather than one overloaded pass. See [P15 Scope the work, not the world](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p15--scope-the-work-not-the-world).
- **Session hygiene by design.** The [app shell](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout) makes the **session** the unit of work: the **New session** CTA starts a clean, bounded context, and each filing gets its own thread (searchable, pinnable in the sidebar) so context doesn't bleed across unrelated filings. This is the primary structural defense against context overflow.
- **Context indicator + gentle nudge.** A subtle session indicator shows when a working session is getting large, with a plain-language nudge — *"This is a big batch; I'll work through it in stages and checkpoint results so they stay accurate"* — rather than exposing raw token counts to a compliance user.
- **Checkpoint & resume.** Long efforts checkpoint into artifacts, so a session can be summarized and continued fresh without losing state or accuracy.

### The accuracy safeguards behind it

Bounded context is necessary but not sufficient — it's backed by:

- **Deterministic cross-checks** on the two signature moments catch any drift ([governance](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md)).
- **Confidence routing** ([G4](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g4--no-defined-confidence-model)) sends low-confidence work to review rather than trusting a strained context.
- **Continuous evaluation / shadow comparison** ([G5](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g5--evaluation--shadow-mode-asserted-not-designed)) flags regressions.
- **Reproducibility** — because results derive from bounded, cited inputs, they can be regenerated and verified.

---

## Design summary

| Goal | Primary mechanism |
|------|-------------------|
| User always informed | Progress transparency, work summary, activity view, findings tray ([P16](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p16--progress-transparency)) |
| No noise / no fatigue | Quiet-by-default, digests, one-ask-at-a-time ([P7](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine)) |
| Context stays bounded | Externalized memory (facts + artifacts), deterministic tools, scoped workers ([P14](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p14--artifacts-as-durable-memory)) |
| Users kept on the rails | Prompt library, auto-decompose, session hygiene, context nudge ([P15](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p15--scope-the-work-not-the-world)) |
| Results stay accurate | Cross-checks, confidence routing, continuous eval, reproducibility |

## Related

- Durable memory store: [Artifact Library](./artifact-library.md)
- Scoped fan-out: [Multi-agent orchestration](./multi-agent-orchestration.md)
- Scheduled findings reporting: [Scheduled agents](./scheduled-agents.md)
- Patterns: [P14](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p14--artifacts-as-durable-memory), [P15](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p15--scope-the-work-not-the-world), [P16](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p16--progress-transparency)
