## Purpose

Give the user **one place that contains everything the agents produce**, quickly accessible from anywhere — and make that store double as the Operator's **durable, externalized memory** (which is what keeps agent context bounded and results accurate — see [context-and-communication.md](./context-and-communication.md)).

## What counts as an artifact

Every meaningful output an agent generates, at any phase:

| Phase | Example artifacts |
|-------|-------------------|
| Front door | Readiness briefing, obligation assessment |
| Scope | Scope plan, cross-check report, scope-approval record |
| Map & ingest | Mapping table, source-match report, coverage report |
| Collect & chase | Drafted requests, captured replies, worklist snapshots |
| Validate | Reconciliation report, validation results, scope-delta |
| Prepare & assemble | Draft package, populated forms, readiness report |
| Review | Judgment ledger, final-verification report |
| Close | Filing package, evidence bundle, next-year baseline, monitoring plan, [regulator-ready explainability export](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i3--regulator-ready-explainability-artifact) |
| Scheduled runs | Run reports from [scheduled agents](./scheduled-agents.md) |

Machine outputs (CSV / XML / PDF for a form class) are artifacts too.

## Artifact vs evidence — kept distinct

- **Artifact** = something an *agent produced* (a scope plan, a draft package).
- **Evidence** = *source proof* a value rests on (an ERP export, an email reply).

They link: an artifact cites the evidence behind it, and some artifacts (the evidence bundle) *collect* evidence. This mirrors the substrate's "link, not duplicate" rule ([object-model.md](../04-information-architecture/object-model.md)).

## Every artifact carries

| Attribute | Why |
|-----------|-----|
| **Type & title** | Filter/find |
| **Producing agent + filing run + phase** | Traceability |
| **Version + status** (`draft` / `approved` / `final` / `superseded`) | Amendment & audit ([G1](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g1--no-correction-amendment-or-restatement-lifecycle)) |
| **Provenance / lineage** — what facts, rules, and evidence produced it; what it fed into | "No uncited" contract; reasoning one step away |
| **Confidentiality classification + permissions** | Respect that filing data is confidential ([G2](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g2--confidentiality--llm-data-handling-under-specified)) |
| **Timestamp + actor** | Audit trail |
| **Blueprint & rule-pack version** | Reproducibility |

## Where it lives

The Artifact Library is the **"Artifacts" destination in the left sidebar** ([app shell](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout)) — always one click away — and is also reachable per-filing from within a session.

Two access altitudes, one store:

- **Portfolio view (sidebar → Artifacts)** — all artifacts across all filings, **grouped by Reports / Packages / Audits** by default (the user's mental model), then filterable. This is the "quickly access it" surface.
- **Per-filing view (in session)** — every artifact for one filing run, in phase order (the natural drill-down from a filing).

**Default grouping (sidebar Artifacts view):**

| Group | Contains |
|-------|----------|
| **Reports** | Per-report artifacts — readiness briefings, scope plans, mapping tables, populated forms, readiness reports |
| **Packages** | Assembled filing packages + evidence bundles, per filing/period |
| **Audits** | Judgment ledgers, audit trails, and [regulator-ready explainability exports](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i3--regulator-ready-explainability-artifact) |

Additional filters within any group: type, filing, period, entity, producing agent, status, date, confidentiality. Search across titles and (permitted) contents.

## What the user can do

- **Preview / open** any artifact without leaving the surface.
- **Download / export** (respecting permissions) — including the evidence bundle and the regulator-ready explainability doc.
- **Version compare & restore** — diff versions; supersede with lineage (never silent — [P10](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p10--override-with-record)).
- **Trace lineage** — "show what produced this" and "show what this fed into" (the provenance graph).
- **Pin / organize** — pin key artifacts to the filing header; group by phase.
- **Share** — within permissions; sharing is an audited action.
- **Retention controls** — retention/legal-hold per confidentiality policy.

## Why this is also the Operator's memory

Because every output is externalized here with provenance, the Operator **references artifacts and governed facts instead of re-deriving or re-loading everything into context**. This is the mechanism behind bounded context and reproducible results:

- Memory lives in the **substrate + artifact store**, not the conversation window.
- An agent picks up work by loading the relevant *artifact*, not the whole history.
- Reproducibility: an artifact + its lineage can regenerate or verify a result.

See [P14 Artifacts as durable memory](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p14--artifacts-as-durable-memory) and [context-and-communication.md](./context-and-communication.md).

## Governance ties

- Artifacts are **first-class in the object model** ([object-model.md](../04-information-architecture/object-model.md)) and the audit trail.
- Status transitions (`draft → approved → final → superseded`) align with the [action model](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md): an artifact becomes `final` only through the relevant Commit / signature commit.
- Confidentiality is enforced **below the UI**, per seat and per entity.

## Related

- Who produces them: [Multi-agent orchestration](./multi-agent-orchestration.md), [Scheduled agents](./scheduled-agents.md)
- As memory: [Context & communication](./context-and-communication.md)
- Object model: [object-model.md](../04-information-architecture/object-model.md)
- Realizes: [I3 explainability export](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i3--regulator-ready-explainability-artifact), supports [G1 amendments](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g1--no-correction-amendment-or-restatement-lifecycle)

## Purpose

A filing is a team sport — **multiple people and multiple agents work the same filing at once.** This feature makes that collaboration safe and legible by answering three questions at all times:

1. **Who's here / who's viewing?** — presence
2. **Who can do what, and who did it?** — roles + attribution
3. **What changed?** — the change log / activity feed

This resolves [G10 (no collaboration/concurrency model)](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g10--no-collaboration--concurrency-model).

## Shared by default, permissioned throughout

Filings, sessions, and the agents working them are **shared** across the people who have access — everyone with permission sees the same live state and the same agent progress. Access is governed by seat and by entity/confidentiality: **you only ever see what you're permitted to** (a data owner sees their affiliate, not the whole filing). Sharing is an audited action.

## 1 · Who's viewing — presence

- **Live presence** on a filing/session shows who else is here and, at a glance, **what surface they're on** (e.g. "Reviewer is on the judgment ledger").
- Presence is visible on [Home (Dashboard)](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout) as "what other people are doing," and inside a session as avatars/indicators.
- **Viewing is not acting** — being present is passive; changing state requires the right role and an explicit action.

## 2 · Who can do what — roles & attribution

Every actor — **human or agent** — has a defined capability, and every action is **attributed**.

### Human roles (layered on the [seats](../03-personas/personas.md))

| Role | Can view | Can comment | Can act (Prepare) | Can Commit | Signature commits | Configure agents |
|------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Viewer** | ✓ | — | — | — | — | — |
| **Commenter** | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| **Preparer** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ *(permitted)* | — | — |
| **Reviewer-approver** | ✓ | ✓ | — | ✓ | ✓ *(confirm scope, final approval)* | — |
| **Workspace Admin** | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | ✓ |
| **Data / Source Owner** | ✓ *(their scope)* | ✓ | ✓ *(their fields)* | — | — | — |

- The two **signature commits** are reserved to the Reviewer-approver — no role or agent autonomy can reach them ([governance](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md#two-kinds-of-governance-kept-separate)).
- **Agents are actors too**, capped by their [autonomy ceiling](../02-glossary/glossary.md#autonomy-ceiling); their work is attributed to the agent (and to the human who approved any Commit).

### Attribution

Every change records **who** (which person or which agent), **when**, **what changed**, and **why** (for overrides). Attribution is shown **inline** (e.g. "value accepted by Julie · mapped by Collection agent · from Maria Keller's email") and rolled into the **[audit trail](../06-features/governed-substrate.md)**. This is [override-with-record](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p10--override-with-record) extended to every actor.

## 3 · What changed — the change log / activity feed

- A per-filing **activity feed** shows a chronological record of every material action — human and agent — with attribution and a link to the artifact/decision.
- The [Activity view](./multi-agent-orchestration.md) shows *live* agent work; the change log is the *durable* record of what happened.
- Home aggregates activity across the portfolio ("what you, the agents, and other people are doing").

## Concurrency — many actors, no collisions

- **Scoped slices.** People and agents work different entities/sections/fields in parallel; the Operator partitions work to avoid collision (same mechanism as agent [fan-out](./multi-agent-orchestration.md#concurrency--conflict-handling)).
- **Locking where it matters.** Signature-commit moments (scope confirmation, final approval) lock the relevant state so two people can't approve conflicting versions; routine edits use optimistic concurrency.
- **Conflicts surfaced, never silently resolved.** If two actors (or an actor and an agent) change the same thing, the Operator flags it for a human ([P5](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p5--reasoning-one-step-away)).

## Handoffs, delegation & coverage

- **Reassign / delegate** work (e.g. hand 10 affiliates to a colleague) or **delegate approval** — with audit ([G10](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g10--no-collaboration--concurrency-model)).
- **Out-of-office coverage** so a filing never stalls on one person.
- **Comments & @mentions** in place — request a review, ask a question, resolve a thread — distinct from Operator prompts (human-to-human, not human-to-agent).

## How it shows up in the shell

| Surface | Collaboration element |
|---------|-----------------------|
| **Home (Dashboard)** | People activity + presence across the portfolio; pending approvals routed to you |
| **Session** | Live presence; inline attribution; comments/@mentions |
| **Activity view** | Who (human/agent) is doing what, now |
| **Change log** | Durable, attributed record of what changed |
| **Artifacts** | Sharing (audited) and per-artifact attribution/lineage |

## Governance ties

- **Commit is permissioned per seat**; viewing never implies acting.
- **Every actor is attributed** — human or agent — and every override is recorded.
- **Confidentiality is per-seat and per-entity**, enforced below the UI — collaboration never over-shares.

## Related

- Seats & mapping: [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md)
- Live agent work: [Multi-agent orchestration](./multi-agent-orchestration.md)
- Governance: [governance-and-action-model.md](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md)
- Pattern: [P19 Legible collaboration](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p19--legible-collaboration)
- Resolves: [G10](../10-analysis/gaps-and-solutions.md#g10--no-collaboration--concurrency-model)

## Note on "pages"

Agentic CRR runs inside a **desktop app shell** — a persistent, collapsible **left sidebar** for global wayfinding and a **main content area** that renders the active session or a selected global view (see [App shell layout](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout)). Inside a session, the main content is **not** a set of fixed pages: it is the conversational control surface that renders phase-appropriate **views**, always with a **next best step** and provenance one step away.

## Shell surfaces (left sidebar)

Stable global destinations — wayfinding, not workflow steps.

| Surface | Purpose | Primary actions | Seat |
|---------|---------|-----------------|------|
| **✚ New session** | Start a fresh, context-bounded working thread | Pick/confirm a report, or ask ad-hoc | All |
| **⌂ Home (Dashboard)** | Overview of everything you, the agents, and other people are doing; a **Recent reports** list (last 5 changed) opens the report dashboard | Open a report's dashboard, triage findings & approvals, view activity, ask the Operator inline, drill from a stat into the work behind it, page through the upcoming-reports calendar | All |
| **▤ My Reports** | Every report grouped in-progress / completed / archived | **Create a new report**, or open a report's [dashboard](#the-report-dashboard) | Preparer, Reviewer |
| **▣ Artifacts** | All agent outputs, grouped by Reports / Forms / Packages / Audits — the **Forms** tab lists every form grouped under the report that owns it | Browse, preview, open a form's page, export, trace lineage | Preparer, Reviewer |
| **⛁ Source data** | Connected sources + manual uploads | View sources, upload a file, see what's linked to each report | Preparer, Workspace Admin |
| **⏱ Schedules (Monitoring)** | Set/manage scheduled & standing agents; see findings | Create/edit/pause schedule, set reporting, triage findings | Workspace Admin, Preparer |
| **⌕ Search sessions** | Find a session | Search by report/period/entity/content | All |
| **★ Pinned sessions** | Quick access to active/important reports | Open, unpin | All |
| **≣ All sessions** | Full session history | Open, resume, archive | All |
| **⚙ Settings** | Workspace/user config + **Agents & Skills** management | Connectors, notifications, permissions, autonomy defaults; open Agents & Skills | Workspace Admin |

## In-session surface inventory (main content)

| Surface | Purpose | Primary actions | Seat | Phase |
|---------|---------|-----------------|------|-------|
| **Home (Dashboard) → portfolio** | One workspace for many reports | Open a report, see what's due/missing/to-act-on | Preparer | Front door |
| **Readiness briefing** | The Operator "starts ahead" for a filing | Review briefing, *Prepare scope plan* | Preparer | A |
| **Scope plan** | Affiliates/claims grouped by outcome, each with evidence + rule | Review, resolve/route flags, *Send for scope approval* | Preparer | B |
| **Scope confirmation** | What changed + exceptions + cross-check | *Confirm scope* / *Send back* | Reviewer-approver | B |
| **Source & mapping view** | Matched sources/fields, low-confidence flags | Confirm sources, review mappings, *Prepare requests* | Preparer | C |
| **Collection worklist** | Each gap as a tracked request | *Send*, *Accept*, *Send reminder* | Preparer (+ Data owner) | D |
| **Request preview** | The drafted request to an owner | Review & *Send* | Preparer | D |
| **Draft package** | Values populated from accepted facts, each sourced | Review, *Prepare for review* | Preparer | E–F |
| **Readiness view** | % ready, blockers, warnings, pending evidence, approved changes | Resolve gaps, *Prepare for review* | Preparer | F |
| **Judgment ledger** | Complete decision record | *Approve final package* / *Send back* | Reviewer-approver | G |
| **Package & close** | Staged bundle, evidence, next-year baseline | *Create monitoring plan* | Preparer | H |
| **Agent dispatch card** | An inline chat card, shown when the Operator spins up specialist agents for a step — each row names the **agent** and the **purpose** it was dispatched for (e.g. *Scope & Entity — grouping 42 affiliates*, *Collection & Chase — chasing 8 owners*) with a live status (Working → Done). It surfaces the delegation the Operator would otherwise hide, right in the conversation; the full task tree stays one step away in the [Activity view](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md) | Read; open Activity view for the full tree | Preparer | All |
| **Provenance / cross-check panel** | Where a value came from; deterministic cross-check | Inspect (always one step away) | All | All |
| **Governed prompt library** | Curated next-best-step prompts | Choose/accept a proposed step | Preparer | All |

### Agent-operations surfaces ([section 11](../11-agent-operations/README.md))

| Surface | Purpose | Primary actions | Seat | Doc |
|---------|---------|-----------------|------|-----|
| **Activity view (Work view)** | Make multi-agent work legible & interruptible | Observe, steer, answer, approve, pause/stop | Preparer | [F1](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md) |
| **Artifact Library** | One place for everything agents produce | Preview, export, compare versions, trace lineage, pin, share | Preparer, Reviewer | [F2](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md) |

## The Home dashboard

Home is the portfolio-level front door — a summary a user should be able to act from directly, not just read. Top to bottom:

| Panel | What it shows | Action it opens |
|-------|----------------|------------------|
| **Stat cards** (Active reports · Needs your approval · Overdue inputs · Deadline this week) | The four numbers that answer "where do things stand" | Each stat is a drill-down, not a static count: *Active reports* → **My Reports**; *Needs your approval* → the **work queue**, scoped to the decision + approval groups; *Overdue inputs* → the work queue, scoped to the data-chase group; *Deadline this week* → the specific report that's due, opened directly on its [dashboard](#the-report-dashboard) |
| **Ask the Operator** | A slim single-line command bar directly under the stat cards — a plain input plus a handful of [smart starter prompts](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p2--next-best-step). Deliberately lightweight so it reads as a persistent entry point, not a hero panel competing with the work | Typing or picking a prompt opens a new session pre-loaded with that question — the same governed-prompt-library mechanic used inside a session, surfaced one level higher |
| **Needs you** (work queue) | The governor's **exceptions queue** ([P11](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p11--governor-not-operator)) — everything needing a person across obligations, reports, data, and approvals, urgent items first (overdue/blockers on top). It sits **directly beneath the command bar, above Upcoming**, because "what needs me now" is the story Home tells first ([P7](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine)); a per-card count and an "only blockers" toggle keep it scannable | Each item's CTA (e.g. *Send reminder*, *Open the form*, *Review scope*, *Review obligation*) is the action itself, not a link to go find it |
| **Upcoming reports** | *What's coming next*, one level below "Needs you": a compact month calendar plus an agenda list of the next reports coming due, nearest first. The calendar **pages month-by-month** (‹ / ›) so a user can look ahead to future deadlines; deadlines carry real dates and land on the correct month, and "today" is only highlighted in the current month | Any marked day or agenda row opens that report's dashboard |
| **Recent reports / Agent activity / Present now / From your monitors** | The existing portfolio feed — most-recently-changed reports, what agents just did, who else is around, what standing monitors found | Opens the report, or is read-only context |

**Why stat cards drill down.** A count with nothing behind it ("2 approvals waiting") forces the user to go hunt for which two. Making every stat clickable — straight into the filtered work queue or the one report it refers to — turns the summary into the start of the action, consistent with [P2 Next best step](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p2--next-best-step) and [P7 surface ambiguity](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine).

## The report dashboard

**My Reports** lists every report grouped by **in progress / completed / archived**, with a **New report** action in the header for starting a fresh obligation (see [Creating a report](#creating-a-report)); opening one lands on that report's **dashboard** — a read-first control surface for a single report, distinct from (and linked to) its Operator [session](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#sessions-the-unit-of-work). Where the session is the *conversation that does the work*, the dashboard is the *at-a-glance state of the work*.

The dashboard is laid out in three tiers so it tells a story top-to-bottom — *know the state → act on what needs you → explore the work and reference*:

| Tier | Panel | What it shows |
|------|-------|---------------|
| **1 · State** | **Header + strip** | Code, title, status, readiness %, **forms complete** (e.g. "38 of 42 complete"), current phase; a prominent **Open in Operator** button that jumps to the report's chat session |
| **2 · Needs you** | **Needs you** (full-width band) | The governor's focus, promoted directly under the strip: the signature commits/decisions **pending human confirmation** *and* the open **blockers & warnings**, merged into one severity-ranked band ([P4](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p4--protect-the-signature-commits), [P7](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine)). Each item carries the **CTA to act** (e.g. *Open judgment ledger*, *Send reminder*, *Review obligation*). When nothing is outstanding it collapses to a calm *"On track — nothing needs your confirmation right now"* state |
| **3 · Work** (main column) | **Forms in this report** | The [forms](#a-report-bundles-forms) this report bundles — for BEA, a BE-11A for the U.S. Reporter plus **one form per foreign affiliate in scope** (BE-11B / BE-11C) — each with the entity/jurisdiction it covers and a status (Complete / In progress / Blocked / Not started). Leads the main column as the report's substance; shows a sample with a "showing N of M" count. **Each row opens that form's own page** (see [the form page](#the-form-page)) |
| **3 · Work** (main column) | **Agents used & outputs** | Below the forms: every specialist agent that has run on this report and what it produced — each output links to its [artifact](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md) (the evidence behind the work) |
| **3 · Reference** (right rail) | **Filing lifecycle** | The 8-step spine (front door → close), with signature gates, marking done / current / upcoming for *this* report — the same lifecycle view the Operator session uses |
| **3 · Reference** (right rail) | **Key dates** | The three dates the report carries — **start date**, **data collection due**, and **filing due** — captured when the report is created (see [Creating a report](#creating-a-report)) |
| **3 · Reference** (right rail) | **People involved** | The [seats](../03-personas/personas.md) on this report with their roles ([collaboration](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md)) |

The dashboard reads the same governed record the session acts on — it never becomes a second source of truth. It is a *view*, per [P16 progress transparency](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p16--progress-transparency): the whole state of a penalty-bearing report, legible at a glance, with the reasoning one step away.

### A report bundles forms

A **report** is one regulatory obligation for a period (e.g. *BE-11 · FY25*). It is not a single document — it **bundles the forms** that obligation requires. For BEA's BE-11 survey the report fans out into a **BE-11A** for the U.S. Reporter's consolidated domestic business plus **one form per foreign affiliate in scope** — a **BE-11B** for each majority-owned affiliate and a **BE-11C** for each minority-owned affiliate above the size test; a BE-577 report produces a form per affiliate with reportable transactions. Other report classes fan out on their own unit — Country-by-Country produces a schedule per **tax jurisdiction**, SF-425 a form per **federal award**. The forms are generated once scope is confirmed, and the report's readiness rolls up from the state of its forms. See [object model](../04-information-architecture/object-model.md) (Report → Filing blueprint → forms) and [glossary](../02-glossary/glossary.md).

### The form page

Opening a form (from the report dashboard's **Forms in this report** panel, or from the **Forms** tab in **Artifacts**) lands on that single form's page — the agency form itself, laid out the way the real BEA document is. A BE-11B renders **Part I — Identification** (U.S. Reporter, affiliate name, country/city of location, fiscal-year end, whether it became an affiliate this year), **Section A — Direct Ownership** (equity and voting %), **Section B — Industry Classification** (major activity, product/service, ISI code), **Part II** employment / compensation / R&D and the $300M size test, and **Part III/IV** financials (net income, sales, balance sheet, PP&E). Every value is either **populated from an accepted, sourced fact** (with its source noted) or shown as **awaiting data** for figures still being chased — so a blocked or not-started form reads as a partly-filled document, not an error. The BE-11A variant renders the U.S. Reporter's consolidated data; BE-11C uses the minority-owned layout. A **status pill**, the **agent** that populated it, and an **Open in Operator** button sit above the form. Nothing on the page is filed without a recorded human approval.

### Creating a report

From **My Reports**, **New report** opens a short form with just what's needed to open the obligation: a **report name** (the title shown across the workspace, e.g. *BE-11 · FY25*), the **report type** (BE-11, BE-577, BE-125, Country-by-Country, SF-425), a **start date** and **due date**, and a **data collection due date**. On create, the report appears at the top of *In progress*, opens on its dashboard with those dates shown in the **Key dates** panel, and is added to the Home **Upcoming reports** calendar on its due date. The Operator starts at the front door (reading entity data and prior filings) and, once scope is confirmed, generates one form per entity in scope. In practice most reports are also surfaced proactively by [Obligation Scout](../06-features/obligation-scout.md); the manual **New report** path covers the case where a preparer already knows what they need to file.

## Relationships

```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph Sidebar[Left sidebar]
    New[✚ New session]
    Home[⌂ Home]
    Filings2[▤ My Reports]
    Library[▣ Artifacts]
    Sources2[⛁ Source data]
    Schedules2[⏱ Schedules]
    Sessions[≣ / ★ Sessions]
    Settings[⚙ Settings → Agents & Skills]
  end
  New --> Session[Session in main content]
  Sessions --> Session
  Home --> Session
  Session --> Briefing[Readiness briefing]
  Briefing --> Scope[Scope plan]
  Scope --> Confirm[Scope confirmation]
  Confirm --> Sources[Source & mapping view]
  Sources --> Worklist[Collection worklist]
  Worklist --> Preview[Request preview]
  Worklist --> Draft[Draft package]
  Draft --> Readiness[Readiness view]
  Readiness --> Ledger[Judgment ledger]
  Ledger --> Close[Package & close]
  Close -.next cycle.-> Home
  Prov[Provenance / cross-check] -.one step away.- Scope
  Prov -.one step away.- Ledger
  Prompts[Prompt library] -.proposes next step.- Session
  Activity[Activity view] -.one step away.- Worklist
  Schedules[Scheduled agents] -.findings.-> Home
```

**Two kinds of surface:** the **sidebar** hosts stable global destinations (Home, Agents & Skills, Artifacts, Sessions, Settings); the **main content** hosts the active session, where the lifecycle plays out. Agent-operations panels (activity view, findings tray, session indicator) are one step away from anywhere in a session — see [section 11](../11-agent-operations/README.md).

## Cross-surface principles

- **Hide the machinery, never the reasoning** — the user doesn't see *which capability* runs; provenance and cross-check are always reachable.
- **Next best step everywhere** — each surface ends with a proposed action.
- **Attention-only** — routine passed checks stay quiet; surfaces highlight the few items needing judgment.
- **Confidentiality** — surfaces respect that report data is confidential (per seat and entity).
- **Collaborative & attributed** — surfaces are multi-user; presence shows who's viewing, and every change shows who did it (human or agent). See [F6](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md).

See [design-patterns.md](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md) for the design rationale.

## The Operator is a control surface, not a chatbot

Agentic CRR presents as **one conversational, action-capable surface** — the Regulatory Filing Operator. It centralizes a *portfolio of filings* into a single workspace and proposes work through a [governed prompt library](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-prompt-library). Two rules define the surface:

- **Hide the machinery** — the user should not have to know *which capability* is running (Obligation Scout vs Mapping vs Collection).
- **Never hide the reasoning** — provenance and the deterministic cross-check are always **one step away**.

## App shell layout

The product is a **desktop app shell** (modeled on the Hermes agent desktop app): a persistent, **collapsible left sidebar** for global wayfinding and a **main content area** on the right that renders the active session or the selected global view.

│  ▣  Artifacts             │   (active session, or the selected           │
│  ⏱  Schedules             │    global view: Home / Agents & Skills /     │
│                           │    Artifacts / Schedules / Settings)         │
│  ⌕  Search sessions…      │                                              │
│                           │                                              │
│  ★ Pinned sessions        │                                              │
│    · BE-11 FY25           │                                              │
│    · Q3 chase review      │                                              │
│                           │                                              │

### Sidebar navigation map

| Sidebar item | Opens in main content | Maps to |
|--------------|-----------------------|---------|
| **✚ New session** | A fresh working thread (pick/confirm a report, or ask ad-hoc) | [Session](#sessions-the-unit-of-work) · context boundary ([F5](../11-agent-operations/context-and-communication.md)) |
| **⌂ Home (Dashboard)** | Overview of everything *you*, the *agents*, and *other people* are doing | Portfolio workspace + [Activity view](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md) + collaboration |
| **▤ My Reports** | Every report grouped by *in progress / completed / archived*; **New report** starts a fresh obligation; each opens a per-report [dashboard](../07-pages/operator-surfaces.md#the-report-dashboard) | [Report dashboard](../07-pages/operator-surfaces.md#the-report-dashboard) |
| **▣ Artifacts** | All agent-generated outputs, grouped by Reports / Packages / Audits | [F2 Artifact Library](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md) |
| **⛁ Source data** | Connected source systems + manually-uploaded files the Operator draws on; where the agent's upload requests land | [Source Discovery & Ingestion](../06-features/source-discovery-and-ingestion.md) |
| **⏱ Schedules** | The monitoring hub — set/manage scheduled & standing agents and see how they report back | [F4 Scheduled agents](../11-agent-operations/scheduled-agents.md) |
| **⌕ Search sessions** | Find a session by report, period, entity, or content | Session search |
| **★ Pinned sessions** | Quick access to active/important reports | Pinned [sessions](#sessions-the-unit-of-work) |
| **≣ All sessions** | Full session history | Session history |
| **⚙ Settings** | Profile, workspace, connectors, notifications, permissions, autonomy defaults, and **Agents & Skills** management | Settings + [F3 registry](../11-agent-operations/agent-and-skill-registry.md) |

The sidebar **collapses to icons** to give the main content full width — the work is in the main content; the sidebar is wayfinding.

### Reconciling the shell with "not fixed pages"

Earlier framing said navigation follows the *lifecycle, not a fixed IA of tabs*. Both are true and non-conflicting:

- The **sidebar is global wayfinding** — stable destinations (Home, Agents & Skills, Artifacts, Sessions, Settings), *not* workflow steps the user must assemble.
- The **filing work is still the phase-driven control surface**, and it renders **inside the active session in the main content**. The user never navigates the lifecycle via tabs; the Operator drives it with the next best step.

So: the shell gives durable orientation; the session's main content stays conversational and lifecycle-driven.

## Sessions: the unit of work

A **session** is a working thread with **bounded context** — the shell's core object and the mechanism behind accurate results ([F5](../11-agent-operations/context-and-communication.md), [P15](../09-design-patterns/design-patterns.md#p15--scope-the-work-not-the-world)).

- **Recommended scope:** one filing per session (e.g. *"BE-11 FY25"*) so context doesn't bleed across unrelated work; ad-hoc question/task sessions are fine too.
- **New session CTA** starts a fresh, clean context.
- Sessions are **searchable, pinnable, and listed** (pinned = active/important; all = history).
- **Session vs filing run:** a *session* is the interaction/working thread; a [filing run](./object-model.md) is the durable governed work object. One filing run may be touched across sessions; keeping a session to one filing is the context-hygiene default. The governed record lives in the run and the [Artifact Library](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md), not in the session transcript.

## In-session navigation (the filing lifecycle)

Within a session's main content, the Operator renders context-appropriate views and the next best step; the human moves through phases by accepting, editing, or declining.

```mermaid

  Briefing[Readiness briefing] --> Scope[Scope plan]
  Scope --> ScopeReview[Scope confirmation - reviewer]
  Scope --> Sources[Source & mapping view]
  Sources --> Worklist[Collection worklist]
  Worklist --> Draft[Draft package]
  Draft --> Readiness[Readiness view]
  Readiness --> Ledger[Judgment ledger - reviewer]
  Ledger --> Package[Package & close]
  Provenance[Provenance / cross-check panel] -.one step away.- Briefing
  Provenance -.one step away.- Scope
  Provenance -.one step away.- Ledger
  Activity[Activity view] -.one step away.- Worklist
```

## Surface map

Surfaces fall into three homes: **shell / global** (reached from the sidebar), **in-session** (the filing work in main content), and **one-step-away** panels.

### A. Shell / global surfaces (sidebar)

| Surface | Purpose | Primary seat | Maps to |
|---------|---------|--------------|---------|
| **Home (Dashboard)** | Overview of everything you, the agents, and other people are doing — active reports & readiness, agent activity, people activity, deadlines, pending approvals | All | Portfolio workspace + [Activity view](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md) |
| **My Reports** | Every report grouped in-progress / completed / archived; **New report** creates one; opens a per-report [dashboard](../07-pages/operator-surfaces.md#the-report-dashboard) | Preparer, Reviewer | [Report dashboard](../07-pages/operator-surfaces.md#the-report-dashboard) |
| **Artifacts** | All agent-generated outputs, grouped by Reports / Packages / Audits | Preparer, Reviewer | [F2](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md) |
| **Source data** | Connected sources + manual uploads; the destination for the agent's upload requests | Preparer, Workspace Admin | [Source Discovery & Ingestion](../06-features/source-discovery-and-ingestion.md) |
| **Schedules (Monitoring)** | Set/manage scheduled & standing agents; see findings & digests | Workspace Admin, Preparer | [F4](../11-agent-operations/scheduled-agents.md) |
| **Sessions (search / pinned / all)** | Find, pin, and revisit working threads | All | [Sessions](#sessions-the-unit-of-work) |
| **Settings** | Profile, workspace, connectors, notifications & digests, permissions, autonomy defaults, and **Agents & Skills** management | Workspace Admin | Settings + [F3](../11-agent-operations/agent-and-skill-registry.md) |

> **Agents & Skills lives under Settings** — it's a configuration/administration surface (managing the agent workforce), so it's reached from **Settings → Agents & Skills** rather than a top-level sidebar item.

### B. In-session surfaces (main content — the filing lifecycle)

| Surface | Purpose | Primary seat | Phase |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **Readiness briefing** | The pre-prepared "Operator starts ahead" view for a filing | Preparer | A |
| **Scope plan** | Affiliates/claims grouped by recommended outcome, each with evidence + rule | Preparer | B |
| **Scope confirmation** | What changed, exceptions resolved, independent cross-check | Reviewer-approver | B |
| **Source & mapping view** | Matched sources/fields; low-confidence mappings flagged | Preparer | C |
| **Collection worklist** | Each gap as a tracked request: requested → submitted → accepted/rejected | Preparer (+ Data owner) | D |
| **Draft package** | Values populated from accepted facts, each with a source | Preparer | E–F |
| **Readiness view** | Percent ready, blocking errors, warnings, pending evidence, approved changes | Preparer | F |
| **Judgment ledger** | Complete decision record for sign-off | Reviewer-approver | G |
| **Package & close** | Staged filing bundle, evidence bundle, next-year baseline | Preparer | H |

### C. One-step-away panels (from anywhere in a session)

| Surface | Purpose | Primary seat |
|---------|---------|--------------|
| **Activity view (Work view)** | Drill-down into the orchestrator → specialist-agent → task tree; observe/steer/approve | Preparer |
| **Provenance / cross-check panel** | Where a value came from; the deterministic cross-check | All |
| **Findings tray / inbox** | Where workers and scheduled agents surface items needing attention | Preparer |
| **Session-context indicator** | Subtle signal of working-session load with a plain-language nudge | Preparer |
| **Presence & change log** | Who's here / viewing, and an attributed record of what changed (human or agent) | All |

See [operator-surfaces.md](../07-pages/operator-surfaces.md) for surface detail and [section 11](../11-agent-operations/README.md) for the mechanics.

## Collaboration in the shell

Filings and sessions are **shared and multi-user**: several people (and many agents) work the same filing, each seeing the same live progress within their permissions. **Home** shows what other people are doing; **presence** shows who's viewing what; every action is **attributed** (human or agent); and **who can act vs only view** is governed by role. See [collaboration-and-presence.md](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md).

## Access, permissions & confidentiality

- **Governed autonomy is enforced below the UI** — every load-bearing figure comes from a deterministic tool; scope and final approval are backed by an independent verification the Operator cannot bypass.
- **Permissions** — official actions (*Commit*) are permissioned per seat; Base CRR is the permission source of record.
- **Confidentiality** — filing data is confidential; the surface must respect that in what it shows and to whom.
- **Evaluation gate** — nothing reaches a customer-facing surface without passing [shadow mode](../02-glossary/glossary.md#shadow-mode).

## Platform (Agent Factory)

Capabilities and human-confirmed actions are **configured and versioned** on the Agent Factory. Skills, context, rule sets, and confirmation gates are **SDC-configurable per report** — the same surface adapts to each filing via its [governed bundle](../02-glossary/glossary.md#governed-bundle).

## Purpose

How Agentic CRR objects relate in product language. The model has three tiers: the **commercial packaging** (what's sold), the **governed substrate** (what the Operator runs on, authored by SDCs/SMEs), and the **runtime record** (what a filing produces). Base CRR objects (Report, Entity, Form, Source data) are defined in the base [object model](../../CRR%20Product%20Memory/04-information-architecture/object-model.md); this shows what Agentic CRR adds on top.

## Three tiers

```mermaid
graph TD
  Pack[Pack - SKU bundle] --> Report[Report]
  Report --> Form[Form - one per entity in scope]
  Report --> Bundle[Governed bundle]
  Bundle --> Blueprint[Filing blueprint]
  Bundle --> RuleSet[Rule set]
  Bundle --> Skills[Skills & tools]
  RuleSet -.cites.-> KB[Knowledge base]
  Blueprint -.authored from.-> KB
  Report --> Run[Filing run]
  Run --> ScopePlan[Scope plan]
  ScopePlan --> ScopeItem[Scope item / affiliate outcome]
  Run --> Request[Collection request]
  Request --> Fact[Governed fact]
  Fact -.provenance.-> Evidence[Evidence]
  Run --> Ledger[Judgment ledger]
  Run --> Package[Filing package]
  Package --> Audit[Audit trail]
  Eval[Deterministic evaluator] -.cross-checks.-> ScopePlan
  Eval -.cross-checks.-> Package
  OrgIntel[Source & org intelligence] -.routes.-> Request
  OwnGraph[Ownership graph] -.scopes.-> ScopePlan
```

## Commercial packaging

| Object | Role |
|--------|------|
| **Pack** | SKU bundle of related forms; sets pricing & packaging (e.g. Corporate Controllership). A Pack is a bundle of **reports**. |
| **Report** | One filing category / obligation inside a Pack (e.g. BE-11), and the top-level object a user works in **My Reports**. Delivered by exactly one governed bundle. A report is not a single document — it **bundles the forms** the obligation requires: for BEA's BE-11 survey, that means a **BE-11A** for the U.S. Reporter's consolidated domestic business plus a **BE-11B** (majority-owned) or **BE-11C** (minority-owned) for each foreign affiliate in scope; Country-by-Country → a schedule per tax jurisdiction; SF-425 → a form per federal award. |
| **Form** | A single agency document inside a report (e.g. one BE-11B for one foreign affiliate), defined by the [filing blueprint](#governed-substrate-build-time-authored-by-sdcsme). Generated once scope is confirmed (one per entity/jurisdiction/award in scope). **Each form has its own page** — the agency form laid out section by section (identification, ownership, employment, income, balance sheet), with every value populated from accepted, sourced facts or shown as awaiting data. The report's readiness rolls up from the state of its forms. |

## Governed substrate (build-time, authored by SDC/SME)

The six governed elements, defined by **role, not topic** — where two seem to touch, the relationship is a *link (citation)*, not a duplicate. See [governed-substrate.md](../06-features/governed-substrate.md).

| Object | Defines | Non-overlap note |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| **Filing blueprint** | *What the filing is* — forms, sections, fields, instructions, conditional logic, package & evidence requirements, version, approval status | — |
| **Rule set** | *How it reasons* — applicability, scoping, thresholds, exemptions, routing, required/derived facts, validation, review gates, citations, test cases | Each rule **cites** the knowledge base |
| **Knowledge base** | Regulatory reference — agency instructions, definitions, guidance, citations | Source; rule set is its encoding |
| **Source & org intelligence** | Customer's sources/schemas/periods + org operating model (who owns/provides data) | Decides *who to ask* |
| **Ownership graph** | Equity ownership structure | Decides *who files* |
| **Deterministic evaluators** | Authority for repeatable logic; independent cross-check | Cannot be lowered/bypassed |
| **Evidence, audit & permissions** | Provenance, approval history, version history, audit trail | First-class, attached everywhere |

## Runtime record (per filing)

| Object | Role |
|--------|------|
| **Obligation set** | The full set of filings detected from one data intake (e.g. BE-11 + CbCR); each becomes its own filing run on confirmation |
| **Filing run** | An instance of the Operator carrying one report through the lifecycle (created at *Commit*) |
| **Scope plan** | Proposed scope — scope items grouped by recommended outcome, each with evidence + rule |
| **Scope item** | One affiliate/entity/claim outcome (e.g. "BE-11B recommended · majority-owned · sales above threshold") |
| **Collection request** | A tracked request for a missing value, tied to field/affiliate/owner/due date/evidence requirement |
| **Governed fact** | An accepted value with provenance, mapped to a filing field |
| **Judgment ledger** | The complete decision record used for sign-off |
| **Filing package** | Final forms + evidence bundle + provenance + approval record + versions + audit trail |
| **Next-year baseline** | Saved filing record **and** operating history (response times, delays, rework, exceptions) for next cycle |

## Agent-operations objects (the operating environment)

Objects introduced by [section 11](../11-agent-operations/README.md) — how agents run, what they produce, and how they're managed. All inherit the substrate's evidence/audit and the action model.

```mermaid
graph TD
  Operator[Operator - orchestrator] --> AgentTask[Agent task]
  Specialist[Specialist agent] --> AgentTask
  AgentTask --> Artifact2[Artifact]
  Artifact2 --> ArtifactLib[Artifact Library]
  Artifact2 -.lineage.-> Fact2[Governed fact]
  Artifact2 -.cites.-> Evidence2[Evidence]
  Registry[Capability registry entry] -.configures.-> Specialist
  Registry -->|ceiling| Ceiling[Autonomy ceiling]
  Schedule[Schedule] -.dispatches.-> Specialist
  Schedule --> RunReport[Run report artifact]
```

| Object | Role | Governance |
|--------|------|------------|
| **Specialist agent** | A capability run as an agent the Operator dispatches (scope, mapping, collection, …) | Capped by an autonomy ceiling; Commit escalates |
| **Agent task** | A dispatched unit of work with its own state machine | Provenance per task; audited |
| **Artifact** | Any agent output (plan, table, package, ledger, run report) | Versioned, provenance-linked, permissioned |
| **Artifact Library** | The store of all artifacts (per-filing + portfolio) | Confidentiality below the UI; doubles as durable memory |
| **Capability registry entry** | The catalog record for an agent or skill | Enable/disable + configure = audited; edit logic = governed authoring |
| **Autonomy ceiling** | Cap on how far an agent acts unattended | Never authorizes a signature commit or regulatory gate |
| **Schedule** | A cadence/event trigger binding an agent to a scope | Read/Recommend/Prepare only; audited; writes a run report |
| **Session (working thread)** | The [app shell](./operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout)'s unit of work — a bounded working context, listed/searchable/pinnable in the sidebar | Scoped to keep context accurate; distinct from a filing run |
| **Actor + role** | A person (Viewer/Commenter/Preparer/Reviewer/Admin) or an agent that acts on a filing | Role governs what they may do; Commit permissioned; signature commits reserved |
| **Presence** | Live indication of who's viewing what | Viewing ≠ acting |
| **Change log entry** | An attributed record of one material action (human or agent) | Who/when/what/why; feeds the audit trail |
| **Comment / mention** | Human-to-human note or @mention on a filing | Distinct from Operator prompts |
| **Data source** | A connected system (ERP, consolidation, HRIS, channel) or a manually-uploaded file, linked to the filings it feeds | Managed on the Source data surface; an upload becomes a governed fact with the file as evidence |
| **Report dashboard** | A read-first per-report view (agents & outputs, forms in the report & their status, phase, people, pending, blockers) | A *view* over the filing run — never a second source of truth |

**Artifact vs evidence:** an *artifact* is agent-produced; *evidence* is source proof. Artifacts cite evidence and some (the evidence bundle) collect it — link, not duplicate.

## Key relationships

1. **Pack → Report → Forms** — the Pack is what the customer buys; a **report** is one obligation inside it (e.g. BE-11 · FY25); each report **bundles many forms** — for BEA, one per entity in scope — defined by the [filing blueprint](#governed-substrate-build-time-authored-by-sdcsme) and generated once scope is confirmed. The governed bundle is how the Operator runs each report. This is what lets one Pack span many forms on a single experience.
2. **Rule set → Knowledge base** — every rule cites the passage it encodes; scope logic appearing in both is *source + encoding linked by citation*, not duplicated.
3. **Ownership graph → Scope plan** vs **Source & org intelligence → Collection request** — one decides *who files*, the other decides *who to ask*.
4. **Collection request → Governed fact** — an accepted reply becomes a governed fact with evidence; only governed facts populate the package.
5. **Deterministic evaluator → Scope plan / Package** — the independent cross-check behind the two signature commits.
6. **Filing run → Next-year baseline** — the cycle's record *and* its operating history are saved so next year starts ahead.
7. **Session ↔ Filing run** — a *session* is the interaction/working thread (context boundary, listed in the sidebar); a *filing run* is the durable governed record. Usually one session per filing for context hygiene, but one run may be worked across several sessions. The governed truth lives in the run + artifacts, never only in a session transcript.
8. **Obligation set → many filing runs** — one data intake can surface several obligations (BE-11, CbCR, …); each confirmed obligation becomes its own filing run, and governed facts are reused across them (collect once, use across the set).
9. **Actor → change log** — every actor (human *or* agent) that touches a filing produces attributed change-log entries; multiple actors work concurrently on scoped slices, with locking on signature commits.

## Purpose

Reference for the **filing lifecycle** (phases A–H) and the **four-level action model** that bounds the Operator at each phase. The lifecycle is *report-agnostic in shape and report-specific in content* — every report runs this arc.

## The lifecycle (phases)

```text
A Front door → B Scope → C Map & ingest → D Collect & chase → E Validate → F Prepare & assemble → G Review → H Close
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> A_FrontDoor
  A_FrontDoor --> B_Scope: prepare scope plan
  B_Scope --> C_MapIngest: scope confirmed
  C_MapIngest --> D_Collect: gaps identified
  D_Collect --> E_Validate: facts accepted
  E_Validate --> F_Prepare: reconciled
  E_Validate --> B_Scope: figure flips status - reopen scope
  F_Prepare --> G_Review: package composed
  G_Review --> H_Close: final approval
  G_Review --> F_Prepare: sent back with comments
  H_Close --> [*]: package staged, baseline saved
```

| Phase | Seat | What the Operator does | Action level |
|-------|------|------------------------|--------------|
| **A · Front door** | Preparer | Scans rules/facts/prior filings; returns required / confirm / not-yet-decidable | Read · Recommend |
| **B · Scope** | Preparer → Reviewer | Builds ownership graph, routes forms/claims, self-cross-checks before the reviewer commits | Recommend → **Commit** |
| **C · Map & ingest** | Preparer | Identifies sources, maps fields, pulls in-scope figures; surfaces low-confidence mappings | Recommend · Prepare |
| **D · Collect & chase** | Preparer (+ data owner) | Turns each gap into a tracked request, chases owners, tracks responses | Prepare · Commit |
| **E · Validate** | Preparer | Reconciles and re-tests on real numbers; reopens scope if a figure flips status | Recommend · Prepare |
| **F · Prepare & assemble** | Preparer | Populates from accepted facts, runs checks, composes the package | Prepare |
| **G · Review** | Reviewer | Writes the judgment ledger, runs final verification, releases on commit | **Commit** |
| **H · Close** | Preparer | Stages the package, builds evidence bundle, saves next-year baseline & operating history | Commit · Read |

**Two moments carry the design weight:** *scope* (present the plan beside its deterministic cross-check — the most expensive mistakes are cheapest to catch here) and *review* (the reviewer signs in minutes because the ledger is complete, or refuses with the exact divergence named).

## The four-level action model

Confirmation is **graded to consequence** — the heaviest moments are a tier of action, not the only checkpoints. Full detail in [governance-and-action-model.md](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md).

| Level | What it covers | Confirmation |
|-------|----------------|--------------|
| **Read** | Inspect state, explain a field/rule, compare periods, show provenance | None — runs freely |
| **Recommend** | Propose a filing, scope, mapping, routing, or next step | Cites evidence & confidence |
| **Prepare** | Draft a task set, mapping, filing-run setup, or review package | Staged — user review before any official change |
| **Commit** | Create a filing run, accept data, confirm a fact, mark ready, route/approve, lock the package | Permission + confirmation + audit trail |

### The two signature commits

Confirming **scope** and giving **final approval** carry the most legal weight but live inside the same model as every other commit. Designing against **approval fatigue** is a first-class goal — the Operator confirms only where judgment, accountability, or official state matters.

## Autonomy gradient

Autonomy rises left→right across the lifecycle as work becomes more deterministic and trust accrues — but a human approval gate exists where accountability or official state changes. **The Operator never files unsupervised.**

| A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read·Recommend | →Commit | Recommend·Prepare | Prepare·Commit | Recommend·Prepare | Prepare | Commit | Commit |

## Request lifecycle (within phase D)

The Collection & Chase capability tracks each gap through its own state machine, with full provenance and audit:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> requested: send (Commit)
  requested --> submitted: owner replies
  submitted --> accepted: accept as governed fact (Commit)
  submitted --> rejected: value fails validation
  rejected --> requested: re-request
  requested --> escalated: overdue
  escalated --> submitted: reminder answered
  accepted --> [*]
```
