## How to use this document

This is the pattern library for designing the Regulatory Filing Operator. Each pattern states the **principle**, **why it matters**, **how to apply it** in the UI, and an **anti-pattern** to avoid. The patterns are not independent — they compose into a single experience whose thesis is: *the human is a governor, not an operator-of-steps.*

The ten core design principles from the brief map to the patterns below:

| Principle (brief appendix) | Pattern(s) |
|----------------------------|------------|
| The Operator is the experience, not a chatbot | [P1](#p1--control-surface-not-chatbot), [P2](#p2--next-best-step) |
| Confirmation is graded to consequence | [P3](#p3--graded-confirmation) |
| Protect the signature commits; design against approval fatigue | [P3](#p3--graded-confirmation), [P4](#p4--protect-the-signature-commits) |
| Make reasoning legible | [P5](#p5--reasoning-one-step-away), [P6](#p6--evidence-and-provenance-on-every-value) |
| Surface ambiguity, route exceptions, hide routine | [P7](#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine) |
| Obligation discovery is the front door — incl. "not decidable yet" | [P8](#p8--start-ahead--the-honest-not-yet-decidable) |
| One shape, many reports | [P9](#p9--one-shape-many-reports) |
| Override-with-record | [P10](#p10--override-with-record) |
| The human is a governor, not an operator-of-steps | [P11](#p11--governor-not-operator) |
| Agents/skills/context/rules are SDC-configurable per report | [P12](#p12--configurable-per-report) |

> **Extension patterns.** Patterns **P13–P18** come from the [Agent Operations extension](../11-agent-operations/README.md) — multi-agent orchestration, the artifact library, the agents & skills registry, scheduled agents, and context management. They apply the same governance spine to the *operating environment around* the Operator.

| Extension concern (section 11) | Pattern |
|--------------------------------|---------|
| Spinning off many agents legibly | [P13](#p13--legible-orchestration) |
| Artifacts as the Operator's durable memory | [P14](#p14--artifacts-as-durable-memory) |
| Bounded context for accurate results | [P15](#p15--scope-the-work-not-the-world) |
| Never a silent black box | [P16](#p16--progress-transparency) |
| Unattended agents stay bounded | [P17](#p17--sub-agents--scheduled-agents-inherit-the-action-model) |
| Toggling/configuring vs authoring logic | [P18](#p18--configuration-vs-authoring) |
| Multi-user collaboration made legible | [P19](#p19--legible-collaboration) |
| Data-first, multi-obligation intake | [P20](#p20--start-from-the-data-not-the-form) |

---

## P1 · Control surface, not chatbot

**Principle.** The Operator is a control surface. **Hide the machinery** (which capability is running) but **never hide the reasoning**.

**Why.** A chatbot puts the burden of orchestration on the user. A control surface carries the work and lets the user govern it. Users should never need to know whether "Obligation Scout" or "Mapping & Resolve" is running.

**How to apply.**
- Present phase-appropriate **views** (readiness briefing, scope plan, worklist, ledger) — not a chat transcript as the primary UI.
- Never label capabilities as separate products or tabs the user must choose between.
- Conversation is an *affordance within* the surface, not the surface itself.

**Anti-pattern.** A free-text prompt box as the main interface; exposing internal agent/tool names; making the user assemble the workflow.

**Shell note.** The [app shell](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#app-shell-layout) (collapsible left sidebar + main content) *hosts* the control surface; it does not replace it. The sidebar is **global wayfinding** (Home, Agents & Skills, Artifacts, Sessions, Settings), never workflow steps — the filing work stays lifecycle-driven inside the active session's main content.

---

## P2 · Next best step

**Principle.** After every phase, the Operator proposes the single most useful next action through a **governed prompt library** — the user accepts, edits, or declines.

**Why.** It keeps momentum, teaches the flow, and keeps the user in control without a blank page. It is the connective tissue of the whole experience.

**How to apply.**
- End each view with one clear, primary proposed action (e.g. *"Want me to prepare a scope plan for review?"* → **Prepare scope plan**).
- Offer at most one or two secondary options; avoid a wall of choices.
- Make the proposed step reversible or staged whenever it isn't a commit.
- **Vary the prompt library by session state, not just phase** — a session waiting on a person (*"Send a reminder"*, *"What exactly are we waiting on?"*, *"What happens if they don't respond in time?"*), one that's actively running (*"What's the current status?"*, *"Anything blocking this filing?"*, *"What still needs data?"*), one that's done (*"Show me the filing package"*, *"What changed vs. last cycle?"*, *"Open the audit trail"*), and an ad-hoc chat log (follow-ups grounded in what was just asked, e.g. *"Show me the 6 needing ownership confirmation"* after a BE-11 exposure question) each warrant different next-best-steps. A single static list of starters ("What do we need to file?", "Start a filing…") only fits the very first turn of a brand-new session — every session after that should propose questions that are actually answerable from what's happened in it, including from **Home**, one level above any single session (see [Home dashboard](../07-pages/operator-surfaces.md#the-home-dashboard)).

**Anti-pattern.** Dead-end screens; forcing the user to figure out what to do next; auto-advancing past a decision the user should make; showing the same generic starters regardless of what state the session is actually in.

---

## P3 · Graded confirmation

**Principle.** Confirmation is **graded to consequence** across the four action levels — [Read, Recommend, Prepare, Commit](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md).

**Why.** Confirming everything trains users to click through blindly (approval fatigue); confirming nothing is unsafe. Match friction to stakes.

**How to apply.**

| Level | UI treatment |
|-------|--------------|
| **Read** | No confirmation; runs freely; provenance available |
| **Recommend** | Show evidence + confidence; a proposal, not a change |
| **Prepare** | Staged; visible "draft" state; user reviews before anything official |
| **Commit** | Explicit confirm + permission check + audit entry |

- Visibly distinguish a *draft* (Prepare) from an *official change* (Commit).
- Reserve heavyweight confirmation dialogs for Commit-level actions only.

**Anti-pattern.** A confirmation modal on every action; silently committing at what should be a Prepare step.

---

## P4 · Protect the signature commits

**Principle.** The two [signature commits](../02-glossary/glossary.md#signature-commits) — **confirm scope** and **final approval** — get the most design care; everything else is designed to *not* compete with them for attention.

**Why.** These carry the most legal weight. If the surface nags at every step, the user arrives at these numb. Scope is where the most expensive mistakes are cheapest to catch; review is where the reviewer must sign in minutes on evidence.

**How to apply.**
- **Scope confirmation:** present the plan **beside its deterministic cross-check**; show what changed from last year and the exceptions resolved. Make "Confirm scope" and "Send back with comments" equally weighted.
- **Final approval:** present the [judgment ledger](#p6--evidence-and-provenance-on-every-value) so the reviewer can approve on evidence or refuse with the exact divergence named.
- Strip incidental confirmations elsewhere so these two moments stand out.

**Anti-pattern.** Making scope/approval look like any other button; burying the cross-check; approval fatigue from over-confirming routine steps.

---

## P5 · Reasoning one step away

**Principle.** Provenance and the deterministic cross-check are **always one step away** — never hidden, never forced into the foreground.

**Why.** Legible reasoning is what converts "faith" into "confidence." But surfacing all of it at once is noise. One step away is the balance.

**How to apply.**
- Every recommendation, value, and outcome has an inline affordance to "show why" (evidence, rule, source, cross-check).
- Default to the conclusion; reveal the reasoning on demand.
- The cross-check result is a first-class, glanceable element on scope and readiness views (*"no blocking issues"*).

**Anti-pattern.** Black-box recommendations; or dumping raw reasoning/logs into the primary view.

---

## P6 · Evidence and provenance on every value

**Principle.** Every load-bearing value shows its **source**; the reviewer's view is a **judgment ledger**, not a stack of forms.

**Why.** "No invented figures" and "no uncited regulatory answers" are contract invariants. The reviewer signs the *judgment*, so the judgment must be visible.

**How to apply.**
- Each populated field carries a source chip (system source vs accepted email response, with confidence).
- The **judgment ledger** aggregates: final scope, changes from last year, every outcome/threshold/value-with-source, warnings & resolutions, overrides, final verification.
- Distinguish deterministic-tool values from accepted human responses visibly.

**Anti-pattern.** Values without provenance; a review screen that shows forms instead of decisions.

---

## P7 · Surface ambiguity, route exceptions, hide routine

**Principle.** Show the few items that need judgment; keep the routine quiet.

**Why.** The Operator's value is triage. If it surfaces everything, it's just a longer to-do list. **Attention is the scarce resource.**

**How to apply.**
- Readiness views lead with blockers/warnings/pending items and keep passed checks collapsed (*"92% ready · 0 blocking errors · 3 warnings"*).
- Flag ambiguous scope rows and low-confidence mappings; route field-level questions to the right owner.
- Quantify the shape of the work (*"3 scope items need review"*, *"12 missing inputs"*).

**Anti-pattern.** Flat lists where routine and exceptional items look identical; hiding a blocker among passed checks.

---

## P8 · Start ahead & the honest "not-yet-decidable"

**Principle.** Never a blank page. The Operator starts with a prepared briefing — and states honestly what it **cannot** conclude yet.

**Why.** Obligation discovery is the front door. Overclaiming (asserting a legal obligation) breaks trust; a blank page wastes the head start Workiva's data provides.

**How to apply.**
- Open each filing with a readiness briefing (what's known / likely / to-confirm).
- Use an explicit **not-yet-decidable** state for items blocked on a dependency (e.g. current-year financials) — visually distinct from "required" and "excluded."
- Obligation Scout **recommends, never asserts**; cite the signal (e.g. 10-K subsidiary disclosures) and route into a governed workflow.

**Anti-pattern.** Blank forms; false precision that hides uncertainty; asserting an obligation as fact.

---

## P9 · One shape, many reports

**Principle.** The experience is **report-agnostic in shape, report-specific in content**. A preparer who has filed BE-11 should recognize any other filing instantly.

**Why.** It's how one Pack spans many forms on a single experience, and how the product scales across the portfolio without re-teaching users.

**How to apply.**
- Keep the phase arc, action model, next-best-step rhythm, and provenance patterns identical across reports.
- Let content differ only via the [governed bundle](../06-features/governed-substrate.md) (blueprint, rule set, skills) — never the interaction model.
- Reuse the same components for scope plan, worklist, readiness, and ledger regardless of report type.

**Anti-pattern.** Bespoke UI per form class; report-specific navigation that forces relearning.

---

## P10 · Override-with-record

**Principle.** Users can override the Operator — and **every override is recorded, never silent.**

**Why.** Human judgment must win, but accountability must be preserved. This is a contract invariant.

**How to apply.**
- Allow the user to change any recommendation, mapping, or outcome.
- Capture who, when, from-what-to-what, and (optionally) why; surface overrides in the judgment ledger.
- Never let an override quietly disappear into the accepted state.

**Anti-pattern.** Locking users out of the Operator's decisions; or accepting overrides without an audit record.

---

## P11 · Governor, not operator

**Principle.** Design for a human who **governs** the work, not one who executes every step.

**Why.** This is the product thesis. The value is fewer coordination cycles and more confident sign-off — not a faster way to do the same manual steps.

**How to apply.**
- Default the Operator to carrying the work; the human's primary verbs are *review, resolve, confirm, approve, override*.
- Frame the user's exceptions queue, not their task list.
- Copy and layout should read as supervision (*"Approve final package?"*), not operation (*"Fill field 7"*).

**Anti-pattern.** Recreating the manual workbench with an assistant bolted on; making the user do the Operator's job.

---

## P12 · Configurable per report

**Principle.** Agents, skills, context, and rule sets are **SDC-configurable per report**; only what's relevant turns on.

**Why.** New filings deploy as a **governed bundle**, not a toggle — focused, lower-risk, explainable. The design must accommodate variation without special-casing the UI.

**How to apply.**
- Drive views from the published blueprint/rule set/skills; the surface adapts to whatever the bundle enables.
- Show only the capabilities the report's bundle turns on.
- Respect **confidentiality** — the surface reflects permissions and never over-shares filing data.

**Anti-pattern.** Hard-coded per-report screens; showing capabilities that aren't configured for that filing.

---

## P13 · Legible orchestration

**Principle.** When the Operator spins off many agents, show the **shape of the work**, not every keystroke. Default to a plain-language summary; make the full work tree one step away.

**Why.** Fan-out is how the product delivers speed (42 affiliates evaluated at once), but exposing raw agent activity would recreate the "operator-of-steps" burden and violate [P1](#p1--control-surface-not-chatbot). The user needs to *trust and steer* the work, not micromanage it.

**How to apply.**
- Summarize (*"Chasing 12 inputs across 8 owners · 3 need you"*); let the user expand into an **[activity view](../11-agent-operations/multi-agent-orchestration.md#the-activity-view-aka-work-view)** with the orchestrator→agent→task tree and per-task status/provenance.
- Provide five supervision verbs: observe, steer, answer, approve, pause/stop.
- **Batch homogeneous commits** ("Send all 8 requests") to fight approval fatigue — but never batch a signature commit.

**Anti-pattern.** A live feed of every agent action as the primary UI; forcing the user to dispatch or track agents by hand; N separate confirmations for N identical requests.

---

## P14 · Artifacts as durable memory

**Principle.** Everything agents produce is written to a central, versioned, provenance-linked **[artifact library](../11-agent-operations/artifact-library.md)** — which doubles as the Operator's externalized memory.

**Why.** Two wins at once: the user gets one place to find any output, and the Operator can **reference durable artifacts instead of re-loading everything into context** — the mechanism behind bounded context and reproducibility ([P15](#p15--scope-the-work-not-the-world)).

**How to apply.**
- Persist every meaningful output as a typed artifact with version, status, lineage, confidentiality, and producing agent/run.
- Let users preview, export, compare versions, and **trace lineage** ("what produced this / what this fed into").
- Agents load the relevant *artifact*, not the whole history, when resuming work.

**Anti-pattern.** Outputs that live only in a conversation transcript; artifacts without provenance or version; memory that grows unbounded in-context instead of living in the store.

---

## P15 · Scope the work, not the world

**Principle.** Keep each agent's working context **bounded** — and guide the user to make well-scoped requests — because an overloaded context window produces inaccurate results. For a penalty-bearing filing, bounded context is a *correctness* requirement.

**Why.** Accuracy and the "no invented figures" contract depend on the right facts being present and load-bearing facts not being buried. Users shouldn't need to understand token limits; the product should keep them on the rails.

**How to apply.**
- **Externalize memory** (facts + [artifacts](#p14--artifacts-as-durable-memory)); do the math in deterministic tools, not the model's context; reference sources by pointer and retrieve on demand.
- **Fan out into scoped slices** so each worker holds only its entity/section/field.
- **Auto-decompose** over-broad asks ("do all 200 filings now") into batches, explaining why; steer via the [prompt library](#p2--next-best-step).
- **Make the [session](../04-information-architecture/operator-surface-and-navigation.md#sessions-the-unit-of-work) the context boundary.** The app shell's *New session* CTA and one-filing-per-session default keep each working thread scoped; the sidebar (search/pinned/all) lets users return without re-loading everything into one bloated thread.
- Show a **subtle session-context indicator** with a plain-language nudge — never raw token counts to a compliance user — and checkpoint long work into artifacts.

**Anti-pattern.** One agent trying to "hold the whole filing"; pasting entire sources into context; letting a single thread accumulate unrelated work; exposing token mechanics as the user's problem.

---

## P16 · Progress transparency

**Principle.** The Operator is **never a silent black box.** At any moment the user can see what it's doing now, what it read, what it's about to do, and what it needs.

**Why.** Trust (and the "make reasoning legible" principle) requires that unattended, long-running, multi-agent work is observable — otherwise users either over-supervise or disengage.

**How to apply.**
- Stream progress; keep an always-visible **work summary** and a **findings tray** for items needing attention.
- Keep reasoning/provenance one step away ([P5](#p5--reasoning-one-step-away)); surface pending approvals and blocking questions clearly.
- **Quiet by default, loud when it matters** ([P7](#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine)); **digest, not deluge** for scheduled findings.

**Anti-pattern.** A spinner with no detail during a long run; findings that arrive as noise; silent completion of consequential work.

---

## P17 · Sub-agents & scheduled agents inherit the action model

**Principle.** Every spun-off agent and every [scheduled agent](../11-agent-operations/scheduled-agents.md) is bound by the [four action levels](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md): it may Read, Recommend, and Prepare autonomously, but **Commit always escalates to a human**, and it can **never cross a signature commit** or a regulatory gate.

**Why.** "The Operator never files unsupervised" must hold *most strongly* for unattended and parallel work — that's where silent, consequential action is most tempting and most dangerous.

**How to apply.**
- Set an **autonomy ceiling** per agent in the [registry](../11-agent-operations/agent-and-skill-registry.md); ceilings can be *earned* upward ([I2](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i2--earned-adaptive-autonomy)) but never authorize a signature commit.
- Scheduled agents queue Commit-level findings as **next-best-steps**, never auto-execute them.
- Audit every unattended run; write a run-report artifact even when nothing surfaced.

**Anti-pattern.** A background agent that files, sends, or locks without a human; an autonomy setting that can bypass scope/approval; unattended runs with no audit trail.

---

## P18 · Configuration vs authoring

**Principle.** Users can **configure** governed capabilities (enable/disable, set autonomy ceilings, tune thresholds within bounds) directly and with audit — but **editing the logic** (rule sets, blueprints, skills) routes to the **governed authoring flow** (SDC/SME, shadow mode, publish). Only published artifacts run.

**Why.** The registry must be powerful without becoming a backdoor around "no unapproved rules." Separating tuning from authoring preserves the contract while giving customers real control.

**How to apply.**
- In the [registry](../11-agent-operations/agent-and-skill-registry.md), make configuration inline and audited; make "edit logic" an explicit hand-off to authoring with visible governance status (`in shadow`, `published`).
- Treat on/off toggles as **governed, permissioned, audited** changes — not preferences.

**Anti-pattern.** Letting a customer edit rule logic live; silent capability toggles; configuration that can raise autonomy past a structural gate.

---

## P19 · Legible collaboration

**Principle.** A filing is multi-user. Always make three things visible: **who's here** (presence), **who can do what and who did it** (roles + attribution), and **what changed** (change log) — for humans *and* agents alike.

**Why.** Multiple people and many agents touch the same penalty-bearing filing. Without presence, people collide or duplicate; without attribution, accountability evaporates; without a change log, no one can trust the state. Collaboration must extend the same legibility the product gives to reasoning.

**How to apply.**
- Show **live presence** (who's viewing what) on Home and inside a session; make clear **viewing ≠ acting**.
- Gate actions by **role** (Viewer / Commenter / Preparer / Reviewer-approver / Admin); reserve the signature commits to the Reviewer-approver; cap agents by autonomy ceiling.
- **Attribute every action** — human or agent — inline and in the audit trail ("accepted by Julie · mapped by Collection agent · from Maria's email").
- Support **delegation, handoff, OOO coverage**, and **comments/@mentions** distinct from Operator prompts.
- Partition concurrent work into **scoped slices**; **lock** signature-commit state; **surface conflicts**, never auto-resolve.

**Anti-pattern.** A single-user mental model; unattributed changes; two people able to approve conflicting versions; agents acting without a named owner; over-sharing beyond a seat's entitlement.

See [collaboration-and-presence.md](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md).

---

## P20 · Start from the data, not the form

**Principle.** Don't assume one form. Let the user start from data — *"here's what we have, what do we file?"* — and detect the **whole [obligation set](../02-glossary/glossary.md#obligation-set)**, then run a coordinated filing per obligation.

**Why.** Real obligations travel together: the same subsidiary/financial data that triggers BE-11 also triggers Country-by-Country. Forcing "one form at a time" hides obligations the customer may not know they have and wastes the cross-filing leverage that is Workiva's advantage.

**How to apply.**
- Scan intake data against **every governed rule set**, not one; classify each obligation required / confirm / not-yet-decidable.
- **Recommend, never assert** each obligation (cite evidence + threshold); the human picks which to pursue ([P8](#p8--start-ahead--the-honest-not-yet-decidable)).
- Spin up **one filing run per confirmed obligation**, coordinated on Home; **reuse accepted facts across the set** (collect once, use everywhere — [I1](../10-analysis/product-improvements.md#i1--compounding-facts-across-the-portfolio)).
- Keep signature commits **per filing** (scope and approval are per obligation).

**Anti-pattern.** A form picker as the only entry; detecting one obligation and stopping; re-collecting the same fact separately for each filing.

See [Obligation Scout — multi-obligation intake](../06-features/obligation-scout.md#multi-obligation-intake-here-is-my-data-what-do-i-file) and the [Country-by-Country example](../05-operator-flows/report-patterns/country-by-country.md).

---

## Cross-cutting non-negotiables (the contract, in UI terms)

These map the [contract](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md#the-contract) to what the design must guarantee:

| Contract invariant | Design guarantee |
|--------------------|------------------|
| No invented figures | Every load-bearing value shows a deterministic source or accepted-fact provenance |
| No silent state changes | Official changes require Commit + permission + audit; a threshold flip surfaces an approvable delta |
| No unapproved rules | Only published, governed rule packs drive the UI |
| No uncited regulatory answers | Compliance answers link to the knowledge-base passage |
| No package release without final approval | The package cannot be staged until the signature commit is recorded |
| Every override recorded | Overrides are captured and appear in the judgment ledger |

## Governance affordances checklist

For any new Operator surface, verify:

- [ ] Correct action level, with confirmation graded to consequence ([P3](#p3--graded-confirmation))
- [ ] A clear next best step ([P2](#p2--next-best-step))
- [ ] Reasoning/provenance reachable in one step ([P5](#p5--reasoning-one-step-away), [P6](#p6--evidence-and-provenance-on-every-value))
- [ ] Routine hidden; exceptions surfaced ([P7](#p7--surface-ambiguity-route-exceptions-hide-routine))
- [ ] Gates tagged **regulatory** (non-negotiable) vs **corporate** (configurable) ([governance](../06-features/governance-and-action-model.md#two-kinds-of-governance-kept-separate))
- [ ] Overrides possible and recorded ([P10](#p10--override-with-record))
- [ ] Confidentiality respected ([P12](#p12--configurable-per-report))
- [ ] Multi-agent work is legible and interruptible, not micromanaged ([P13](#p13--legible-orchestration))
- [ ] Outputs persisted as provenance-linked artifacts ([P14](#p14--artifacts-as-durable-memory))
- [ ] Context kept bounded; over-broad requests decomposed ([P15](#p15--scope-the-work-not-the-world))
- [ ] Progress observable; no silent black box ([P16](#p16--progress-transparency))
- [ ] Sub/scheduled agents capped below Commit; never auto-file ([P17](#p17--sub-agents--scheduled-agents-inherit-the-action-model))
- [ ] Config separated from authoring; toggles audited ([P18](#p18--configuration-vs-authoring))
- [ ] Multi-user: presence shown, actions attributed (human/agent), conflicts surfaced ([P19](#p19--legible-collaboration))
- [ ] Intake detects the whole obligation set, not one form ([P20](#p20--start-from-the-data-not-the-form))

## Journey overview

Agentic CRR moves the customer **from doing the filing to governing it**. The Operator carries one filing through eight phases; the human enters only where judgment, accountability, or official state matters. The journey threads through one BE-11 filing, but the shape is the reusable pattern — every report runs this arc.

```text
A Front door → B Scope → C Map & ingest → D Collect & chase → E Validate → F Prepare & assemble → G Review → H Close
```

| Phase | Seat | What the Operator does | Action level | Primary flow |
|-------|------|------------------------|--------------|--------------|
| **A · Front door** | Preparer | Scans rules/facts/prior filings; returns required / confirm / not-yet-decidable | Read · Recommend | [Front door](../05-operator-flows/front-door-obligation.md) |
| **B · Scope** | Preparer → Reviewer | Builds ownership graph, routes claims, self-cross-checks before commit | Recommend → Commit | [Scope & confirmation](../05-operator-flows/scope-and-confirmation.md) |
| **C · Map & ingest** | Preparer | Identifies sources, maps fields, pulls figures; flags low-confidence | Recommend · Prepare | [Map & ingest](../05-operator-flows/map-and-ingest.md) |
| **D · Collect & chase** | Preparer (+ data owner) | Turns each gap into a tracked request; chases; tracks responses | Prepare · Commit | [Collect & chase](../05-operator-flows/collect-and-chase.md) |
| **E · Validate** | Preparer | Reconciles on real numbers; reopens scope if a figure flips | Recommend · Prepare | [Validate](../05-operator-flows/validate.md) |
| **F · Prepare & assemble** | Preparer | Populates from accepted facts; runs checks; composes package | Prepare | [Prepare & assemble](../05-operator-flows/prepare-and-assemble.md) |
| **G · Review** | Reviewer | Writes judgment ledger; final verification; releases on commit | Commit | [Review & approval](../05-operator-flows/review-and-approval.md) |
| **H · Close** | Preparer | Stages package; saves baseline & operating history | Commit · Read | [Package & close](../05-operator-flows/package-and-close.md) |

**Two moments carry the design weight:** *scope* and *review*.

> **Two shape notes.** (1) **The journey is multi-user** — several seats and many agents work one filing at once, with presence, role-gated actions, and attributed changes ([collaboration](../11-agent-operations/collaboration-and-presence.md)). (2) **Intake is not one form at a time** — a user can start from data (*"what do we file?"*), the Operator detects the whole [obligation set](../02-glossary/glossary.md#obligation-set) (e.g. BE-11 + CbCR), and each confirmed obligation runs this same arc as its own coordinated filing, reusing shared facts ([Obligation Scout](../06-features/obligation-scout.md#multi-obligation-intake-here-is-my-data-what-do-i-file), [CbCR](../05-operator-flows/report-patterns/country-by-country.md)).

---

## Persona legend

Agentic CRR seats are canonical; base CRR / JTBD aliases in parentheses. See [personas.md](../03-personas/personas.md).

| Seat | Group | Alias | Role in journey |
|------|-------|-------|-----------------|
| [Preparer](../03-personas/personas.md#preparer) | Governs | Report Owner / Compliance Manager | Directs the Operator A–H; resolves exceptions |
| [Reviewer-approver](../03-personas/personas.md#reviewer-approver-controller--responsible-officer) | Governs | Reviewer | Confirms scope (B) and final approval (G) |
| [SDC / SME](../03-personas/personas.md#sdc--sme) | Supplies (build) | Workspace Admin (adjacent) | Authors & publishes the governed bundle (pre-journey) |
| [Data / Source Owner](../03-personas/personas.md#data--source-owner-contributor) | Supplies (run) | Data Provider / Assignee | Answers targeted requests (D) |

**Notes:**

- SDC/SME work is **build-time** — the governed bundle must be published (and pass shadow mode) before the journey runs.
- E can loop back to B (threshold flip → scope delta); G can loop back to F (send back).
- H seeds the next cycle's front door via the monitoring plan.
- The Operator never files unsupervised.

---

## Autonomy gradient

Autonomy rises left→right as work becomes more deterministic and trust accrues — but a human gate exists wherever accountability or official state changes.

| A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read·Recommend | →**Commit** | Recommend·Prepare | Prepare·Commit | Recommend·Prepare | Prepare | **Commit** | Commit |

The two **bold Commits** are the [signature commits](../02-glossary/glossary.md#signature-commits).

---

## Before / after

| | Before Agentic CRR | After Agentic CRR |
|---|--------------------|--------------------|
| **Preparer** | Runs the whole filing by hand | Directs the work and resolves exceptions |
| **Data owner** | Chased by email across threads | Answers targeted, contextual requests in place |
| **Reviewer** | Signs on faith — judgment invisible in the artifact | Confirms scope & final approval on a legible ledger + clean cross-check |
| **Every number** | Reconciled by hand | Comes from a source or deterministic calculation |
| **Every change** | Untracked | Permissioned and audited |
| **Next year** | Rebuilt from scratch | Starts ahead — record + operating history saved |

The product is not just faster form filling. It is the shift **from filing coordination to governed filing readiness**.

---

## Cross-seat handoffs

| From | To | Trigger | Mechanism |
|------|----|---------|-----------|
| SDC/SME | Preparer | Governed bundle published (post shadow-mode) | Blueprint + rule set + skills available to the Operator |
| Preparer | Reviewer | Scope plan ready | *Send for scope approval* → scope confirmation |
| Preparer | Data owner | Missing fact | Operator drafts request; Preparer *Sends* on the owner's channel |
| Data owner | Preparer | Reply received | Operator maps values; Preparer *Accepts* as governed facts |
| Preparer | Reviewer | Package ready | Judgment ledger presented for final approval |
| Preparer | Agency *(out of app)* | Package staged | Customer's approved submission process |

## Purpose

The narrative demo of one BE-11 filing, end to end — the companion to the product brief. It shows the Operator experience concretely; the [customer journey map](./customer-journey-map.md) and [operator flows](../05-operator-flows/README.md) generalize it. This is a **north-star narrative**, to be proven in shadow mode before anything is customer-facing.

## The setup

**Julie** owns regulatory filings for a global company. Every year, BE-11 creates the same scramble: last year's filing, an affiliate list, ERP exports, consolidation reports, mapping spreadsheets, and a long list of people to chase. Some affiliates changed. Some ownership percentages moved. Some controllers are slow. Some numbers arrive late. The deadline is real, and the controller who signs will ask: *"Can we trust this?"*

In Agentic CRR, Julie does not start from a blank page.

---

## 1 · The Operator starts ahead *(Phase A)*

Julie opens Agentic CRR to a **BE-11 readiness briefing** already prepared:

> BE-11 readiness review started. Prior-year filing found. 42 foreign affiliates detected. 31 appear unchanged. 6 need ownership confirmation. 5 are not yet decidable until current-year financials are available.

The Operator has read the prior filing, current entity data, available source context, the BE-11 blueprint, and the current rule pack. It is not declaring a legal conclusion — it organizes what is known, likely, and still-to-confirm. Then: *"Want me to prepare a scope plan for review?"* Julie clicks **Prepare scope plan**.

→ Flow: [Front door](../05-operator-flows/front-door-obligation.md)

---

## 2 · Scope becomes a decision *(Phase B)*

The Operator opens a **Scope Plan** — affiliates grouped by recommended outcome: *BE-11B · BE-11D · BE-11A rollup · Claim for Not Filing · Needs confirmation · Not decidable yet*.

Julie clicks into **Germany Manufacturing GmbH**:

> BE-11B recommended. Majority-owned foreign affiliate. Current-year sales appear above threshold. Evidence: FY25 ERP revenue table. Rule: BE-11 affiliate size test.

Most scope is clean; *3 scope items need review*. The Operator: *"Want me to route these three scope questions to the right owners before sending for approval?"* Julie resolves one herself, sends two. The Operator updates: *"Scope plan is ready for reviewer confirmation. Independent cross-check found no blocking issues."* Then: *"Send scope plan to controller for approval?"* Julie clicks **Send for scope approval**.

→ Flow: [Scope & confirmation](../05-operator-flows/scope-and-confirmation.md)

---

## 3 · The controller confirms scope *(Phase B — signature commit #1)*

The controller sees not a spreadsheet but the proposed scope, what changed from last year, the exceptions Julie resolved, and the independent cross-check:

> 42 affiliates reviewed. 37 consistent with last year. 3 claims for not filing. 2 require current-year financials before final treatment. No blocking cross-check issues.

*"Confirm scope, or send back with comments?"* The controller clicks **Confirm scope**. Recorded with user, timestamp, scope version, evidence, and rule-pack version.

---

## 4 · The Operator finds the data *(Phase C)*

> I found likely sources for 84% of required BE-11 values.

The Operator matched required fields to source systems and prior mappings — assets, sales/operating revenue, net income, employee count, industry classification, intercompany balances — and is honest:

> 18 fields mapped with high confidence. 7 fields need review. 12 required facts are missing. 4 source periods need confirmation.

*"Want me to prepare the missing-data requests?"* Julie clicks **Prepare requests**.

→ Flow: [Map & ingest](../05-operator-flows/map-and-ingest.md)

---

## 5 · Missing data becomes managed work *(Phase D)*

This is where the Operator becomes **visibly agentic**. Each missing fact becomes a targeted request tied to a specific field, affiliate, owner, due date, and evidence requirement:

> 12 missing inputs. 8 requests ready to send. 2 need owner confirmation. 2 overdue from the prior request cycle.

The Operator previews a task for the German affiliate controller:

> "For the FY25 BE-11 filing, please provide year-end employee count and net income after foreign income tax for Germany Manufacturing GmbH. These values will be used for BE-11B readiness."

*"Send this request by email and track the response here?"* Julie **Sends**. Later, the controller replies **by email** — no new workflow. The Operator captures it:

> Response received from Maria Keller. Employee count → BE-11B Item 10. Net income → BE-11B Item 7. Confidence: high. Evidence attached.

*"Accept these values as governed facts?"* Julie clicks **Accept**. Worklist: *8 received · 2 pending · 2 overdue*. For overdue items: *"Send a Teams reminder and escalate if no response by Friday?"* Julie clicks **Send reminder**.

→ Flow: [Collect & chase](../05-operator-flows/collect-and-chase.md)

---

## 6 · The filing builds from accepted facts *(Phases E–F)*

> Draft BE-11 package prepared from accepted facts only.

BE-11A and affiliate forms are populated; each value has a source. Then the Operator catches a change:

> Scope change detected. Brazil Services Ltd. now appears to exceed the BE-11B threshold based on accepted FY25 revenue.

It does **not** quietly continue with stale scope. *"Want me to reopen scope for this affiliate and prepare the approval delta?"* Julie clicks **Prepare scope update**; the controller reviews the delta and confirms.

→ Flows: [Validate](../05-operator-flows/validate.md), [Prepare & assemble](../05-operator-flows/prepare-and-assemble.md)

---

## 7 · Readiness becomes visible *(Phase F)*

Julie opens the **Readiness view** — she doesn't need to remember whether it's ready:

> BE-11 package is 92% ready. 0 blocking validation errors. 3 warnings. 2 pending evidence items. 1 approved scope change.

Routine checks stay quiet; only what needs attention surfaces. *"Want me to resolve the remaining evidence gaps and prepare the package for final review?"* Julie clicks **Prepare for review**. When final evidence is attached: *"BE-11 is ready for final review."*

---

## 8 · The controller signs from a judgment ledger *(Phase G — signature commit #2)*

Instead of a stack of forms, the controller sees a **judgment ledger**: final scope, changes from last year, every affiliate and outcome, every threshold decision, every value with source, every warning and resolution, every override, final verification result. The Operator summarizes:

> Final verification passed. No blocking issues. 3 warnings resolved. 1 accepted value came from an email response rather than a direct system source. Evidence attached.

*"Approve final package, or send back with comments?"* The controller clicks **Approve final package**. The package is locked; approval recorded.

→ Flow: [Review & approval](../05-operator-flows/review-and-approval.md)

---

## 9 · The package closes and next year starts ahead *(Phase H)*

The Operator stages the package for the customer's approved submission process:

> BE-11 package is complete. Evidence bundle created. Next-year baseline saved.

The package includes final forms, evidence, source provenance, approval record, comments, exceptions, overrides, audit trail, blueprint version, and rule-pack version. The Operator also saves the **operating history**: confirmed scope, mappings, source locations, routed owners, response times, late inputs, rework, scope changes, evidence gaps, resolved exceptions.

*"Want me to create next year's monitoring plan?"* Julie clicks **Create monitoring plan**. The Operator recommends when next year should start — based on how long this took, which entities caused delays, where manual collection was needed, and which inputs created rework.

→ Flow: [Package & close](../05-operator-flows/package-and-close.md)

---

## The story we are telling

**Before:** Julie coordinated the filing by hand — rebuilt the affiliate list, chased controllers, reconciled spreadsheets, assembled a package, and asked the controller to sign on trust.

**After:** the Operator carries the filing:

- Julie **directs** the work and resolves exceptions.
- Data owners **answer** targeted questions.
- The controller **confirms** scope and final approval.
- Every number comes from a source or deterministic calculation.
- Every official change is permissioned and audited.

The shift is **from filing coordination to governed filing readiness**.
